MacBook Pro (14-inch, M5 Pro, 1TB, Touchscreen): £2,674.97  (£224 off at Amazon, RRP £2,899)

Mac mini (M6, 256GB, 16GB): £759 (£140 off at Amazon, RRP £899)
Mac mini (M5 Pro, 512GB, 24GB): £1,499 (£200 off at Amazon, RRP £1,699)
PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 26, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November.
Black Friday is one of the best opportunities to save on a Mac, with retailers competing to discount MacBooks and desktop models – including recently released machines. The Black Friday Mac deals are already here, and the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage is where we’d start for most people. Amazon has listed it for $999 in the U.S. and £1,149 in the U.K., saving $300 and about £150 off Apple’s current prices. If you already have a display, keyboard, and mouse, the M6 Mac mini is a cheaper way to get a new Mac at $779 or £759.
There are bigger savings on MacBook Pro models if you need the extra power. In the U.S., Amazon has listed the 14-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro with 36GB of memory and 2TB of storage for $3,599, $500 off. In the U.K., the 16-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory and 1TB of storage is £2,599, £400 off. That’s about £536 less than the equivalent touchscreen model on sale, so think about how much you’d benefit from the OLED display before paying the premium.
Apple’s June price increases make the advertised savings worth a closer look. The U.S. MacBook Air deal is $50 below its pre-increase price, while the U.K. offer is still about £50 above what Apple charged before June. We compare prices for the same configurations so you can see which deals are worth taking and which have been better before.
Below, we explain which Mac to buy at these prices, from the budget MacBook Neo to the Mac Studio. If you’re deciding whether to buy now or wait for Apple’s November 27–30 promotion, compare what you’d pay today with what you’d actually use from a gift card on a future purchase. For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our Apple Black Friday deals roundups of the best iPad deals, Apple Watch deals and AirPods deals.
Apple Store Black Friday offer: From November 27 to 30, Apple is offering a gift card worth $200/£160 with either size of M5 MacBook Air, $250/£200 with an eligible 14-inch M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro, $300/£240 with an eligible 16-inch M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro, and $100/£80 with an eligible Mac mini. The gift card is for a future Apple purchase. Compare its value with the upfront discounts we share below. See the full Apple Black Friday offer.
Which Mac or MacBook should you buy this Black Friday?


MacBook Air – Our best overall choice 

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




The MacBook Air is our recommendation for most buyers. Both sizes offer a lightweight, silent laptop for everyday work, studying, and occasional creative projects. Choose the 13-inch for portability or the 15-inch for more workspace without MacBook Pro pricing.
We’d prioritize a competitive price on the memory and storage you need. For regular lengthy exports or other sustained demanding tasks, consider a MacBook Pro with active cooling instead.
U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the 13-inch M5 Air with 16GB memory and 512GB storage to $1,099, and the equivalent 15-inch to $1,299. We are already seeing up to $300 off the 13-inch models, and $300 off the 15-inch options, bringing the price below the original MSRP from before Apple increased prices. These savings are better than Apple’s $200 gift card.
U.K. Black Friday price: October offers included approximately £1,199 for the 13-inch M5 Air and £1,349 for the 15-inch, both with 512GB storage. Last Black Friday’s M4 models with 256GB reached £849 and £1,025. Match storage capacities when comparing generations. Amazon has the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage, 16GB of memory, and an 8-core GPU for £1,149, saving £150 off Apple’s £1,299 price. That’s about £50 less than it cost during October Prime Day. Amazon also has the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage and 16GB of memory for £1,299, saving £200 off Apple’s £1,499 price. Earlier in November, we saw a larger £200 discount on the 13-inch MacBook Air.
The £160 Apple gift card is close to the £150 upfront discount on the 13-inch 512GB Air.
Apple’s Deal: Apple’s £160 gift card is worth about £10 more than Amazon’s upfront discount on the 13-inch model. On the 15-inch model, Amazon’s upfront discount is £40 more than the gift card’s value.






MacBook Neo – Our budget choice, at the right price

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




The MacBook Neo suits browsing, schoolwork, streaming, and office apps. Its lower starting price makes it appealing, but its fixed 8GB of memory leaves less room for demanding workloads.
Check which configuration is discounted: only the 512GB version includes Touch ID. Both lack a backlit keyboard, MagSafe, and Thunderbolt. Compare clearance MacBook Air stock before deciding how much those compromises save you.
U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has the 256GB MacBook Neo for $599 ($100 off) and the 512GB model with Touch ID for $699 ($100 off) – the original on-sale prices for those models before Apple increased prices in June. 
U.K. Black Friday price: The 256GB MacBook Neo is £679.97 (£19.03 off), and the 512GB model with Touch ID is £719 (£80 off).






MacBook Pro M6 – Best step up from the Air

				
					

				
			
Macbook Pro M6 Aufmacher

Halyna Kubiv




The standard M6 MacBook Pro is worth considering if you want a better built-in display, more connections, and cooling for sustained workloads without paying for a Pro or Max chip. It comes in a 14-inch size, with a non-touch Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI, and an SDXC card slot.
It starts with 16GB memory and 1TB storage, so account for those specifications when comparing prices with an Air or older Pro. Despite the newer generation number, the standard M6 isn’t automatically the better choice for demanding work than an M5 Pro or M5 Max.
U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 model wasn’t available during October Prime Day, but it’s on offer for Black Friday with $200 off at Amazon, where it’s $1,799. B&H also has $150 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6)
U.K. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the older 14-inch M5 with 16GB memory and 1TB storage reached approximately £1,619. Amazon has the 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro with 16GB of memory and 1TB of storage for £1,829.97, saving £169.03. That’s just £30.97 more than the equivalent M5 model at £1,799, so we’d buy the M6.






MacBook Pro M5 Pro – Best for demanding professional work

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The non-touchscreen M5 Pro MacBook Pro is a strong choice for development, photography, video editing, and heavier multitasking. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, it offers professional performance without the Max chip’s higher price.
Compare it with the touchscreen version using the same memory and storage. Both offer M5 Pro configurations, so a discounted non-touch model could be particularly good value if its existing XDR display meets your needs.
U.S. Black Friday price: October prices included $2,339 for the 14-inch M5 Pro with 24GB memory and 1TB storage, and $2,749 for the equivalent 16-inch. So far this Black Friday month we are seeing $300 off the 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and $300 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro. Note that Amazon takes $250 off upfront while Apple offers $250 or $300 (depending on the model) in future credit, so it might be worth waiting for Apple’s deal if you are likely to want to make future Apple purchases.
U.K. Black Friday price: The equivalent configurations reached approximately £2,250 and £2,700. Last Black Friday, selected previous-generation M4 Pro models received discounts of around £350. The 14-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro, 24GB memory, 1TB SSD) is £2,289 (£210 off at Amazon), almost beating Apple’s £240 Gift card offer in the U.K.
Apple’s Deal: Apple will give a $250 U.S. or £200 U.K. Apple Gift Card with a 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro or M5 Max and a $300 U.S. or £240 U.K. Apple Gift Card with a 16-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro or M5 Max.






MacBook Pro M5 Max – Best for demanding graphics and video

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




Consider the non-touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro if your work benefits from additional graphics power or more memory than an M5 Pro supports. Complex 3D projects and demanding video production make a stronger case for it than everyday productivity.
We’d choose the configuration around the work you do. A larger advertised discount on a Max doesn’t necessarily make it better value than a less expensive Pro that meets your needs. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the options.
U.S. Black Friday price:  October offers included $3,499 for a 14-inch M5 Max with 2TB storage and $3,899 for a 16-inch with 36GB memory and 2TB storage. Last Black Friday, selected M4 Max configurations were $500 off and this Black Friday month we are already seeing $500 off the M5 Max models. 
U.K. Black Friday price:  In the U.K., both the 14-inch MacBook Pro and 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Max are currently on offer for £3,999 each.






Touchscreen MacBook Pro – Best for its OLED display

				
					

				
			


Roman Loyola/Foundry




The touchscreen MacBook Pro is most compelling for its OLED display and thinner, lighter design. Improved blacks and reduced blooming could matter more to your everyday experience than touch controls, particularly if you spend most of your working day using the built-in screen.
Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, these models offer comparable processing performance to their non-touch equivalents. Compare matching configurations: the regular premium is $400/£400, so consider how much you’ll benefit from the display before paying extra.
U.S. Black Friday price:  These models arrived in November, so there are no equivalent October Prime Day or Black Friday 2025 prices. So far, we’re seeing $200 off the 16-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro.
U.K. Black Friday price: In the U.K. we have seen Amazon knock £244 off the price of the MacBook Pro PROLED XDR Display (14-inch, M5 Pro, 1TB, Touchscreen),  although it’s now £224 off.






Mac mini M6 – Our best-value desktop choice

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The M6 Mac mini suits buyers who already own a display, keyboard, and mouse. It offers a compact desktop for everyday work and lighter creative projects. Check storage carefully: the entry-level model has a restrictive 256GB SSD.
U.S. Black Friday price: October’s entry-level M6 mini reached approximately $780. Last Black Friday, the older M4 equivalent was $479. So far this November we’ve seen $150 off the 512GB model.
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s M6 model reached approximately £824, compared with £499 for the M4 last Black Friday. For Black Friday the deal is even better at £140 off the 256GB Mac mini – the best price we’ve seen at £759. 
Apple’s Deal: Apple will give a $100 U.S. or £80 U.K. Apple Gift Card with a Mac mini purchase. 






Mac mini M5 Pro – Best compact desktop for professional work

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




The M5 Pro mini offers more processing power and memory capacity for demanding work without moving to a Studio. Compare upgraded configurations carefully: if the total approaches Mac Studio pricing, check which machine better suits your workload.
U.S. Black Friday price: The 24GB/512GB M5 Pro mini reached approximately $1,550 in October. Last Black Friday’s M4 Pro equivalent was $1,249. So far this November we’ve seen $150 off the 512GB model.
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s M5 Pro configuration reached approximately £1,647. The previous-generation M4 Pro with 24GB/512GB was £1,269 last Black Friday. There is £200 off the 512GB Mac mini M5 Pro in the U.K.
Apple’s Deal: Apple will give a $100 U.S. or £80 U.K. Apple Gift Card with a Mac mini purchase. 






iMac – Best complete desktop setup

				
					

				
			

Foundry




The iMac combines a 24-inch 4.5K display with the computer and matching accessories. Compare the two-port and four-port versions carefully: the latter adds processing power, connections, and a Touch ID keyboard. Factor those differences into the final price.
U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 wasn’t available during October Prime Day. The entry-level M4 predecessor reached approximately $1,360 in October and $1,149 last Black Friday. We are seeing $74 off the iMac M6 at Amazon. 
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s four-port M4 with 256GB storage was £1,620. Last Black Friday, comparable four-port M4 stock reached £1,349. These are predecessor prices rather than M6 targets. There’s £100 off the M4 iMac. 






Mac Studio – Best for demanding desktop workflows

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




The M5 Max Studio suits demanding graphics, video, and other professional workloads. Compare it with the M5 Pro mini first. The considerably more expensive M5 Ultra is for exceptional workloads requiring its additional performance and memory; most buyers won’t need it. Budget for a display and peripherals.
U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has the M5 Max Mac Studio with 36GB of memory and 512GB of storage for $2,299, matching October Prime Day’s $200 discount.
U.K. Black Friday price: The Mac Studio was £209 off in the U.K., but it’s back to full price now.

Should you buy a Mac or MacBook now or wait for a better deal?
With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need a Mac immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so an early offer can be worth taking if it matches or approaches a previous low for the same configuration. Waiting can be a gamble if you’re buying clearance stock with a particular screen size, memory capacity, or finish. If the retailer discount is close to Apple’s gift card value and you already have another Apple purchase planned, it may be worth waiting until November 27 to take advantage of Apple’s gift card offer, but note that MacBook Neo, standard M6 MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac Studio are not included in Apple’s Black Friday deal. 
The M5 MacBook Air remains an appealing purchase at a good discount, with a replacement not expected until 2027. The recently updated Mac mini and Mac Studio are also worth considering if they meet your needs. The main reason to wait is a better price rather than an imminent replacement.
MacBook Pro buyers no longer need to wait for the rumored October launches: the standard M6 and OLED touchscreen models are now available. However, their recent arrival may limit initial discounts. Non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max models could offer better value, particularly if you don’t need the touchscreen version’s improved display and lighter design. If your existing M4 or M5 MacBook Pro still meets your needs, there’s little reason to upgrade simply because a newer option exists.
The M6 iMac has only just arrived, replacing the aging M4 version. Compare a modest saving on the latest model with a substantial clearance discount on its predecessor, rather than assuming the older machine is automatically the better deal.
Previous prices need context this year. Following June’s increases, a discount from Apple’s current asking price may still leave you paying more than before the increases. Compare retailers as well: Amazon competes with Best Buy, Walmart, and B&H in the U.S., and retailers including Currys and John Lewis in the U.K. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the current choices.






Which Mac specifications are worth paying for?
The cheapest Mac isn’t always the best value. Use Black Friday to get a configuration that will serve you for longer within your budget, but don’t pay for performance or features you won’t use.
Check the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. A standard M6 and an M5 Pro or M5 Max serve different needs: the newer generation number alone doesn’t tell you which is better for your work. For MacBook Pro listings, distinguish the OLED touchscreen version from non-touch models.
Avoid saving a small amount by buying too little memory or storage. Most current Macs start with 16GB of unified memory, but the MacBook Neo has a fixed 8GB, and some desktop configurations include only a 256GB SSD. Unified memory cannot be upgraded later. An external SSD can add storage, but it cannot compensate for insufficient RAM.
Once the processor meets your needs, additional memory may be more useful than a faster chip. Compare a discounted Air with the Neo, too: the M5 Air starts with twice the memory and storage of the entry-level Neo. Our Mac buying guide explains which specifications suit different workloads.
Check whether the configuration includes nano-texture glass. This optional finish reduces glare and reflections, which can help in bright rooms or near windows, but increases the price. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may offer better value.






Should you buy an older Mac or MacBook?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older Mac can be excellent value if its price reflects its age and configuration. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of the newer equivalent, rather than focusing on a large percentage saving from its original launch price.
Previous-generation Apple silicon models are the most promising starting point. A discounted M4 MacBook Air or standard M5 MacBook Pro may meet your needs comfortably. Older Pro and Max configurations can also be worth considering if they provide the memory, graphics performance, and connections your work requires for substantially less money.
Check what the saving buys—and what you give up. An older Mac with more memory or storage could be more useful than a newer entry-level configuration. Conversely, a cheaper older Air with 256GB storage isn’t directly comparable with an M5 Air that starts with 512GB. The non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros also remain current options, despite the arrival of the standard M6 and touchscreen models.
Be much more cautious with Intel Macs. Their software support is winding down, and a low purchase price may leave you with a machine that has a limited useful life for current apps and macOS features. Check compatibility with the software you need before buying any older model.
For used or refurbished Macs, check battery condition on laptops, warranty coverage, and the returns policy. Confirm that Activation Lock has been removed and that the Mac isn’t still enrolled in an organization’s management system.

Mac or MacBook deals to avoid
Treat large advertised discounts carefully. Following June’s price increases, “$400 off” may simply bring a Mac closer to what it cost before the increase. Compare previous selling prices for the same configuration, rather than judging the offer solely against today’s recommended price.
Check whether the price includes AppleCare+ or another protection plan. Some Amazon listings bundle coverage with the Mac. If you don’t want it, a listing without coverage could be cheaper; if you do, compare the bundle with buying the Mac and coverage separately.
Check for a bundled power adapter, too. Some Mac laptops are sold without one in the U.K. and EU. A charger bundle may be useful if you need an adapter, but could mean paying extra unnecessarily if you already own a suitable one.
Compare the complete setup cost. A Mac mini or Studio requires a display, keyboard, and mouse or trackpad, while adapters and docks can add to the cost of any Mac.
Finally, distinguish cash discounts from gift cards, trade-ins, financing, and membership-only offers. Read the conditions, check the seller, and confirm whether the Mac is new, refurbished, or used, along with its warranty and returns policy.






How we choose Mac and MacBook deals
Macworld has covered the Mac since its launch in 1984, and our recommendations draw on decades of experience and hands-on reviews. We consider performance, display quality, battery life, portability, connectivity, and everyday use alongside price to explain which Macs suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess which upgrades are worth paying for. We look at whether additional processing power benefits demanding workloads, when more memory is useful, and whether a premium display justifies the extra cost. A MacBook Air may offer better value for everyday work, while a Pro, Max, or Ultra configuration needs to earn its higher price through the work it enables.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than judging a deal solely against today’s recommended retail price. A large advertised discount doesn’t automatically make an offer exceptional.
We consider the complete purchase, too: the retailer, product condition, warranty, and any conditions attached to the price. For desktop Macs, we also account for the display and accessories you’ll need. Our Mac buying guide and MacBook comparison explain how to choose the right model and configuration.
For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our roundups of the best iPad deals, AirPods deals, and Apple Watch deals.

title: Best AirPods 2026: Which AirPods should you buy?
content:
Macworld





Apple’s AirPods lineup falls into three main families: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. For most buyers, the choice is between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3. AirPods 5 start at $129 and combine an open-ear design with Active Noise Cancellation, while the $249 AirPods Pro 3 use foam-infused silicone tips for a more secure fit and stronger noise isolation. They also add heart-rate sensing and Apple’s hearing-health features. AirPods Max 2 are a different proposition: $549 over-ear headphones for buyers who value sound quality and noise cancellation and prefer an over-ear fit. Right now is a fantastic time to buy AirPods because, thanks to Black Friday prices, there are some excellent bargains to be had.

When deciding which AirPods to buy, start with the fit you’ll be happy wearing for hours, then compare what you’d actually pay for the features you’ll use. If you prefer an open fit, AirPods 5 are the better buy, and the wireless charging version is worth a small premium for its longer battery life and swipe volume controls. If a sale brings AirPods Pro 3 close to the price of AirPods 5 and you’re comfortable with silicone tips, the Pro 3 are the better value for their stronger noise cancellation and longer battery life. Even at a discount, AirPods Max 2 make the most sense if you specifically want over-ear headphones.
In this guide, we compare Apple’s current AirPods on fit, sound, noise cancellation, battery life, hearing features, and price. We also explain which version of AirPods 5 to buy and when a discount makes an older model worth considering.


Which AirPods are the best?
We recommend AirPods Pro 3 as the best AirPods overall, thanks to their combination of noise cancellation, secure fit, longer battery life and additional health features.
For many people, however, AirPods 5 will be the better buy. They now include Active Noise Cancellation, Adaptive Audio, Transparency mode and Conversation Awareness, closing much of the feature gap with the Pro model while costing substantially less. They’re also the obvious choice if you prefer an open fit rather than silicone ear tips.
AirPods Max 2 are best considered separately. They are over-ear headphones rather than earbuds and cost more than twice as much as AirPods Pro 3, so they make most sense for buyers specifically looking for that style of headphone.

In our review, Jason Cross praised their more comfortable and secure fit, improved battery life, better noise cancellation and Transparency mode, and effective heart-rate sensor. Taken together, those apparently small changes add up to a significant improvement.
The biggest physical change is the fit. AirPods Pro 3 have redesigned earbuds with foam-infused tips available in five sizes, including XXS. In our testing, they stayed securely in place even during intense activity and felt more comfortable than the previous generation.
Noise cancellation is another major advantage. Apple says AirPods Pro 3 remove twice as much noise as AirPods Pro 2, while our review also found improvements to noise reduction, Transparency mode and bass response.
Battery life is strong too. Apple rates the earbuds for up to eight hours with ANC enabled, an estimate that was broadly borne out in our testing. The charging case takes total ANC listening time to up to 24 hours.
AirPods Pro 3 also have features the AirPods 5 don’t. The built-in heart-rate sensor works with workouts in the Fitness app, while Apple’s Hearing Test, Hearing Aid and Hearing Protection features make the Pro model particularly compelling for users interested in hearing health.

AirPods 5 vs AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy?

				
					

				
			
AirPods Pro 3 vs AirPods 5

Foundry





AirPods 5 are better if…
You dislike earbuds that seal your ear canal.
You want to spend less.
An open fit is more important than maximum noise isolation.
You want ANC but don’t need the Pro health features.
AirPods Pro 3 are better if…
You want Apple’s hearing-health features.
Strong noise cancellation is a priority.
You want longer battery life.
You want a more secure in-ear fit.
You want heart-rate sensing.
The difference between standard AirPods and AirPods Pro used to be straightforward: standard AirPods were cheaper and open-fitting, while the Pros added ANC and Apple’s more sophisticated listening modes.
With the AirPods 5, that distinction is less clear. Both AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 use Apple’s H2 chip and support Active Noise Cancellation, Adaptive Audio, Transparency mode, Conversation Awareness, Voice Isolation and Personalized Spatial Audio.
The remaining differences are nevertheless significant.
Design and fit
AirPods 5 use an open-ear design and don’t use ear tips. AirPods Pro 3 sit more tightly in the ear canal and come with foam-infused silicone tips in five sizes. When we reviewed the AirPods Pro 3 we found the redesigned tips substantially improved comfort and security and kept the earbuds in place during strenuous exercise.
Choose AirPods 5 if you don’t like the plugged-ear sensation of silicone tips.
Choose AirPods Pro 3 if you want a tighter, more secure fit and better isolation.
Noise cancellation
AirPods 5 include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, unlike AirPods 4, which were sold with or without ANC. But their open-ear design means they approach noise reduction differently from the AirPods Pro 3.
AirPods Pro 3 use ear tips to create a seal in the ear canal, giving them a natural advantage when it comes to isolation. Apple says their ANC removes up to twice as much noise as AirPods Pro 2, and in our testing both noise cancellation and Transparency mode were improved over the previous generation.
AirPods 5 don’t create a seal, but their open-ear ANC is significantly more effective than before. Apple says they remove up to 50 percent more external noise than AirPods 4 with ANC.
AirPods 5 are the better choice if you dislike the feeling of a sealed in-ear fit.
AirPods Pro 3 remain the better choice if maximum noise reduction and isolation are your priorities.
Battery life
AirPods Pro 3 have a significant battery advantage. They last up to eight hours with ANC enabled and up to 24 hours including the charging case.
The $129 AirPods 5 manage up to four hours with ANC, while the $149 Wireless Charging Case version increases that to five hours.
That’s a substantial difference if you frequently use your AirPods for long journeys or extended listening sessions.
AirPods 5 = 4 hours battery life 
AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case = 5 hours battery life
AirPods Pro 3 = 8 hours battery life
Health and hearing features
The AirPods Pro 3 include a heart-rate sensor that can measure your heart rate during workouts, and our reviewer found the results comparable to an Apple Watch during testing.
They also support Apple’s Hearing Test, Hearing Aid and Hearing Protection features.
Those features aren’t available on AirPods 5.
AirPods Pro 3 are also the obvious choice if Apple’s health features are important.
Price
The Pro model costs $100 more than the AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case and $120 more than the cheapest version.
The gap can shrink during sales. AirPods Pro 3 fell to $149 during Black Friday 2026, which is the same price as the AirPods 5 with wireless charging, so it’s always worth checking the live price comparison before deciding.
AirPods 5 start at $129, or $149 with the Wireless Charging Case.
AirPods Pro 3 are $249.






Which AirPods 5 should you get? 
Unlike AirPods 4, Apple doesn’t sell one AirPods 5 model with ANC and another without it. All AirPods 5 have Active Noise Cancellation.
Instead, the choice is between cases.
The $129 model has a USB-C charging case. It offers up to four hours of battery life with ANC and up to 20 hours including the case.
For $149, the Wireless Charging Case can also charge using an Apple Watch charger or Qi charger and includes a speaker for Find My. The earbuds in this package also support volume adjustment by swiping the stems. Battery life increases to five hours with ANC and 22 hours with the case.
Our recommendation: Buy the version with wireless charging case – given the relatively small $20 difference, the $149 version is the better buy for most people.






Should you buy older AirPods?
We’d generally recommend buying the latest generation rather than deliberately seeking out older AirPods because there is a considerable gap between the different generations. 
Should you buy AirPods 4?
AirPods 5 start at the same $129 MSRP previously charged for AirPods 4 without ANC, but now include ANC as standard, along with improved noise cancellation and sound quality.
That makes AirPods 4 difficult to recommend unless you find them at a substantial clearance discount. They dropped to $99 during Prime Day 2026, but with AirPods 5 now available at $129, we’d want to see them priced noticeably lower than that.
Our recommendation: Only buy AirPods 4 at a steep discount.

Should you buy AirPods Pro 2?
AirPods Pro 2 remain capable earbuds, but AirPods Pro 3 improve the fit, noise cancellation and battery life, while adding heart-rate sensing.
Our recommendation: We’d buy AirPods Pro 2 only if they’re at least $30 or £30 cheaper than the best AirPods Pro 3 price you can get. If the gap is smaller, we’d pay the difference for the Pro 3’s stronger noise cancellation, longer battery life, and improved fit.
Should you buy the original AirPods Max?
AirPods Max 2 retain many aspects of the original design but add the H2 chip, which enables Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Voice Isolation and Live Translation. ANC has also been improved.
If you’re going to spend close to AirPods Max money, the second-generation model is therefore the one to get.

 FAQ 


1.
What’s the difference between AirPods and AirPods Pro?
The biggest difference is fit. AirPods 5 use an open-ear design, while AirPods Pro 3 use foam-infused silicone tips that seal the ear canal.
Both now have Active Noise Cancellation, Adaptive Audio, Transparency mode and Conversation Awareness. AirPods Pro 3 nevertheless offer stronger isolation, longer ANC battery life and exclusive features including heart-rate sensing, Hearing Test, Hearing Aid and Hearing Protection.
AirPods 5 start at $129; AirPods Pro 3 cost $249.





2.
Do AirPods work with Macs and iPads?
Yes. AirPods work particularly well with Apple devices.
Once your AirPods are paired, they can automatically connect to devices associated with your Apple account, and Automatic Device Switching can move playback between devices depending on what you’re using.
Apple lists current versions of macOS and iPadOS among the supported platforms for AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2.





3.
Can you use AirPods with non-Apple devices?
Yes. AirPods are Bluetooth headphones and can be used with non-Apple hardware.
We have, for example, demonstrated how AirPods can be paired directly with a Nintendo Switch using its Bluetooth Audio settings.
Apple also explicitly states that current AirPods can be used as Bluetooth headphones with non-Apple devices, although some functionality may be limited.
The main reason to use AirPods with Apple hardware is therefore the deeper ecosystem integration rather than basic Bluetooth compatibility.





4.
Do AirPods have Find My?
Yes, but the capabilities depend on the model and case.
AirPods can be located through Apple’s Find My system. The $149 AirPods 5 Wireless Charging Case includes a speaker for Find My alerts, while the standard $129 USB-C case does not. AirPods Pro 3 also include a speaker in their MagSafe charging case.
Find My support is useful not just for locating misplaced AirPods but also when checking whether a suspicious pair of AirPods behaves as genuine Apple hardware. See our guide to spotting fake AirPods for more advice.





5.
Are AirPods waterproof?
No. AirPods aren’t “waterproof”, but they do offer some water resistance. 
AirPods 5 are rated IP57 for dust, sweat and water resistance. AirPods Pro 3 and their charging case are also rated IP57.
That makes them suitable for exercise and provides protection against water exposure, but water resistance isn’t the same thing as waterproofing and shouldn’t be taken as an invitation to use them for swimming.
AirPods Max 2 don’t have a water-resistance rating.

title: Turn your iPhone Duo into the world’s smallest laptop with this cute app
content:
Macworld





Every time I refer to the iPhone Duo as “Apple’s first foldable product” I pause for a moment and wonder: do laptops count? After all, they’ve had a folding hinge for decades. The iPhone Duo, if you think about it, is really just a tiny laptop.
If that strikes you as a whimsical thought, you’ll be delighted to hear about a newly updated app which offers to make that comparison a reality. A really, really cute reality.
Screens 5: VNC Remote Desktop is, as the name suggests, an app which enables you to remotely share screens between devices. You can use it, for example, to access your work MacBook on your iPhone, iPad, another Mac, or Vision Pro. It’s a largely work-focused app that you’d expect to focus on productivity rather than eye-catching features.
But with the version 5.10.6 update, which was rolled out for the iPhone on November 25 (maker Edovia says the equivalent update for the Mac version is awaiting App Store approval), something rather fun has been added: Laptop Mode for iPhone Duo. When you use this mode on a semi-folded Duo and connect to a MacBook, the shared output is displayed in a way which mimics the layout of a laptop. “Simply fold your iPhone Duo halfway to turn it into a pocket-sized workstation, with your remote desktop on the upper half and a custom keyboard and trackpad below,” Edovia explains in a blog post.
It’s absolutely adorable. And functional, too. “The trackpad supports the same familiar gestures you’ve come to expect from Screens,” Edovia adds, “while the custom keyboard supports multiple languages, follows your selected system keyboard language, and lets you swipe down on keys to access secondary characters, just like on iPad.”
Screens is officially a free app, but it has pretty much zero functionality without a subscription. If you’re keen to try out the new mode and turn your iPhone Duo into a tiny laptop, you could start a trial subscription, but (assuming you don’t find the app so useful that you decide to use it in the long term) remember to cancel it before you get charged. It’s a cute feature, but on its own it probably isn’t worth $4.99 a month.

title: Kodak Launches Unique AirTag Rival With E-Ink Display
content:
Kodak licensee Reto this week introduced the SlideTag, a $34.99 Find My-compatible item tracker with a color E Ink screen for displaying personal photos.


The SlideTag's design draws on Kodak's Kodachrome slide mounts, placing a square display inside a retro frame with an attachment point for a keyring. Its 1.54-inch screen has a resolution of 240 × 240 pixels and uses six ink colors to reproduce images. As it is an E Ink panel, it retains a static image without needing continuous power to display it.

Users can manage photos through the Kodak Memory Link app for iOS and Android, separately from the accessory's tracking features. They can transfer up to 12 images over Bluetooth and arrange them into slideshows, or use the screen to display information such as contact details, a QR code, or a to-do list.

Find My app, the SlideTag can be located through the ‌Find My‌ network. There is also support for Google's Find Hub. A built-in buzzer provides an audible way to find nearby belongings.

AirTag, but slightly thinner. Apple's tracker measures 31.9mm in diameter and 8mm thick, and weighs 11.8 grams.

The ‌AirTag‌ retains some advantages, including Ultra Wideband technology for Precision Finding, which provides distance and directional guidance to nearby items on compatible devices. The ‌AirTag‌ also has a higher IP67 rating, providing protection against immersion in water up to one meter deep for up to 30 minutes.

title: Best AirPods Black Friday deals 2026: Our picks for Pro, standard AirPods and Max
content:

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 26, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
Black Friday is a great time to buy AirPods, with retailers competing to offer discounts across Apple’s earbuds and over-ear headphones. Previous sales have brought substantial savings on established models, clearance bargains on older generations, and even discounts on newly released AirPods. But the biggest percentage saving doesn’t necessarily mean the best buy: an older pair needs to be sufficiently cheaper than its replacement to justify missing out on newer features.
The best Black Friday AirPods deal we’ve seen so far is on the AirPods Pro 3. Amazon has listed them for $149 in the U.S. and £156 in the U.K., saving $100 and £63, respectively. If Amazon lists the AirPods Pro as out of stock, the $149 deal is also available at Walmart. That’s a much bigger U.S. discount than the roughly $30 off we saw last Black Friday. If you prefer over-ear headphones, Amazon has also listed the AirPods Max 2 for $419 in the U.S., $130 off and just $20 above the lowest price we’ve tracked.
If you prefer an open-ear fit, AirPods 5 are the cheaper option: in the U.K. we’ve seen £20 off the wireless charging AirPods 5, at £119, while it was still at its regular $149 U.S. price at our last check. Below, we explain which AirPods to choose and how the offers compare with previous discounts. For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our Apple Black Friday deals roundups of the best Mac deals, iPad deals, and Apple Watch deals.
Apple’s own Black Friday offer runs November 27–30, 2026. Buy eligible AirPods directly from Apple, and you’ll receive a gift card to use on a future purchase. More details here: Apple Black Friday 2026: Up to $300/£240 in gift cards – full list of eligible products.




Which AirPods should you buy this Black Friday?


AirPods Pro 3 – Our best overall choice

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods Pro 3 are especially worth considering if you want strong noise cancellation, a secure in-ear fit, or Apple’s hearing-health features. Their foam-infused ear tips help improve the fit, while an in-ear heart-rate sensor adds another reason to choose them over standard AirPods. Battery life is rated at up to eight hours with noise cancellation enabled.
For most buyers looking for noise-isolating earbuds, these would be our first choice. Older AirPods Pro 2 are worth considering only when the clearance savings are substantial.
U.S. Black Friday price:  Amazon has slashed $100 off the AirPods Pro 3, to just $149, the same price as the AirPods 5 with wireless charging case and below their previous all-time low of $169. Amazon sold out for a day or so, but got more stock; if that happens again, Walmart also has them at that price.
U.K. Black Friday price: Earlier in November, AirPods Pro 3 were £30 off in the U.K., before rising to £200, then dropping down to £174, only to return to £200. Amazon now has the AirPods Pro 3 for £155.98, £63.02 off the £219 RRP! We recommend being quick because that price is going up and down like a Swanee whistle.
Apple’s deal: You can get a $50/£40 gift card with your purchase. 






AirPods 5 – Best for buyers who prefer earbuds without silicone tips

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods 5 offer a lower-cost entry point and an open-ear design for people who don’t like silicone-tipped earbuds. They include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, alongside Transparency mode and Adaptive Audio.
Check which charging case you’re buying. The Wireless Charging Case package adds wireless charging, longer battery life, a Find My speaker, and volume adjustment by swiping the stems. It’s our preferred package when the price difference is small.
U.S. Black Friday price: We’ve not seen a discount yet on the AirPods 5.
U.K. Black Friday price:  You can get £20 off the AirPods 5 with wireless charging in the U.K. That’s the same as Apple’s gift card ‘saving’.
Apple’s deal: Get a $25/£20 gift card with the purchase of AirPods 5.






AirPods Max 2 – Best for over-ear listening

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods Max 2 are the option to consider if you specifically want over-ear headphones. The March 2026 update introduced Apple’s H2 chip and improved noise cancellation, while retaining the premium design and a choice of colors.
We find them difficult to recommend at full price, so the size of the discount matters. Compare any offer with previous sale prices rather than judging it solely against Apple’s asking price.
U.S. Black Friday price:  Amazon has the AirPods Max 2 for $419, a $130 saving.
U.K. Black Friday price:  AirPods Max 2 were reduced to £449 at Amazon, but they are now back at the full £499. From November 27, Apple will include a £60 gift card with AirPods Max purchases. 
Apple’s deal: Get a $75/£60 gift card with the purchase of AirPods Max 2. 






Other headphones – Worthy AirPods alternatives

				
					

				
			
Beats




If AirPods aren’t in your budget, Apple also sells a line of Beats headphones and earbuds that offer many of the same features for a lower price, including the popular on-ear Solo 4 and Powerbeats Pro 2. We’ll also track headphone deals in our roundup of the best earbuds for iPhone and best over-ear headphones if you’d like to see deals on other brands.

U.K. Black Friday price:  There is £90 off the Powerbeats Pro 2 and £100 off the Powerbeats Fit at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.

Should you buy AirPods now or wait for a better deal?

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need AirPods immediately. But the sales now stretch across much of November, so you don’t necessarily need to wait for Black Friday itself. If an early offer is close to a model’s previous low, it can be worth taking: last year’s best deals frequently sold out, and popular offers could go quickly again.
Previous sale prices provide useful benchmarks. At $149, AirPods Pro 3 are $20 below the previous low we tracked, while AirPods Max 2 fell to $399 during June Prime Day. An offer above those prices may still be worth considering, but a reduction from Apple’s regular price doesn’t automatically make it an exceptional deal.
For AirPods 5, waiting for a discount makes sense if you aren’t in a hurry: they didn’t receive a significant reduction during October Prime Day. With AirPods Max 2, we’d hold out for a substantial saving rather than pay full price.
Compare retailers, too. Amazon isn’t always cheapest: Walmart and Best Buy also compete on AirPods pricing, while Argos offered competitive U.K. deals last year. Our guide to the best time to buy AirPods has more advice on purchase timing.






Should you buy an old pair of AirPods? 
Older-generation AirPods can be a good buy at the right clearance price. Compare their actual selling price with the discounted price of their replacement, rather than focusing on the percentage saving from an old launch price. A substantial discount can make an older pair worthwhile; a small difference may leave you sacrificing useful features for little saving.
AirPods 4 are harder to recommend now that AirPods 5 include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, starting at the same $129 price previously charged for AirPods 4 without ANC. Check which AirPods 4 version you’re buying—there were models with and without noise cancellation—and look for a substantial saving over AirPods 5.
AirPods Pro 2 remain worth considering if they’re significantly cheaper than Pro 3. However, the newer model improves fit, noise cancellation, and battery life, while adding heart-rate sensing. Compare their sale prices carefully: a strong Pro 3 discount could make the older pair’s clearance offer less attractive.
The original AirPods Max also need a substantial discount to justify choosing them over Max 2. The newer headphones add the H2 chip, improved noise cancellation, and features including Adaptive Audio and Conversation Awareness. Check the generation rather than relying on the charging port alone: the original AirPods Max were also sold in a USB-C version.
Buying older stock new is different from buying used or refurbished AirPods. For those pairs, check the stated condition, charging case, warranty, and returns policy, and buy from a reputable seller. Be cautious about battery condition and unusually low marketplace prices, since convincing counterfeits can resemble genuine AirPods. Our guide explains how to spot fake AirPods.
For more advice, see our AirPods buying guide and guide to the best time to buy AirPods.






AirPods deals to avoid

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Check exactly what an offer includes before comparing prices. Different charging-case packages can affect features and value, so make sure you’re comparing equivalent versions. Also check any spending requirements, contracts, or rebates attached to offers advertising “free” AirPods.
Judge the price against previous selling prices as well as the advertised discount. A large saving from the recommended retail price doesn’t necessarily mean a particularly good deal if retailers regularly charge less.
Check whether the listing is for a new, refurbished, or used pair. For used or refurbished AirPods, look for clear information about condition, warranty, and returns coverage. Battery condition deserves particular caution: a low purchase price may be less attractive if listening time has deteriorated.
Finally, check who is selling and dispatching your order, particularly when shopping through a marketplace. Unusually low prices from unfamiliar sellers warrant caution, since counterfeit AirPods can look convincing. Our guide explains how to tell if AirPods are fake.






How we choose AirPods deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on AirPods reviews. We consider sound quality, noise cancellation, comfort, battery life, and everyday use – not just the specifications or advertised saving.
Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our AirPods Pro 3 review assessed how securely the redesigned ear tips stayed in place during exercise, checked battery life against Apple’s claims, and evaluated the heart-rate sensor. Our AirPods Max 2 review weighed their excellent sound and noise cancellation against drawbacks including weight and the Smart Case.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. Our Best AirPods guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the best choice for everyone: fit, listening habits, and the features you need all matter.

The biggest savings are on configurations with more storage. Amazon has listed the 11-inch M5 iPad Pro with 1TB for $1,499 in the U.S. a saving of about $300. The gift card is for a future purchase. See our full guide to Apple’s Black Friday offer.
Which iPad should you buy this Black Friday?


M4 iPad Air – Our best all-round choice

				
					

				
			
Apple Inc




The iPad Air offers a strong balance of performance, screen size, and price without the premium cost of the Pro. The 11-inch model suits buyers who prioritize portability, while the 13-inch version gives you more room for multitasking and creative work.
A good Black Friday discount could make either size an attractive purchase. Compare storage capacities carefully, though: a larger advertised saving on a high-capacity model isn’t necessarily better value if you don’t need the extra space. 
U.S. Black Friday price: At Amazon, you can already get a saving of $100 off some iPad Air models, although in some cases these are selling out, in which case we are seeing Best Buy match the $100 off.

iPad Pro – Best for demanding creative work

				
					

				
			
Apple Inc




The iPad Pro is the option for buyers who need Apple’s highest-end tablet performance and premium display. It comes in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes, but its capabilities – and price – will exceed what many people need for browsing, streaming, and everyday apps.
We’d look for a substantial saving rather than buy simply because it’s the most powerful iPad. Compare discounted M4 iPad Pro models, too: an older Pro could offer better value if its price is sufficiently below the equivalent M5 configuration.

Apple

That makes the final purchase price particularly important. A modest discount from today’s higher asking price may still leave you paying more than this iPad previously cost. With a replacement expected early in 2027, we’d look for a substantial Black Friday saving and compare the price with discounted iPad Air models before buying.

Apple

Because it has only just arrived, we’d expect initial discounts to be smaller than clearance savings on its predecessor. The older A17 Pro mini could still be worthwhile at a sufficiently low price, but compare the saving with what you give up – particularly the new display.

Should you buy an older iPad? 

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older iPad can be a good buy if its price reflects its age and the features you give up. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of its replacement, matching screen size, storage, and connectivity where possible. A large saving from an old launch price doesn’t necessarily make it better value.
The M3 iPad Air and M4 iPad Pro are worth considering at substantial clearance discounts. Both remain capable options, and you may get more benefit from a lower price or additional storage than from the latest processor. However, if the newer equivalent costs only slightly more, the saving may not justify choosing the older generation.
The A17 Pro iPad mini also deserves consideration now that the A20 Pro model has arrived. It supports Apple Intelligence and remains a capable compact tablet, but you miss the newer model’s OLED display, faster processor, and thinner, lighter design. We’d want a meaningful saving rather than a small reduction from its former asking price.
Be more cautious with much older models. Check whether they support the current version of iPadOS and the apps and features you need. Compatibility today doesn’t guarantee how many future software upgrades they’ll receive. Apple Intelligence support also varies: don’t assume every older Air, Pro, or mini includes it.
If you already own an Apple Pencil or keyboard, check compatibility before changing generations. Keeping compatible accessories could make an older iPad better value, while replacing them could erase part of your saving. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges.






iPad deals to avoid
Check the exact configuration before comparing offers. Retailer listings can emphasize iPad, Air, or Pro without making the generation obvious. Confirm the chip, screen size, storage capacity, and whether you’re buying Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi + Cellular. A cheaper listing may be a different model rather than a better deal.
Don’t let a large advertised discount tempt you into paying for storage or connectivity you won’t use. A heavily reduced high-capacity or cellular iPad can still cost more than a simpler configuration that meets your needs. Compare the final purchase prices, rather than assuming the biggest saving represents the best value.
Check whether the price includes nano-texture glass, too. This optional finish (on the 1TB and 2TB M5 iPad Pro and the 256GB and 512GB A20 Pro iPad mini) reduces glare and makes fingerprints and oily smudges less noticeable, which can be useful if reflections make your iPad difficult to see in bright rooms or outdoors. It avoids much of the washed-out appearance associated with ordinary matte finishes, but contrast can drop at some viewing angles and the surface may be more scratch-sensitive. Availability depends on the model and storage configuration, so you could end up paying for both the finish and additional storage. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may be better value. Read our guide to nano-texture glass and whether you need it.
Our iPad buying guide considers cellular a luxury for most buyers. If you mainly use your iPad somewhere with Wi-Fi, you may get little benefit from the extra hardware. For occasional use elsewhere, sharing your iPhone’s connection through Personal Hotspot can be a more economical option.
Cellular makes more sense if you regularly need an independent connection while commuting or traveling; it also adds built-in GPS for accurate location tracking. Factor in any data-plan charges and compare the total cost of a contract with buying outright. A cellular model can still be worthwhile if its sale price matches or beats the equivalent Wi-Fi version—you don’t have to activate a data plan simply because the hardware is included.
Judge savings against previous selling prices as well as Apple’s current price. Following June’s price increases, a discounted iPad may still cost more than it did earlier in the year. Also distinguish a cash discount from a gift-card offer: a gift card doesn’t reduce the amount you pay for the iPad and is useful only if you’ll spend it.
Check what any bundle includes. A keyboard, case, or stylus doesn’t automatically make an offer better value, particularly if the accessories aren’t the versions you want. Read the conditions attached to “free” iPads, trade-in promotions, contracts, and rebates before comparing their total cost with buying outright.
Finally, check whether the iPad is new, refurbished, or used, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For used or refurbished models, look for information about battery condition and confirm that Activation Lock has been removed. Be cautious about devices that remain tied to a previous owner or an organization’s management system.






How we choose iPad deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on iPad reviews and everyday use. We consider performance, display quality, portability, battery life, and accessory support alongside price to explain which iPads suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess whether paying more brings practical benefits. A faster processor or premium display may matter for demanding creative work, while a less expensive iPad can be perfectly capable of browsing, streaming, and schoolwork. We also consider the cost of keyboards, Apple Pencils, and other accessories when judging an iPad’s value.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than relying solely on savings against today’s recommended price.
Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside newer alternatives. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges, while our purchase-timing guide helps you decide whether to buy now or wait.

title: Apple Still Working on Giant Foldable iPad That Could Cost $5,000
content:
Apple is still developing a large foldable iPad despite ongoing technical challenges and uncertainty about whether it will ever launch, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.


Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast, Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "Project J312." He described it as a foldable iPad with a display measuring around 19 to 20 inches, saying it would resemble a "gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside." The device could cost between $3,000 and $5,000.

Apple apparently originally wanted to announce the device by 2027, before pushing that target to 2028. The timeframe has since slipped to around 2029, although Gurman cautioned that it remains uncertain whether the product will ever reach the market.

Gurman cited cost and display manufacturing yield issues among the obstacles facing development, along with concerns that the ‌iPad‌ could be cumbersome. Apple has also yet to determine which operating system it would run, with macOS, iPadOS, and an entirely new platform all remaining possibilities. Gurman described the unresolved software direction as another complication, but expressed excitement about the device's potential.

report from research firm Omdia in September, which claimed that Apple had canceled plans for a foldable MacBook measuring between 16.1 and 18 inches when unfolded. Earlier reports had described that device as a large-screened foldable ‌iPad‌, although it remains unclear whether Omdia was referring to the same project Gurman discussed.

discussed the foldable ‌iPad‌ in April, describing it as a priority for John Ternus while warning that it could remain an unreleased experiment. Should you buy an older Apple Watch?

Don’t assume an older Apple Watch is a bad buy. The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are only one generation old and can make excellent purchases if they’re substantially cheaper than the Series 12 or Ultra 4. Both retain many of their replacements’ core features, although you miss the newer Health Sensing System and, with the Ultra 3, the Ultra 4’s longer battery life.
Compare actual selling prices, matching case size, material, connectivity, and band where possible. A $50 difference between a Series 11 and Series 12 may not be enough to justify giving up the newer model’s health features, whereas a substantially larger saving could change the calculation. Be much more cautious with the Series 8, SE 2, and original Ultra: those models cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 9 is the oldest standard Apple Watch compatible with the latest software, while the Ultra 2 is the oldest supported Ultra and the SE 3 is the only supported SE. Missing the latest software doesn’t make an older watch unusable, but it makes it harder to recommend as a purchase today.
The Series 9, Series 10, and Ultra 2 can still be worth considering at sufficiently low prices. However, compatibility with today’s software doesn’t guarantee how many future upgrades they’ll receive. Weigh the savings against the watch’s age and features, rather than assuming every supported generation offers equally good value.






Apple Watch deals to avoid 

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Don’t let a bigger advertised discount tempt you into paying more for a cellular Apple Watch you won’t use. If your iPhone is usually nearby, a GPS model can already handle calls, messages, and notifications through your phone. It can also track runs, use Apple Pay, and play downloaded music without your iPhone. As our experience testing a cellular Apple Watch showed, the extra connectivity may add little to everyday use.
Cellular is worth considering if you regularly leave your iPhone behind and want to remain contactable without Wi-Fi, or you’re setting up a watch for a child without an iPhone. Otherwise, you could pay extra for the hardware and then add an ongoing mobile-plan charge for a feature you rarely need. You don’t have to activate a plan on a cellular model, so it can still be a good buy if its sale price matches or beats the GPS version. Our GPS versus cellular Apple Watch guide explains the trade-offs.
Check the rest of the configuration, too. A premium case material or expensive band can make a heavily discounted watch cost more than a simpler version that meets your needs. Judge offers against previous selling prices as well as the advertised reduction: a large saving from the original launch price doesn’t necessarily mean exceptional value. Check any spending requirements, contracts, trade-ins, or rebates attached to offers advertising a “free” Apple Watch.
Finally, check whether you’re buying a new, refurbished, or used watch, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For a used or refurbished model, check the stated battery condition and confirm that it has been removed from the previous owner’s account, with Activation Lock turned off. Make sure the watch is compatible with your iPhone before ordering.






How we choose Apple Watch deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on Apple Watch reviews and everyday wear. We consider comfort, performance, battery life, charging, health and fitness features, and value – not just the specifications or advertised saving.
Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our Series 12 review assessed battery life and charging performance alongside its newer health features. We also draw on everyday experience: our cellular Apple Watch testing examines whether staying connected without an iPhone justified the extra hardware and subscription costs.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. We check the generation, case size, material, connectivity, and included band so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside discounted replacements.

title: Did Apple just save the iPhone Duo?
content:
Macworld





The tech industry is obsessed with change, but most customers feel much more ambivalent about the concept. The announcement of a tweak to Facebook’s algorithm or Netflix’s interface is rarely the cause of celebration: “Why did they change it?” is the motto of casual tech users across the planet. And when it comes to hardware, the world can be divided into a tiny minority of novelty seekers, and a vast majority who just want a product that does the same as the last generation in a new color and with fewer bugs.
The iPhone Duo is designed to appeal to the first demographic far more than the second, which is why it will struggle to achieve mainstream appeal. It is, by the standards of iPhones at any rate, remarkably different from its predecessors, and I don’t mean that as a compliment. It’s aggressively, confrontationally new, and the word that keeps occurring to me is “difficult.”
I’ve been using one as my primary device for a month. I’d never claim to be a fast learner, but by this point in the testing cycle I’m generally up to speed. (Switching from the Home button on the iPhone 8 to the upward swipe on the iPhone XS, for example, felt natural within days.) That isn’t the case with the Duo. The folding and unfolding process still doesn’t come naturally; I haven’t found a comfortable way to hold it when open and in landscape orientation; it’s more difficult to jump up to the top of webpages and to summon the Control Center; and my brain is yet to fully take on board the shift of many interface elements from the bottom or top to the side of the screen.
The onboarding speed bump that’s caused me the most annoyance, however, is Touch ID. This is surprising, because I would consider myself a fan of that technology. When Touch ID began its transition to Face ID way back in 2017, I was in the “Why did they change it?” crowd. Touch ID was reliable, and not noticeably slow. Face ID sometimes went wrong and was not appreciably more convenient. I recognized that the change allowed Apple to ditch the Home button and claw back more screen space, but facial recognition itself struck me then as a means to an end rather than a positive evolution of the user experience.

				
					

				
			Where’s the Touch ID sensor? It’s on the right. This time.

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry




However, my love of Touch ID is because the conventional iPhone design suits Touch ID. With other devices and in other contexts, it’s not quite as convenient. Such is the case with my 5th-gen iPad Air, which sits most of the time on a stand next to my MacBook with its power button awkwardly placed slightly behind the laptop. Any time I have to log in, I’m reminded of how much easier life would be if the iPad Air had Face ID, and I sometimes even look up prices of second-hand iPad Pros. Or the MacBook Pro itself, which has a raised-up stand of its own and therefore forces me to reach up to access its in-keyboard fingerprint sensor, evoking similar reservations to those I have about touchscreen laptops.
The iPhone Duo is the worst of all. It’s a nightmare for accessing the Touch ID sensor precisely because of its formal versatility. If it’s closed and in portrait orientation, or open and landscape, the sensor is two-thirds of the way up the right-hand edge (where no such sensor has ever previously been on an Apple product, as far as I’m aware), so realistically you have to use your right index finger. But it doesn’t feel natural, and certainly isn’t comfortable. When closed, you can just about reach behind the phone and use your left index fingertip, but the angle makes it very unreliable.
The opposite two modes, closed in landscape and open in portrait, put the sensor partway along the top edge. Both are inconvenient, but in subtly different ways. For closed/landscape, when you hold it a little like a game controller, the left index can reach up without moving the hand, although the angle is suboptimal. For open/portrait, your hands most likely sit at the lower end to avoid the camera module, so you have to reach upwards, and the right index is probably your best choice.
Now, I worry that the preceding two paragraphs may have strained the reader’s patience. But such is the experience of using Touch ID on the iPhone Duo: tedious and complicated. It’s essential to record at least two fingerprints (you may also want to include your right thumb for occasional use in open/landscape), and the methods of accessing the sensor vary so much from each other and from what’s come before that you have no hope of depending on, or building, muscle memory. Add in the fact that, unlike the Home button, the power button is not visible from the front of the device, and it becomes clear why Apple feels it necessary to add on-screen indicators to help you find the sensor.

				
					

				
			Setting up Unlock with Front Camera is easy, and well worth doing.
David Price / Foundry




My dissatisfaction with all this turned to delight, however, when Apple found a way to achieve the impossible and retrospectively add a hardware feature to an already released product. Well, sort of. The iPhone Duo is obviously not getting Face ID, because the necessary sensors are not there. But it’s getting the next best thing. As of the second beta of iOS 27.3, the Duo gets a new feature called Unlock with Front Camera that was borrowed from HomeView. I explain how to get this in a separate article, but I’ll tell you here: It’s a game-changer.
Facial unlock doesn’t have the same access privileges as Face ID, because it depends on sensors that aren’t as sophisticated and cannot offer the same level of security. Quite a lot of the time, including sensitive app unlocks, the Duo will insist that you use the more secure Touch ID instead (or enter your passcode). But many phone unlocks can now be performed by looking at the front camera, and a glance can also uncover details of previously hidden notifications. For removing a large number of small pain points, and for making a difficult device significantly less difficult, Apple deserves tremendous praise.

title: Apple Faces Korean Regulator Review Over iPhone 16 AI Advertising
content:
Apple is facing a formal probe in South Korea over allegations that its iPhone 16 advertising misled consumers about the availability of Apple Intelligence features.


Investigators at the country's Fair Trade Commission (FTC) have referred Apple and Apple Korea for review, alleging that several Apple Intelligence features were not delivered as advertised, including Genmoji, Image Playground, and Siri's ability to understand personal context and onscreen awareness.

The allegations focus on whether Apple adequately explained which features were available and when others would arrive. For example, the FTC's report notes that Siri's personal-context capabilities were advertised for Korean availability in early April 2025 but did not arrive until October 2026, approximately 18 months later.

Apple provided MacRumors with the following statement:
"At Apple, we deeply value the relationship with our customers in Korea and have always focused on delivering the best products and services in the world. Since we added Korean language support for Apple Intelligence last year, users have benefited from dozens of powerful features that are integrated across Apple's platforms. And we have continued to build on that commitment with the recent launch of Korean language support for Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that's more capable, conversational, and personal. We have cooperated with the KFTC's investigation and disagree with the conclusions in the Examiner's Report. We look forward to presenting a fulsome defense before the Commission."
The Commission has yet to issue a final ruling or impose a penalty.

removed its "available now" marketing claim on its Apple Intelligence page, following a National Advertising Division inquiry. The advertising watchdog found that the wording implied that all listed features were available, and that a footnote explaining the phased rollout was insufficiently clear. Apple disagreed with the findings but ultimately complied with the recommendation.

$250 million settlement in May 2026 over a U.S. class-action lawsuit alleging it misled buyers about the availability of Apple Intelligence and Siri features when the iPhone 16 was released in September 2024.

Original article updated with Apple's statement.

The monitor might be the second-most important part of your Mac’s setup after the Mac, of course–you can’t use any desktop computer without one and even the 16-inch screen on the MacBook Pro feels cramped if you are having a particularly productive morning. Spread your work out by plugging in multiple monitors to your Mac and extending your desktop over a wider space.
Because you’ll spend a lot of time looking at the display, you’ll want to invest wisely. Not only will you want a monitor that provides a pleasing experience, but the quality of the images on the screen can also affect your work.
However, picking a new monitor can be daunting. Not only are there many manufacturers to choose from, but there are also lots of sizes, resolutions, and features to consider—and when we say lots, we mean lots. We’re here to help guide you while you shop, and we have some tips on what to look for in a monitor plus advice on how many monitors each Mac can handle.
Best Mac monitors 2026
These are the best desktop Mac monitors we have tested. We round up the best portable displays for Mac separately if you want to take a larger display out on the road or easily store one out of sight when you’re not using it.
We’ve included Apple’s Pro Display XDR and the Apple Studio Display, not because they are necessarily the best choice, but for comparative purposes.

There are two screen options with this affordable 4K display: matte (MA270U) and glossy (MA270UP). If you want to banish glare and reflections more so than with the pricey Nano texture glass on the Apple Studio Display, got for Nano Matte.
Some displays sell the stand separately so there’s an additional cost consideration, but that’s not the case here as the stand is included. It offers a great range of adjustment: -5 to 20 degrees of tilt, swivels 15 degrees left or right, and 115 mm of height. The display can also pivot 90 degrees to Portrait mode, a far greater range of motion than the Studio Display. 
The MA270U/P can connect to a Mac through HDMI or USB-C. The USB-C connection offers 90 watts of power so it can charge your MacBook at the same time. If you want to use the display as a connection hub, you need to connect to the Mac via USB-C. Its built-in spare USB-C port offers 15W of power output and the USB-A 7.5W. There are two HDMI ports so you can connect to another device for multitasking.
The one thing that’s immediately noticeable with the MA270U/P is its impressive image quality. Colors are full of life and the detail is excellent. One standout aspect of the image quality is how sharp text appears. This is great for production and design work, but it can even make it more enjoyable to read and write.
It offers image quality that could satisfy users in a production environment–that’s one way of saying that its quality is better than what general users usually get. You might be able to find a 27-inch 4K display that’s a little cheaper, but it won’t look this good.–Roman Loyola
Read the full BenQ MA270UP Monitor review.
The 27-inch BenQ MA270U/P provides a very affordable alternative to Apple’s expensive 5K Studio Display. The BenQ 32-inch MA320U is slightly more expensive, but as well as providing a larger screen it produces a brighter display with bolder, crisper colors, although also at 4K. As a production display, the Studio Display is still expensive but looks affordable compared to the Apple Studio Display XDR. Buyers will enjoy its handsome design, good image quality, and impressive spatial audio, but you can save a lot of money by going with a non-Apple display.
Apple displays have always produced very good image quality, and the Studio Display continues that tradition. Colors are rich, contrast is good, and the brightness is suitable for most tasks.
The Studio Display has a tilt-adjustable stand, but it does not pivot between landscape and portrait modes—a WESA mount beings you a portrait option with the right monitor arm or stand. You can get a stand that provides about four inches of height adjustment but it doesn’t come cheap. The price tag for the tilt- and height-adjustable stand is a whopping $400/£400 more. That Apple stand on its own is about half the price of a comparable third-party 5K monitor with its own height-adjustable stand, such as the BenQ MA270S, reviewed below.
The Studio Display has six speakers (four force-canceling woofers, and two high-performance tweeters) that sound better than most displays we’ve used but are no match for a decent independent speaker.
There’s nothing wrong with this display. Brightness uniformity is good, and color accuracy is excellent. It’s just an old panel, with poor motion clarity from a slow pixel response and a complete lack of modern expected display properties. It’s 2026, and all but the very cheapest monitors have refresh rates over 60Hz, adaptive refresh, HDR, or all of the above.
For a monitor being sold new in 2026, the Studio Display looks like what a nice $999 5K display should. The XDR version has a mini-LED backlight array with up to 2304 dimming zones that can crank the brightness up to 1000 nits for SDR content and a peak of 2000 nits for HDR content. It supports resolutions up to 120Hz and variable refresh rates, too. (A note on 120Hz support: Macs with M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, M1 Ultra, M2, and M3 will only drive the display up to 60Hz. While both Studio Display models support P3 wide color, the XDR model adds a host of additional color reference modes, including P3 + Adobe RGB, and even DICOM medical imaging.
The webcam is Apple’s 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View. The image quality is vastly improved on previous Studio Displays. White balance, clarity, resolution, and smoothness are all so much better.
