title: Google Says Apple's iOS Browser Rules Offer 'Choice on Paper, Not in Practice'
content:
Google's Chrome for Developers team today supported Mozilla's complaint about Apple's rules on non-WebKit browser engines in the European Union, calling out restrictions that make launching an alternative engine too difficult.


Mozilla recently joined a coalition of up to 55,000 businesses and organizations to ask the European Commission to force Apple to change its browser rules. Apple started allowing alternative browser engines in the EU in early 2024, but the coalition says no browser maker has been able to transfer its EU users from Apple's WebKit engine to a new engine because of Apple's conditions.

Mozilla explained that using its Gecko browser engine instead of WebKit would require releasing a second Firefox app. Apple says apps with alternative browser engines have to be distributed only in the EU, so Mozilla has been unable to add Gecko to its existing app. Firefox users in the EU would need to transfer to a new app and move all their content, and many users might not be willing to switch. Mozilla said Apple's conditions are "unworkable" and that Apple has only complied with the EU's Digital Markets Act "on paper."

Chrome for Developers echoed the statement in its X post:
We agree with @mozilla. Nearly 3 years after alternative browser engines on iOS were EU-mandated, zero launched due to remaining Apple restrictions. Forcing browsers to ship separate apps and re-acquire users is choice on paper, not in practice.

Though one Google team expressed support for Mozilla, Google did not sign the open letter to the European Commission. In 2023, Google started work on an experimental version of Chromium for iOS with the Blink engine, but Google said it was only a prototype that would not be released.

participated in a DMA workshop where Mozilla brought up iOS support for third-party browser engines. According to Mozilla, Apple claimed Google and Mozilla have "everything they need" to ship an alternative browser engine in the EU and "have chosen not to do so." In its documentation for alternative browser engines, Apple says its requirements help keep users safe online.

is in talks with Apple over its browser engine restrictions. It is also consulting Mozilla and other signatories on how rival browsers can compete with Safari on Apple devices.

title: These gifts every Apple fan will love all cost less than AirPods 5
content:
Macworld






The holiday season is upon us, and picking the right gifts for our favorite people can be challenging. We want to skip the cliché socks this year, but spending a grand on a new iPhone or iPad isn’t in the cards, either. Luckily, Apple and other reputable brands sell a wide range of helpful gadgets that top out at $129. Even without breaking the bank, these practical picks are guaranteed to impress anyone on your list for months to come.



AirPods 5

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




The AirPods 5 are the benchmark for this list, so we had to include them. Despite maintaining the same $129 starting price as their predecessors, the entry-level AirPods 5 now come with ANC for the first time, essentially a $50 price cut over the AirPods 4. Beyond muffling external noise, the ANC technology unlocks Apple’s Live Translation feature, which lets users chat more naturally with locals when traveling internationally.
Other neat perks include support for immersive Spatial Audio content, water and dust resistance, Automatic Device Switching, and Siri AI commands. It’s a well-rounded pair of wireless earbuds that will seamlessly connect to all of their Apple devices, providing a comfortable listening experience.
Shopping tip: You can save some money if you shop for AirPods at Amazon and other retailers. It often sells the AirPods below the MSRP. AirPods 5 haven’t yet gone on sale, but be sure to check for any Black Friday deals.






MagSafe wallet

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani/Foundry




Ever since Apple baked MagSafe into the iPhone, magnetic wallets have boomed in popularity, especially among minimalists aiming to carry fewer separate items. The Apple FineWoven Wallet with MagSafe ($59 MSRP; $53 on Amazon) is one of the most stylish options, offering a slender design, several colors, native Find My support with detachment alerts, and room for up to three cards. While the FineWoven material doesn’t age as gracefully as its leather forefather, it does get the job done for a few years.
If you’re looking for something cheaper, larger, more versatile, or just generally different, you can check out the various MagSafe wallets listed on Amazon and pick a positively rated product. Before proceeding, ensure the recipient has a compatible iPhone model, as the Duo does not support standard-size wallets (including Apple’s official accessory), and some lower-end variants like the 16e miss out on MagSafe altogether.






AirTag with Key Ring

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani/Foundry




The AirTag 2 ($29.99 MSRP; $23 on Amazon) is one of the safest and most inexpensive gifts on this list, as iPhone users can never have enough of these reliable Bluetooth trackers. They could toss one in their backpack, purse, or luggage to pinpoint its exact location using the Find My app at all times. And with the second-gen model upgrading the speaker and detection range, the coin-sized tracker is louder and easier to find than ever before.
If you’re looking to spend a bit more on this gift, you could pair it with Apple’s AirTag FineWoven Key Ring ($35 MSRP; available on Amazon), helping the recipient attach it to keys and other items more easily.






Apple Pencil (USB-C)

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry





This one is for the valued creatives in your life. Whether they have an iPad with a USB-C port or an iPhone Duo, the USB-C Apple Pencil ($79 MSRP; $49 on Amazon) will supercharge their doodling and note-taking experience. The official stylus supports precise input and tilt sensitivity, making it more dependable for illustration and writing down everyday thoughts than using one’s finger.






Google Fitbit Air

				
					

				
			
Thomas Deehan / Foundry





While Apple Watches are deemed the best overall fitness trackers for casual iPhone users, the cheapest SE model starts at a whopping $249. Fortunately, the third-party alternatives are plentiful, and many of them cost way less. Google’s Fitbit Air ($99 MSRP; available on Amazon) is a screen-less activity tracker with a one-week battery life, offering personalized insights, heart rate measurements, workout recording, sleep tracking, and much more for a lot less money. Any iPhone user can set it up using the Google Health app on iOS and collect metrics similar to those provided by an Apple Watch. It’s the perfect gift for those planning to be more active in 2027.






Nanoleaf smart light strip

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani/Foundry





Christmas is right around the corner, and the Nanoleaf Essentials Matter Lightstrip ($70 MSRP; $45 on Amazon) is the ideal gift for that one friend who hasn’t yet finished setting up their decorations. The smart home product ties directly into Apple HomeKit, enabling native automations, remote control, Control Center access, and much more. It features hundreds of LEDs with separate color zones, letting users opt for a vibrant festive look. After the holidays, they can pair it to their desktop computer or TV to match on-screen hues and create an atmospheric experience or sync to playing music. We’ve linked to the model with 300 LEDs, but Nanoleaf has a variety of lights available.






Sony DualSense controller

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani/Foundry





Now that newer iPhones, iPads, Macs, and even Apple TVs pack ultrafast processors capable of running demanding software, game controllers have become widely sought-after gifts. Sony’s DualSense controller ($75 MSRP; $54 on Amazon) is arguably the best choice for Apple users, as it is natively supported by the operating systems. This unlocks advanced features, such as color customization, button remapping, profile creation, and more. And with support for multiple simultaneous connections, your friend could bring their controller over when visiting you to play local multiplayer games on a single Apple device.






Belkin 3-in-1 wireless charger

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary





Belkin’s $100 Wireless 3-in-1 Foldable Fast Charging Station ($100 MSRP; $77 on Amazon) is suitable for a friend who’s heavily invested in the Apple ecosystem. The charger can accommodate an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods case at the same time, which can help minimize cables and declutter their desk. Thanks to its flexible design, they could use it in pad or stand mode as needed.






Anker power bank

				
					

				
			
Dominik Tomaszewski / Foundry





For portable power, Anker’s Zolo Power Bank ($30 MSRP; $24.69 on Amazon) offers a 10,000mAh battery capacity and 30W fast charging support. It connects to iPhones, iPads, and MacBooks via USB-C, providing uninterrupted charging on the go for all of their Apple devices.






Apple Gift Card

				
					

				
			
Apple





If you’re unsure what exactly your friend needs, you can’t go wrong with an Apple Gift Card. You can set the value to as little as $15 or increase it depending on your budget. You can even customize its design, include a heartfelt message, and schedule it in advance. Amazon will then deliver it via text, email, or a physical package depending on your choice. Once redeemed, your friend will be able to spend the amount on apps, compatible digital purchases, and subscription services or it can be used toward a pricier purchase from the Apple Store.

title: Signal Now Blocks AI Screen Access to Protect Chats
content:
Signal is extending screenshot-blocking protections to iPhones and supported Android devices to prevent AI assistants such as Siri and Gemini from capturing private conversations.


In its announcement, Signal said AI assistants can capture messages displayed on screen, potentially exposing conversations to processing outside the app. End-to-end encryption protects message delivery, but cannot prevent another app from reading messages visible on a recipient's device.

iOS 27, the new "Block ‌Siri‌ AI" setting is enabled by default in Signal version 8.37 or later. It blocks screenshots, screen recordings, and AI screen-reading. On supported Android devices running Signal 8.35.1 or later, screen security activates when an AI assistant attempts to read the screen.

Settings → Privacy → Block Siri AI, either permanently or for 10 minutes to take a screenshot. Apple also offers an Excluded Apps setting under Settings → Siri that prevents ‌Siri‌ from accessing selected apps.

Is free antivirus for Mac good enough?
Free antivirus software can provide basic protection, but it often lacks advanced features such as ransomware protection, firewalls and real-time web security. Paid options offer more comprehensive, all-round protection.
Apple includes built-in security tools like XProtect and Gatekeeper, which block known malware and unverified apps. However, in our testing, it was still possible to install Mac malware or suspicious software if warnings were ignored, showing that Apple’s protections alone are not foolproof.
Free third-party antivirus tools offer an advantage in that they are updated more frequently and can protect against a wider range of threats, including adware, spyware, trojans and ransomware.
The core antivirus engine is often the same in both free and paid versions. The difference lies in the extra features included in premium suites, such as web and phishing protection, VPNs, identity monitoring, parental controls and customer support.
Ultimately, you get what you pay for. If security is a priority, a paid antivirus offers the most complete protection. However, if you’re on a tight budget, a free antivirus is still better than relying solely on Apple’s built-in security tools.

 Best Mac Antivirus: FAQ 


1.
Do Macs need antivirus software?
Yes – while Macs are generally more secure than Windows PCs and include built-in protections like XProtect and sandboxing, which helps limit how far malware can spread, these measures are not enough to defend against modern threats such as phishing, adware and ransomware. 
Adding a dedicated antivirus tool helps close those gaps, provides broader coverage against evolving threats and extra layer of security when browsing the web or downloading files.
For more detail, see our guide to whether Macs need antivirus, along with our Mac security tips and advice on how to remove a virus from a Mac.
Do iPhones need antivirus software? 
You may be considering a Mac Antivirus that also offers to protect your iPhone, but is that protection really necessary? 
Apple’s iOS is designed with strong built-in security, including app sandboxing, strict App Store review processes and system-level protections that prevent traditional viruses from infecting your device. This makes it very difficult for malware to spread in the same way it can on other platforms. So, no – iPhones generally don’t need antivirus software.
However, iPhones are not completely risk-free. Threats like phishing attacks, malicious websites and data breaches can still affect users. Instead of installing an antivirus app the best advice is to keep iOS up to date, avoid clicking on suspicious links, use strong passwords and two-factor authentication, and don’t download anything unless you are sure it is safe. 





2.
How does antivirus software protect your Mac?
Mac antivirus software protects your device using a combination of on-demand scans and real-time (always-on) protection.
On-demand scanning checks files when you run a manual or scheduled scan. This can take time, especially on systems with lots of data, and may temporarily use more system resources. For best results, scans are often scheduled to run at convenient times. See how to scan a Mac for malware
Real-time protection works continuously in the background. If malware arrives – for example via an email attachment or downloaded file – the antivirus can detect and block it immediately. Suspicious files are typically quarantined, meaning they are moved to a secure location where they can’t cause harm while you decide whether to delete or restore them.
The effectiveness of these two layers of protection is the most important factor when choosing antivirus software, but additional features can also make a difference.
Many Mac antivirus tools now include ransomware protection, which prevents unauthorised apps from accessing sensitive folders such as Documents or Photos. Only trusted apps are allowed access, and you can customise these permissions.
Web protection is another key feature, often delivered via browser extensions. This helps block malicious websites, phishing attempts and unsafe downloads, reducing the risk of accidentally exposing personal information.





3.
Should my Mac antivirus include a VPN?
Yes, a VPN can be a useful addition to Mac antivirus software. It encrypts your internet connection, helping protect your data – especially on public Wi-Fi. However, built-in VPNs are often limited, so a dedicated VPN service usually offers better performance and features.
Some Mac antivirus packages include a built-in VPN (virtual private network), although VPNs are also widely available as standalone products. For many users, VPNs are appealing because they can mask your location and allow access to region-restricted content, such as streaming services.
More importantly, a VPN improves security by encrypting your internet connection, which is particularly useful when using public Wi-Fi networks. This helps protect your data from interception and reduces the risk of cyberattacks.
While we generally recommend a dedicated Mac VPN service for the best performance and features, a VPN included with antivirus software can still be a useful extra. Just be aware that bundled VPNs often come with limitations, such as data caps or reduced functionality, and may prompt you to upgrade to a full subscription.





4.
What is the best value Mac antivirus?
Value means different things to different users. For some, it’s the best free option; for others, it’s a reasonably priced product with the most useful features. We define value as the best overall balance of protection, performance and features – and for protecting a single Mac, we believe Intego offers the best value.
That said, there are ways to save money on even the top antivirus products. Most Mac antivirus apps are sold as annual subscriptions, often with significant discounts for the first year. When that period ends, you can switch providers to take advantage of new introductory offers, or opt for longer-term plans (such as two- or three-year subscriptions) to reduce the overall cost.
Many antivirus suites also cover multiple devices, including Windows PCs and Android smartphones. If you have several devices in your household, a multi-device plan can offer excellent value.

5.
How to spot fake Mac antivirus software?
Because many of us are waking up to the idea that malware is a threat to the Mac, malware writers have made it their business to play on that fear. There have been cases of malware writers disguising their viruses as antivirus apps – two notable examples are Mac Auto Fixer and MacDefender. It’s important to always read reviews on reputable sites such as Macworld before installing any software on your Mac or MacBook.
At the same time, don’t believe everything you read. MacKeeper is a great example of an antivirus program that has got a bad rap, but it’s worked hard to repair its reputation. It has gained Apple Notarization, which means the software has been checked by Apple for malicious components, and the company has garnering certification from various bodies to prove it isn’t a PUP (potentially unwanted program), including an AV-Test certificate. That said, we haven’t recommended it here, and that’s simply because we feel that there are better options available. If you have already installed MacKeeper and wish to try one of our alternative recommendations, we explain How to uninstall MacKeeper.





6.
What can’t Mac antivirus protect you from?
Using a Mac antivirus product, especially one that includes tools to improve your online privacy, may lull you into believing you’re completely safe from personal and private information leaking out and that you no longer need to keep your wits about you. That’s not quite the case. While there’s no reason to panic, you should still practice caution – and there are a few more issues you should consider when using Mac antivirus, too.
First, an antivirus for Mac product may upload the complete text of files flagged to the cloud, where it can be analyzed by separate tools hosted there. This practice is normal and sensible: some malware can detect when a running process may examine it, and will then engage in subterfuge. Antivirus software makers also can access their massive databases to examine files with characteristics that trigger their algorithms – certain elements that match known malware. As a result, security researchers discover new viruses, worms, Trojans horses, and the like. However, helping the greater good means you’ll have to be comfortable with trusting a third-party with your file contents. Where appropriate, we noted privacy policy issues in individual reviews.
Second, this software may also rely partly or entirely on cloud-based checks of URLs, malware, and the like. Accordingly, an antivirus package might upload every URL you visit, metadata about files, signatures of files, information about your computer’s hardware, a list of running or installed applications, and more. Companies vary on their disclosure of such policies, and may not let you opt out of this kind of sharing. We note issues in each review as appropriate.
Third, antivirus software makers also get a sense of what behavior is happening on your computer that’s being monitored or blocked, and may use that information for their own purposes. In some cases, you can opt out of this information gathering.





7.
What virus cleaner does Apple recommend?
Apple has never recommended a third-party virus cleaner, and has instead focused on the Xprotect and Gatekeeper functions found within macOS, which are regularly updated with operating system updates.





8.
How good is Apple’s virus protection?
It’s actually very good, and there isn’t much that gets past it in the way of viruses and malware, given its Xprotect and Gatekeeper features – but these can be overridden, and questionable software can be installed and activated if the user knows what they’re doing.
Still, the protection is present, it’s updated well, and Apple keeps a good eye on things, but new viruses and malware are sent out from bad actors all the time, and this is where a good third-party application can come in handy.
We have tested Apple’s own solution against a range of malware samples. While it did a reasonable job overall, we found instances where questionable applications could be installed without any warning. A helpful analogy is to think of Apple’s built-in antivirus system, XProtect, as the lock on your Mac’s front door, while a paid antivirus solution acts more like an alarm system with security cameras. Third-party tools update their virus definitions – including not just viruses, but also adware, spyware, trojans, and ransomware – several times a day, often more frequently than Apple’s protections, providing real-time defense against new and emerging threats.
During our testing of Apple’s malware protections, recovery options were limited. In some cases, the only solution was to wipe the Mac and restore from a backup made before the risky behavior – hoping nothing had already spread. Apple does not offer dedicated malware removal support or guarantees if an infection occurs, nor does it protect against cross-platform threats across multiple devices. Paid antivirus software typically includes these services, along with additional features such as web and phishing protection, vulnerability patching tools, VPNs, password managers, parental controls, secure cloud backup, and dark web monitoring.
That said, macOS’s built-in security may be sufficient for low-risk users who install apps only from the App Store or trusted developers, keep automatic updates enabled, avoid pirated software, do not disable Gatekeeper, have limited exposure to risky email attachments, and do not handle sensitive client data.
Ultimately, investing in a reputable security suite for Mac adds an extra layer of protection – and for many users, it’s a case of being safe rather than sorry.





9.
Is there free virus protection for Mac?
The Xprotect and Gatekeeper functions serve as free virus protection for macOS, but you can also get basic virus protection from many of the well-known antivirus providers, we have some recommendations above. 





10.
How to choose the best Mac antivirus for your needs
There are a lot of Mac antivirus programs to choose from. What you want is one that offers a familiar and easy-to-use interface that works well on a Mac – a key reason why we recommend Intego’s antivirus. You should also look for antivirus with a good detection rate – not just for Mac viruses, but also for PC viruses, unless you want to be passing viruses on to friends and clients running Windows. Low impact on system resources is also critical, especially if your Mac isn’t the most powerful model.
Consider the type and number of devices you want to protect – are you looking for an app to cover one Mac, or Mac, iPhone, iPad and even a PC? Your budget matters here, too: do you prefer a subscription model or a one-time payment?
Mac antivirus vendors typically offer different add-ons, and it is certainly a case of you get what you pay for: free products will have fewer bells and whistles, but the most comprehensive Mac security suites will include password managers, parental controls, cloud storage and more. The underlying antimalware engine will usually be the same for all security products from a particular company, so you can save money if you don’t need all those extra features.





11.
When are Apple’s built-in protections sufficient
For many users, Apple’s layered security – XProtect, Gatekeeper and Rapid Security Responses – is more than adequate. If you fit into the “low-risk” category described below, you can probably rely on macOS alone.
You only download apps from the Mac App Store or trusted developers. Gatekeeper ensures that only notarized software from identified developers can run, and XProtect scans these apps for known malware on launch.
You keep automatic updates enabled. Apple regularly updates XProtect’s malware definitions in the background, and with macOS Tahoe, Background Security Improvements can now install critical patches silently without requiring a restart.
You avoid pirated software, torrents, and “cracks.” These are common vectors for malware that can bypass Apple’s checks if a user overrides warnings. 
You do not handle sensitive client data or work in a high-risk environment. For casual home use, the built-in tools are generally enough to block the most obvious threats





12.
When paid Antivirus is worthwhile
Despite Apple’s strong foundation, there are clear gaps that third-party software fills.
You frequently install software from various internet sources. In our hands-on testing, we have found that it is still possible to install malware by ignoring or bypassing Gatekeeper warnings. Our testers were able to install trojans, fake apps, and software that requested access to the microphone, webcam, and keystrokes.
You want protection against phishing and malicious websites. Apple’s XProtect primarily focuses on known malware files. It does not offer the same level of real-time web and phishing protection that suites like Avast One or Bitdefender provide.
You need more frequent updates and broader threat coverage. Third-party tools update their virus definitions several times a day, often more frequently than Apple’s updates. They also cover a wider range of threats, including adware, spyware, trojans, and ransomware.
You want features like a firewall, VPN, password manager, or identity monitoring. Apple does not offer a dedicated, configurable firewall for macOS (it relies on the built-in one) and does not include a VPN, password manager, or dark web monitoring in its security suite. Paid suites bundle these features.
You share files with Windows users. An unprotected Mac can unknowingly harbor Windows viruses that won’t affect macOS but can be passed on to friends and colleagues. A good antivirus will detect and clean cross-platform threats.

title: Things 3.25 for Mac Gains Touch Gestures
content:
Cultured Code today released Things 3.25 for Mac, bringing full optimization for the PROLED MacBook Pro to its task management app.


Since the touchscreen MacBook Pro launched, all Mac apps feature basic touch input, with taps performing the equivalent of mouse clicks. Things already worked with that default behavior, but Cultured Code says version 3.25 fully optimizes the app for touch with additional gestures, improved dragging, and larger controls.

A rightward swipe on a to-do opens the scheduling dialog, while a leftward swipe selects or deselects it. Users can also select several items by moving two fingers up or down through a list. To open a to-do, users can tap it to select it and tap again to expand it, or double-tap.

Cultured Code says dragging to-dos and headings is smoother and more responsive, whether moving one item or a group. Holding a finger on an item in a selection picks up the whole group, rather than only that item. The update also improves how dragging works when some selected items are outside the visible area of the list.



Custom menus and date pickers adapt to the input method, showing more spacious rows and larger touch targets when opened with a finger. Buttons elsewhere in the app also have larger tap targets.

Other changes make it easier to resize the sidebar by touch and rearrange checklist entries within a to-do. Users can cancel either a to-do or an individual checklist entry by pressing and holding its checkbox. The release also includes smaller adjustments to touch interactions and interface polish throughout the app.

title: Apple might make the iPhone 18e’s camera bump much bigger
content:
Macworld





For as long as Apple has been making budget iPhones, they’ve had single cameras. And for as long as iPhones have had single cameras, they’ve been positioned all alone in the top left corner.
According to a new report by Filipe Esposito at Engadget, however, that’s going to change with the upcoming iPhone 18e. Apple is reportedly going to add a small squarish camera array to house the iPhone 18e’s camera components.
Apple uses square arrays on products that have more than one visible sensor. For example, the iPad Pro, while having just a single 12MP wide-angle camera, has a square array to house the camera, flash, ambient light sensor, microphone, and LiDAR scanner. By contrast, the iPad Air has the same 12MP camera as the iPad Pro, but without an array. Instead, it has a single camera and microphone in the top right corner.
The iPhone 17e has a similar setup to the Air and the previous “e” and “SE” phones that came before it. The rear design is stark, with a single camera lens, microphone, and flash at the top right.
Assuming this is the direction Apple has chosen, it’s not clear what this change will add to the phone. For one, the array will appear rather empty with just a single camera. For another, the look won’t match any of the current iPhones, and it will upset the otherwise clean look of the iPhone 18e. In fact, it could make the 18e appear somewhat outdated, since Apple hasn’t used a square array on an iPhone since the iPhone 15. 
The iPhone 18e is expected to arrive in March alongside the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2.

title: EU in Talks With Apple Over Barriers to Rival iPhone Browsers
content:
The European Commission is in talks with Apple over rules that developers say stop them from offering browsers powered by their own technology on the iPhone.


The discussions follow an open letter published yesterday by Mozilla, Shopify, and a coalition representing up to 55,000 EU businesses and organizations. They argue that Apple has technically opened the door to competing browser technology, but made it too difficult to use in practice.

The dispute concerns what happens beneath a browser's interface. Firefox on the iPhone looks different from Safari, but both use Apple's WebKit engine to display websites. Mozilla wants to use its own engine, Gecko, which powers Firefox on the Mac and would let it bring additional Firefox features to the iPhone.

began allowing alternative engines in the EU with iOS 17.4. Mozilla argues Apple's conditions mean it cannot simply switch existing Firefox users to Gecko via an app update. It would need to release a second Firefox app, then persuade users to download it and manually move their bookmarks, passwords, and browsing history.

The coalition says no browser maker has managed to move its existing EU users from WebKit to its own engine more than two and a half years after Apple's deadline to comply with the Digital Markets Act (DMA). It wants the European Commission to open formal proceedings and force Apple to remove the alleged barriers.

POLITICO's Fair Play newsletter that it is "currently in dialogue with Apple." The Commission is also consulting the signatories about how rival browsers can compete with Safari on Apple devices. It described browser competition as a DMA priority because browsers determine how people access the web and how publishers reach their readers.

requirements for competing engines protect users from malicious websites and other security threats. Developers seeking approval must meet privacy and security standards and commit to fixing vulnerabilities promptly.

Every retailer that sells Apple gear gets in on the fun, and we’ll be checking and updating these prices all month, so mark this page and return often so you don’t miss a good deal, some of which are short-lived. Apple runs its own Black Friday shopping event. This year Apple’s confirmed Black Friday promotion runs November 27–30, with gift cards worth up to $300 in the U.S. or £240 in the U.K. available with eligible purchases.
Black Friday has become a month-long event, and we’re already seeing some of the lowest prices of 2026. Whatever Apple device you’re looking for, we’ll help you find a great deal. Browse the latest offers across Apple’s range below.

What you need to know…

The AirPods Max 2 are a minor upgrade over the original model, with an H2 chip to bring better noise cancellation and long-time AirPods Pro features, including Live Translation and Adaptive Audio. They still cost $549, but we’ve previously seen them drop as low as $399. So be on the lookout for a Black Friday sale that pushes them under $400.
AirPods 5, on the other hand, already got a significant price cut compared to the AirPods 4. Where Apple previously charged $129 for standard and $179 for ANC, the AirPods 5 have noise cancellation for $129, essentially a $50 price cut. There’s also a model with a wireless charging case and on-device gesture controls for $149. 
Rounding out the lineup is the AirPods Pro 3, which launched in September 2025 with a slightly new design, foam-infused eartips, and a heart-rate sensor. They were steadily updated with new features and are still excellent earbuds. They are regularly on sale at Amazon and other retailers for $199, and we’ve previously seen the price drop to $169.

If you don’t want the better display, we expect the older M5 Pro and M5 Max models to see significant savings over the Black Friday weekend.

Compare its price with the newer model with the same screen size, memory, and storage. If the difference is small, consider whether the newer model’s improvements justify the extra cost. An older model with more memory or storage may be more useful to you than a newer model at a similar price.
Even with an M5 chip, the MacBook Air is still an excellent laptop for just about everyone. Amazon already dropped prices by $200-$250 in early November, which is the lowest we’ve seen since prices went up in June. On top of that, all iPads got price hikes of $100-$200 in June, so you can expect to pay more than you would have last year for the same tablet, even on sale.
The lone exception is the iPad mini. In October, it got a massive overhaul with an 8.5-inch OLED display, thinner design, landscape FaceTime camera, IP67 water resistance, and an A20 Pro processor. At Macworld we’ve been covering and reviewing Apple and Apple devices for more than 40 years, from the original Macintosh to the most recent M6 MacBook Pro and iPhone 18 Pro. With a working knowledge of everything Apple sells and decades of experience, we know when stores are inflating MSRPs or pushing “normal” sales as limited Black Friday deals. Rest assured, the listings you see here will only be for the best discounts we can find on that particular item.

title: iOS 27 breaks 15 years of muscle memory on iPhone and iPad
content:
Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.
Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.
iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

PRICES CHECKED 24 NOVEMBER 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
Black Friday is a great time to buy an iPad, with discounts spanning affordable everyday tablets, powerful Pro models, and clearance stock from previous generations. This year’s standout Black Friday iPad deal so far is on Apple’s newest tablet. Amazon has listed the 128GB iPad mini (A20 Pro) for $599 in the U.S., $100 off. 
For most people, we’d recommend the 11-inch M4 iPad Air. Amazon has listed the 128GB Wi-Fi model for $649 in the U.S. and £669 in the U.K., saving $100 and £80, respectively. If you mainly want an iPad for browsing, streaming, or schoolwork, the 128GB A16 iPad at $379 is the cheaper U.S. option. It’s $20 below its October Prime Day price, although it still costs $30 more than it did before Apple raised prices in June. 
The biggest savings are on configurations with more storage. Amazon has listed the 11-inch M5 iPad Pro with 1TB for $1,499 in the U.S., and the 512GB version for £1,199 in the U.K., saving about $300 and £200, respectively. Those are worth a look if you need the extra space. If you don’t, a lower-capacity model may still cost less. See our best Apple Black Friday deals for more.
From November 27 to 30, Apple will include a $100/£80 Apple Gift Card when you buy an 11-inch or 13-inch M4 iPad Air directly from Apple, or a $125/£100 Apple Gift Card with an 11-inch or 13-inch M5 iPad Pro. The standard A16 iPad and iPad mini are excluded. Apple is also offering a $25/£20 gift card with eligible purchases of the Apple Pencil Pro or a Magic Keyboard for the iPad Air or iPad Pro. The gift card is for a future purchase. See our full guide to Apple’s Black Friday.
Which iPad should you buy this Black Friday?


M4 iPad Air – Our best all-round choice

				
					

				
			
Apple Inc




The iPad Air offers a strong balance of performance, screen size, and price without the premium cost of the Pro. The 11-inch model suits buyers who prioritize portability, while the 13-inch version gives you more room for multitasking and creative work.
A good Black Friday discount could make either size an attractive purchase. Compare storage capacities carefully, though: a larger advertised saving on a high-capacity model isn’t necessarily better value if you don’t need the extra space. 
U.S. Black Friday price: At Amazon, you can already get a saving of $100 off some iPad Air models, although in some cases these are selling out, in which case we are seeing Best Buy match the $100 off.  
U.K. Black Friday price: Amazon has either £80 or £90 off most configurations of iPad Air. For example, you can get the 11-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB for £669, down from the usual £749. These are reasonable savings, although we saw better discounts during October Prime Day, with up to £144 off. Last Black Friday, selected M3 Air configurations received £100 discounts.
Apple’s deal: You can get a $100/£80 Apple Gift Card when you buy an 11-inch or 13-inch M4 iPad Air from Apple, which is similar to the Amazon U.K. deal. 






iPad Pro – Best for demanding creative work

				
					

				
			
Apple Inc




The iPad Pro is the option for buyers who need Apple’s highest-end tablet performance and premium display. It comes in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes, but its capabilities – and price – will exceed what many people need for browsing, streaming, and everyday apps.
We’d look for a substantial saving rather than buy simply because it’s the most powerful iPad. Compare discounted M4 iPad Pro models, too: an older Pro could offer better value if its price is sufficiently below the equivalent M5 configuration. 
U.S. Black Friday price:  During October Prime Day, the 11-inch M5 iPad Pro with 256GB was $1,099, saving $100. So far we’re seeing nearly $300 off a 1TB 11-inch iPad Pro.
U.K. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought little to recommend on the M5 iPad Pro, with reductions of around £12. Last Black Friday, older M4 iPad Pro offers included a saving of approximately £206 at Amazon. Amazon has the 11-inch M5 iPad Pro with 512GB for £1,199 (£200 off). That matches its pre-June RRP and is £100 above its previous low of £1,099.
Apple’s deal: You can get a $125/£100 Apple Gift Card with an 11-inch or 13-inch M5 iPad Pro.






iPad (A16) – Our budget choice, at the right price

				
					

				
			
Apple




The A16 iPad remains a capable option for browsing, streaming, schoolwork, and everyday use. However, Apple raised its starting price by $100/£100 in June, and it doesn’t support Apple Intelligence.
That makes the final purchase price particularly important. A modest discount from today’s higher asking price may still leave you paying more than this iPad previously cost. With a replacement expected early in 2027, we’d look for a substantial Black Friday saving and compare the price with discounted iPad Air models before buying.
U.S. Black Friday price: This Black Friday we are seeing $70 off the 128GB iPad. The current $379 price is lower than October’s $399 price. We don’t expect it to go any lower.
U.K. Black Friday price: October coverage listed the 256GB model at £499.97, around £29 off. Last Black Friday, the 128GB version was £299 and the 256GB version was £399. We hope to see even lower prices this year, but so far Amazon has the 128GB model for £399 and the 256GB model for £499, both £30 off. 






iPad mini with A20 Pro – Best for portability

				
					

				
			
Apple




The new iPad mini went on sale on November 6, replacing the A17 Pro model. It brings an 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, and a thinner, lighter design, making it the option to consider if you want a compact iPad with the latest hardware.
Because it has only just arrived, we’d expect initial discounts to be smaller than clearance savings on its predecessor. The older A17 Pro mini could still be worthwhile at a sufficiently low price, but compare the saving with what you give up – particularly the new display.
U.S. Black Friday price: The A20 Pro mini wasn’t available during October Prime Day or last Black Friday. Amazon has it for $599, $100 off and the best price we’ve seen so far. Its 128GB A17 Pro predecessor was $499 during October Prime Day and $399 last Black Friday. You might be able to get a good deal on that 128GB A17 Pro iPad mini, which was $449 earlier in November, but it is now back at $499 at Amazon. 
U.K. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought only a small saving on the A17 Pro mini. The 128GB version reached £399 earlier this year, though – before Apple pushed up prices. You can still get the A17 Pro iPad mini for £100 less than the new model, but we hope to see bigger savings as Black Friday approaches.

Should you buy an iPad now or wait for a better deal?

				
					

				
			
There’s an iPad for everyone.

Foundry




With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need an iPad immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so an early offer can be worth taking if the price is competitive. Compare the exact generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity rather than waiting for Black Friday simply because a larger discount might appear.
If you’re buying an iPad Air and already plan to buy an Apple Pencil or keyboard later, Apple’s gift card may be worth waiting for. For the iPad Pro, check retailer prices first. The 11-inch M5 iPad Pro with 1TB has been listed at $299.01 off in the U.S. and £150 off in the U.K. at Amazon, both bigger savings than the Apple Gift Card.
Previous selling prices are particularly important this year because Apple raised iPad prices in June. During October Prime Day, the 128GB A16 iPad was $399, while the 11-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB was $649. Both were discounted against Apple’s increased prices, but cost more than their regular prices before June. A saving from today’s asking price doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting an exceptional bargain.
For the M4 iPad Air and M5 iPad Pro, we’d focus on finding a good price: We don’t expect replacements until 2027, as explained in our guide to the best time to buy an iPad. We’d be more cautious about the A16 iPad, which lacks Apple Intelligence and is expected to be replaced. Unless you find a substantial saving, waiting could get you a more capable entry-level model.
The new A20 Pro iPad mini presents a different decision. It has only just arrived, so we’d expect smaller initial discounts rather than immediate clearance-level savings. If you want its OLED display and newer processor, a modest reduction may still be worthwhile. If price matters more, compare remaining A17 Pro stock – but make sure the saving justifies choosing the older hardware.






Should you buy an older iPad? 

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older iPad can be a good buy if its price reflects its age and the features you give up. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of its replacement, matching screen size, storage, and connectivity where possible. A large saving from an old launch price doesn’t necessarily make it better value.
The M3 iPad Air and M4 iPad Pro are worth considering at substantial clearance discounts. Both remain capable options, and you may get more benefit from a lower price or additional storage than from the latest processor. However, if the newer equivalent costs only slightly more, the saving may not justify choosing the older generation.
The A17 Pro iPad mini also deserves consideration now that the A20 Pro model has arrived. It supports Apple Intelligence and remains a capable compact tablet, but you miss the newer model’s OLED display, faster processor, and thinner, lighter design. We’d want a meaningful saving rather than a small reduction from its former asking price.
Be more cautious with much older models. Check whether they support the current version of iPadOS and the apps and features you need. Compatibility today doesn’t guarantee how many future software upgrades they’ll receive. Apple Intelligence support also varies: don’t assume every older Air, Pro, or mini includes it.
If you already own an Apple Pencil or keyboard, check compatibility before changing generations. Keeping compatible accessories could make an older iPad better value, while replacing them could erase part of your saving. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges.






iPad deals to avoid
Check the exact configuration before comparing offers. Retailer listings can emphasize iPad, Air, or Pro without making the generation obvious. Confirm the chip, screen size, storage capacity, and whether you’re buying Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi + Cellular. A cheaper listing may be a different model rather than a better deal.
Don’t let a large advertised discount tempt you into paying for storage or connectivity you won’t use. A heavily reduced high-capacity or cellular iPad can still cost more than a simpler configuration that meets your needs. Compare the final purchase prices, rather than assuming the biggest saving represents the best value.
Check whether the price includes nano-texture glass, too. This optional finish (on the 1TB and 2TB M5 iPad Pro and the 256GB and 512GB A20 Pro iPad mini) reduces glare and makes fingerprints and oily smudges less noticeable, which can be useful if reflections make your iPad difficult to see in bright rooms or outdoors. It avoids much of the washed-out appearance associated with ordinary matte finishes, but contrast can drop at some viewing angles and the surface may be more scratch-sensitive. Availability depends on the model and storage configuration, so you could end up paying for both the finish and additional storage. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may be better value. Read our guide to nano-texture glass and whether you need it.
Our iPad buying guide considers cellular a luxury for most buyers. If you mainly use your iPad somewhere with Wi-Fi, you may get little benefit from the extra hardware. For occasional use elsewhere, sharing your iPhone’s connection through Personal Hotspot can be a more economical option.
Cellular makes more sense if you regularly need an independent connection while commuting or traveling; it also adds built-in GPS for accurate location tracking. Factor in any data-plan charges and compare the total cost of a contract with buying outright. A cellular model can still be worthwhile if its sale price matches or beats the equivalent Wi-Fi version—you don’t have to activate a data plan simply because the hardware is included.
Judge savings against previous selling prices as well as Apple’s current price. Following June’s price increases, a discounted iPad may still cost more than it did earlier in the year. Also distinguish a cash discount from a gift-card offer: a gift card doesn’t reduce the amount you pay for the iPad and is useful only if you’ll spend it.
Check what any bundle includes. A keyboard, case, or stylus doesn’t automatically make an offer better value, particularly if the accessories aren’t the versions you want. Read the conditions attached to “free” iPads, trade-in promotions, contracts, and rebates before comparing their total cost with buying outright.
Finally, check whether the iPad is new, refurbished, or used, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For used or refurbished models, look for information about battery condition and confirm that Activation Lock has been removed. Be cautious about devices that remain tied to a previous owner or an organization’s management system.






How we choose iPad deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on iPad reviews and everyday use. We consider performance, display quality, portability, battery life, and accessory support alongside price to explain which iPads suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess whether paying more brings practical benefits. A faster processor or premium display may matter for demanding creative work, while a less expensive iPad can be perfectly capable of browsing, streaming, and schoolwork. We also consider the cost of keyboards, Apple Pencils, and other accessories when judging an iPad’s value.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than relying solely on savings against today’s recommended price.
Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside newer alternatives. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges, while our purchase-timing guide helps you decide whether to buy now or wait.
For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our roundups of the best Mac deals, AirPods deals, and Apple Watch deals.

title: Apple solved one of the iPhone Duo’s biggest issues. Here’s how to set it up
content:
Macworld





The iPhone Duo is an impressive device in many ways, but its distinctive folding design comes with a number of compromises. Among these is the loss of the Face ID sensors we’ve all grown used to on recent iPhone models, replaced by the older and mildly less convenient Touch ID fingerprint sensor.
The good news is that, while Face ID itself cannot be added to the phone retroactively, Apple has just used a software update to give it the next best thing: facial unlocking. This means that, instead of always having to put your finger on the power button to open the phone, see a notification, and so on, you can just look at the screen. Here’s how to get this feature on your iPhone Duo.
Update your iPhone to the correct version of iOS
First, you’ll need to make sure you’ve got iOS 27.3 or later. This will immediately exclude some readers, I’m sorry to say, because at the time of writing that version of iOS is only available as a beta, and many iPhone users (quite reasonably) prefer to only use publicly released software. The good news is that iOS 27.3 should officially roll out soon, probably in late November or early December. In fact, it may have arrived by the time you read this article: open Settings and go to General > Software Update to see if it’s available.
Until then, here’s how to get a beta version of iOS on your iPhone. Please be aware that beta software is unfinished and may contain significant bugs.
Note that if you’re using a beta of iOS 27.3, it needs to be the second beta or later. That’s when the feature was added.
Turn on the facial unlock feature
Now that you’ve got iOS 27.3 (or later), we simply need to turn on the facial unlock feature.
Open the Settings app and tap Touch ID & Passcode. (You’ll need to scroll down a bit; it’s in the fourth bank of options.) Enter your passcode for access to this group of settings.

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Scroll down again, and you’ll see a new toggle labelled Unlock with Front Camera. It should currently be grey and white to show it’s turned off. Tap this so it turns green, and then it immediately kicks you into a new setup screen. Tap Get Started, then Continue.
The process is similar to the one for setting up Face ID, only slightly quicker and easier. (I assume this is because the feature has lower security access than full Face ID, so it doesn’t need to be quite as rigorous.) Point the front-facing camera at your face, then look in various directions as directed. It only takes a few seconds.

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




And that’s it! The feature is set up, and you can now unlock your iPhone Duo using only your face.
How to unlock using your iPhone Duo’s front camera
I mentioned that the Unlock with Front Camera feature has lower access than Face ID. What I mean is that in many situations, particularly ones where security is a priority, facial unlocking won’t be possible, and the Duo will direct you to use Touch ID or your passcode instead. This includes Apple Pay and password management.
With that limitation in mind, however, the feature is as easy to use as it was to set up. Let’s say you just received a notification, but because the Duo is locked, you can’t see the details. Simply look directly at the phone, and the notification will unlock and disgorge its secrets. Similarly, you just need to have the phone’s front camera pointed at your face when you swipe up from the bottom of the screen, and it will unlock without any fingerprint identification being needed.
One of the inconveniences of owning an iPhone Duo was just solved. You’re welcome.

Black Friday is a great time to buy an Apple Watch, with retailers discounting everything from the affordable SE to the premium Ultra. Apple Watch deals this Black Friday are already beating some of October Prime Day’s best prices. Amazon has listed the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 for $299 in the U.S. and £329 in the U.K., saving $100 and £40, respectively. In the U.S., the 40mm Apple Watch SE 3 is our budget pick at $179.
The standout U.K. deal is the Apple Watch Ultra 3 at £495. That’s £224 less than the discounted Ultra 4 at £719. Below, we compare the latest prices with previous lows and explain when an older model is worth choosing. For example, the 42mm Series 11 at £269 saves £60 compared with the Series 12 deal above. That’s worth considering if you don’t need the newer health features. For savings on Macs, iPads, AirPods, and more, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.

Which Apple Watch should you buy this Black Friday?


Apple Watch Series 12 – Our best overall choice

				
					

				
			

Apple




The Series 12 is the Apple Watch we recommend for most people. It combines Apple’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate measurements, a Readiness score, and a tougher display with up to 24 hours of battery life.
A worthwhile Black Friday discount could make it an attractive purchase, but compare it with remaining Series 11 stock. The older model has the same quoted battery life, so a substantial saving may outweigh the newer health features.
U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has discounted the 42mm GPS Series 12 to $299, saving $100 and the best price we’ve ever seen. The 46mm version is also $100 off.
U.K. Black Friday price: Amazon has £40 off the new Apple Watch Series 12, both sizes. 
Apple’s deal: Apple will give $50 U.S. or £40 U.K. Apple Gift Card with an eligible Apple Watch Series 12. Amazon’s Series 12 discount in the U.S. is worth more than Apple’s $50 gift card.






Apple Watch Ultra 4 – Best for battery life and outdoor adventures

				
					

				
			

Apple




The Ultra 4 is our choice for endurance athletes, outdoor enthusiasts, and buyers who prioritize battery life. It offers up to 50 hours of normal use, satellite communication, precision dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and Apple’s new Health Sensing System.
It’s more watch than most people need. Compare it with the Ultra 3, though, which retains many of its outdoor features but has a shorter 42-hour battery-life rating.
U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the Ultra 4 down to $774, a $25 saving. This November Amazon is selling the Apple Watch Ultra 4 for $699 on Amazon: that’s $100 off. 
U.K. Black Friday price: The Ultra 4 remained at its full £749 price during October Prime Day, but we’ve already seen it drop by £30 to £719 at Amazon.
Apple’s deal: The Apple Watch Ultra 4 comes with a $100 U.S. or £80 U.K. Apple gift card if you buy direct from Apple.






Apple Watch SE 3 – Our best budget choice

				
					

				
			
Apple / Amazon




The SE 3 is the best-value option for buyers who want the core Apple Watch experience. It includes an always-on display, temperature sensing, fast charging, and the S10 chip, but lacks ECG, blood oxygen monitoring, and the newer Health Sensing System.
It remains part of Apple’s current lineup despite launching in 2025. A strong Black Friday offer could make it an excellent affordable purchase, although its previous discounts mean there’s little reason to settle for a token reduction.
U.S. Black Friday price: Both last Black Friday and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to $199 and the 44mm version to $229 – $50 below their regular prices. This Black Friday, the U.S. price is down to $179, $70 off at Amazon.
U.K. Black Friday price: Black Friday 2025 and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to £199 and the 44mm version to £229, saving £20. So far the Apple Watch SE 3, 40mm has dropped to £199 (£20 off at Amazon).
Apple’s deal: Apple will give $50 U.S. or £40 U.K. Apple Gift Card with an eligible Apple Watch SE 3 when purchased from Apple.






Apple Watch Ultra 3 – Best clearance option for outdoor enthusiasts

				
					

				
			
Apple




The Ultra 3 is worth considering if you want a rugged Apple Watch without paying for the latest model. It offers satellite communication, dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and up to 42 hours of battery life.
You give up the Ultra 4’s longer battery life and newer Health Sensing System. Compare their actual selling prices: the Ultra 3 needs to be sufficiently cheaper to justify choosing the older generation.
U.S. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the Ultra 3 fell to $699, $100 saving. Our October Prime Day coverage found only used models, so it didn’t identify a comparable new-stock offer. So far this November we’ve seen the Apple Watch Ultra 3 for $649, but it’s now out of stock.
U.K. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the Ultra 3 was £719, or £30 off. October Prime Day listed it at £569. The price is even lower this November – you can get it for £495 at Argos, which is £254 less than the usual Apple Watch Ultra 4 price.






Apple Watch Series 11 – Best clearance option for everyday use

				
					

				
			
Apple Watch Series 11




The Series 11 could be a better-value everyday watch than the Series 12 if the price gap is large enough. It has the same quoted 24-hour battery life, although it lacks the newer Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features.
For buyers who don’t need those additions, a substantial clearance discount could be more useful than a small saving on the latest model.

Should you buy an Apple Watch now or wait for a better deal?
With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need an Apple Watch immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so you don’t necessarily need to wait for Black Friday itself. If an early offer matches or comes close to a previous low for the same model and configuration, it can be worth taking – particularly if you want a specific size, color, or band combination.
October Prime Day prices provide useful benchmarks. In the U.S., the Series 12 fell to $349 for the 42mm GPS model and $399 for the 46mm version, while the Ultra 4 reached $774. The SE 3 was $199 in 40mm and $229 in 44mm. Those SE prices also appeared last Black Friday, so we’d look for offers matching or beating them. In the U.K., October highlights included the 40mm SE 3 at £199 and the older 42mm Series 11 at £259.
The Series 12 and Ultra 4 only arrived in September, so finding a better price is the main reason to wait. If you don’t need a watch immediately, those previous offers give you a useful starting point for deciding whether to buy now or hold out.
Compare retailers, too. Last Black Friday, Walmart offered $150 off the Series 10, while U.K. shoppers could find up to £130 off at Currys and £200 off the Ultra 2’s original price at Argos. Our guide to the best time to buy an Apple Watch has more advice on choosing when to purchase.






Should you buy an older Apple Watch?

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Don’t assume an older Apple Watch is a bad buy. The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are only one generation old and can make excellent purchases if they’re substantially cheaper than the Series 12 or Ultra 4. Both retain many of their replacements’ core features, although you miss the newer Health Sensing System and, with the Ultra 3, the Ultra 4’s longer battery life.
Compare actual selling prices, matching case size, material, connectivity, and band where possible. A $50 difference between a Series 11 and Series 12 may not be enough to justify giving up the newer model’s health features, whereas a substantially larger saving could change the calculation. A discounted Series 11 could also be worth considering alongside the SE 3 if a small premium gets you features you’ll use.
Be much more cautious with the Series 8, SE 2, and original Ultra: those models cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 9 is the oldest standard Apple Watch compatible with the latest software, while the Ultra 2 is the oldest supported Ultra and the SE 3 is the only supported SE. Missing the latest software doesn’t make an older watch unusable, but it makes it harder to recommend as a purchase today.
The Series 9, Series 10, and Ultra 2 can still be worth considering at sufficiently low prices. However, compatibility with today’s software doesn’t guarantee how many future upgrades they’ll receive. Weigh the savings against the watch’s age and features, rather than assuming every supported generation offers equally good value.






Apple Watch deals to avoid 

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Don’t let a bigger advertised discount tempt you into paying more for a cellular Apple Watch you won’t use. If your iPhone is usually nearby, a GPS model can already handle calls, messages, and notifications through your phone. It can also track runs, use Apple Pay, and play downloaded music without your iPhone. As our experience testing a cellular Apple Watch showed, the extra connectivity may add little to everyday use.
Cellular is worth considering if you regularly leave your iPhone behind and want to remain contactable without Wi-Fi, or you’re setting up a watch for a child without an iPhone. Otherwise, you could pay extra for the hardware and then add an ongoing mobile-plan charge for a feature you rarely need. You don’t have to activate a plan on a cellular model, so it can still be a good buy if its sale price matches or beats the GPS version. Our GPS versus cellular Apple Watch guide explains the trade-offs.
Check the rest of the configuration, too. A premium case material or expensive band can make a heavily discounted watch cost more than a simpler version that meets your needs. Judge offers against previous selling prices as well as the advertised reduction: a large saving from the original launch price doesn’t necessarily mean exceptional value. Check any spending requirements, contracts, trade-ins, or rebates attached to offers advertising a “free” Apple Watch.
Finally, check whether you’re buying a new, refurbished, or used watch, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For a used or refurbished model, check the stated battery condition and confirm that it has been removed from the previous owner’s account, with Activation Lock turned off. Make sure the watch is compatible with your iPhone before ordering.






How we choose Apple Watch deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on Apple Watch reviews and everyday wear. We consider comfort, performance, battery life, charging, health and fitness features, and value – not just the specifications or advertised saving.
Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our Series 12 review assessed battery life and charging performance alongside its newer health features. We also draw on everyday experience: our cellular Apple Watch testing examines whether staying connected without an iPhone justified the extra hardware and subscription costs.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. We check the generation, case size, material, connectivity, and included band so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside discounted replacements.
Our Best Apple Watch guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the right choice: your budget, wrist size, activities, and the features you need all matter.

title: iPhone 18e to Get Redesigned, iPad Pro-Style Camera
content:
Apple is planning to redesign the appearance of the iPhone 18e's rear camera, according to new design information from Engadget.


The publication says it has seen computer-aided design (CAD) files depicting a raised housing that groups the camera, flash, and microphone together. It measures approximately 28mm by 35mm. This would give the rear of the device a significantly different appearance from the iPhone 17e, whose flash and microphone sit separately from its protruding circular camera.

Engadget likens the arrangement to the M5 iPad Pro's camera module. The redesign could indicate that Apple plans to upgrade the camera in some way.

chip upgrade was the only improvement they could confirm at the time. The device is expected to use Apple's A20 chip, moving from the ‌iPhone 17e‌'s 3nm manufacturing process to 2nm for improved performance and efficiency. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo has also pointed to 9GB of RAM for Apple's lower-end spring 2027 iPhones, up from 8GB.

6.12-inch OLED display with a 60Hz refresh rate and a single 48-megapixel rear camera, along with a potential front-facing camera upgrade. "Fixed Focus Digital" subsequently claimed that the iPhone 18e could instead gain a larger 6.3-inch display and share a 4,430mAh battery with the standard iPhone 18. The iPhone 18e is also rumored to adopt Apple's C2 modem, replacing the C1X in the current model.

Engadget attributes the CAD files to a supply chain source who previously provided accurate details about iPhone 17 and iPhone 18 Pro colors. The iPhone 18e is expected to launch alongside the ‌iPhone 18‌ and iPhone Air 2 in February or March 2027.

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 24, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November.
Black Friday is one of the best opportunities to save on a Mac, with retailers competing to discount MacBooks and desktop models – including recently released machines. The Black Friday Mac deals are already here, and the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage is where we’d start for most people. Amazon has listed it for $1,049 in the U.S. and £1,148.97 in the U.K., saving $250 and about £150 off Apple’s current prices. If you already have a display, keyboard, and mouse, the M6 Mac mini is a cheaper way to get a new Mac at $779 or £759.
There are bigger savings on MacBook Pro models if you need the extra power. In the U.S., Amazon has listed the 14-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro with 36GB of memory and 2TB of storage for $3,599, $500 off. In the U.K., the 16-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory and 1TB of storage is £2,599, £400 off. That’s about £514 less than the equivalent touchscreen model on sale, so think about how much you’d benefit from the OLED display before paying the premium.
Apple’s June price increases make the advertised savings worth a closer look. The U.S. MacBook Air deal is $50 below its pre-increase price, while the U.K. offer is still about £50 above what Apple charged before June. We compare prices for the same configurations so you can see which deals are worth taking and which have been better before.
Below, we explain which Mac to buy at these prices, from the budget MacBook Neo to the Mac Studio. If you’re deciding whether to buy now or wait for Apple’s November 27–30 promotion, compare what you’d pay today with what you’d actually use from a gift card on a future purchase. For discounts on iPads, AirPods, and more, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Apple Store Black Friday offer: From November 27 to 30, Apple is offering a gift card worth $200/£160 with either size of M5 MacBook Air, $250/£200 with an eligible 14-inch M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro, $300/£240 with an eligible 16-inch M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro, and $100/£80 with an eligible Mac mini. The gift card is for a future Apple purchase. Compare its value with the upfront discounts we share below. See the full Apple Black Friday offer.
Which Mac or MacBook should you buy this Black Friday?


MacBook Air – Our best overall choice 

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




The MacBook Air is our recommendation for most buyers. Both sizes offer a lightweight, silent laptop for everyday work, studying, and occasional creative projects. Choose the 13-inch for portability or the 15-inch for more workspace without MacBook Pro pricing.
We’d prioritize a competitive price on the memory and storage you need. For regular lengthy exports or other sustained demanding tasks, consider a MacBook Pro with active cooling instead.
U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the 13-inch M5 Air with 16GB memory and 512GB storage to $1,099, and the equivalent 15-inch to $1,299. We are already seeing up to $300 off the 13-inch models, and $300 off the 15-inch options, bringing the price below the original MSRP from before Apple increased prices. These savings are better than Apple’s $200 gift card.
U.K. Black Friday price: October offers included approximately £1,199 for the 13-inch M5 Air and £1,349 for the 15-inch, both with 512GB storage. Last Black Friday’s M4 models with 256GB reached £849 and £1,025. Match storage capacities when comparing generations. Amazon has the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage, 16GB of memory, and an 8-core GPU for £1,148.97, saving £150 off Apple’s £1,299 price. That’s about £50 less than it cost during October Prime Day. However, earlier in November 2026, we saw £200 off the 13-inch MacBook Air and £200 off the 15-inch model. The £160 Apple gift card is close to the £150 upfront discount on the 13-inch 512GB Air.
Apple’s Deal: Apple will give $200 U.S. or £160 U.K. Apple Gift Card with an eligible MacBook Air.






MacBook Neo – Our budget choice, at the right price

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




The MacBook Neo suits browsing, schoolwork, streaming, and office apps. Its lower starting price makes it appealing, but its fixed 8GB of memory leaves less room for demanding workloads.
Check which configuration is discounted: only the 512GB version includes Touch ID. Both lack a backlit keyboard, MagSafe, and Thunderbolt. Compare clearance MacBook Air stock before deciding how much those compromises save you.
U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has cut the price of both Neo models by $50, the best discount we’ve seen so far. Previously the Neo was only ever discounted by $10-$15.
U.K. Black Friday price: We saw a Prime Day low of £549, but that was before Apple increased prices. Amazon has the 256GB MacBook Neo for £679.97 (£19.03 off) and the 512GB model for £749 (£50 off). The 256GB model has previously dropped to £549, so the current deal is £130.97 above that earlier low.






MacBook Pro M6 – Best step up from the Air

				
					

				
			
Macbook Pro M6 Aufmacher

Halyna Kubiv




The standard M6 MacBook Pro is worth considering if you want a better built-in display, more connections, and cooling for sustained workloads without paying for a Pro or Max chip. It comes in a 14-inch size, with a non-touch Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI, and an SDXC card slot.
It starts with 16GB memory and 1TB storage, so account for those specifications when comparing prices with an Air or older Pro. Despite the newer generation number, the standard M6 isn’t automatically the better choice for demanding work than an M5 Pro or M5 Max.
U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 model wasn’t available during October Prime Day, but it’s on offer for Black Friday with $200 off at Amazon, where it’s $1,799. B&H also has $150 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6)

MacBook Pro M5 Pro – Best for demanding professional work

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The non-touchscreen M5 Pro MacBook Pro is a strong choice for development, photography, video editing, and heavier multitasking. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, it offers professional performance without the Max chip’s higher price.
Compare it with the touchscreen version using the same memory and storage. Both offer M5 Pro configurations, so a discounted non-touch model could be particularly good value if its existing XDR display meets your needs.
U.S. Black Friday price: October prices included $2,339 for the 14-inch M5 Pro with 24GB memory and 1TB storage, and $2,749 for the equivalent 16-inch. MacBook Pro M5 Max – Best for demanding graphics and video

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




Consider the non-touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro if your work benefits from additional graphics power or more memory than an M5 Pro supports. Complex 3D projects and demanding video production make a stronger case for it than everyday productivity.
We’d choose the configuration around the work you do. A larger advertised discount on a Max doesn’t necessarily make it better value than a less expensive Pro that meets your needs. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the options.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro is most compelling for its OLED display and thinner, lighter design. Improved blacks and reduced blooming could matter more to your everyday experience than touch controls, particularly if you spend most of your working day using the built-in screen.
Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, these models offer comparable processing performance to their non-touch equivalents. Compare matching configurations: the regular premium is $400/£400, so consider how much you’ll benefit from the display before paying extra.

The M6 Mac mini suits buyers who already own a display, keyboard, and mouse. It offers a compact desktop for everyday work and lighter creative projects. Check storage carefully: the entry-level model has a restrictive 256GB SSD.

Stephan Wiesend
