Should you buy a Mac or MacBook now or wait for a better deal?
With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need a Mac immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so an early offer can be worth taking if it matches or approaches a previous low for the same configuration. Waiting can be a gamble if you’re buying clearance stock with a particular screen size, memory capacity, or finish. If the retailer discount is close to Apple’s gift card value and you already have another Apple purchase planned, it may be worth waiting until November 27 to take advantage of Apple’s gift card offer, but note that MacBook Neo, standard M6 MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac Studio are not included in Apple’s Black Friday deal. 
The M5 MacBook Air remains an appealing purchase at a good discount, with a replacement not expected until 2027. The recently updated Mac mini and Mac Studio are also worth considering if they meet your needs. The main reason to wait is a better price rather than an imminent replacement.
MacBook Pro buyers no longer need to wait for the rumored October launches: the standard M6 and OLED touchscreen models are now available. However, their recent arrival may limit initial discounts. Non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max models could offer better value, particularly if you don’t need the touchscreen version’s improved display and lighter design. If your existing M4 or M5 MacBook Pro still meets your needs, there’s little reason to upgrade simply because a newer option exists.
The M6 iMac has only just arrived, replacing the aging M4 version. Compare a modest saving on the latest model with a substantial clearance discount on its predecessor, rather than assuming the older machine is automatically the better deal.
Previous prices need context this year. Following June’s increases, a discount from Apple’s current asking price may still leave you paying more than before the increases. Compare retailers as well: Amazon competes with Best Buy, Walmart, and B&H in the U.S., and retailers including Currys and John Lewis in the U.K. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the current choices.






Which Mac specifications are worth paying for?
The cheapest Mac isn’t always the best value. Use Black Friday to get a configuration that will serve you for longer within your budget, but don’t pay for performance or features you won’t use.
Check the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. A standard M6 and an M5 Pro or M5 Max serve different needs: the newer generation number alone doesn’t tell you which is better for your work. For MacBook Pro listings, distinguish the OLED touchscreen version from non-touch models.
Avoid saving a small amount by buying too little memory or storage. Most current Macs start with 16GB of unified memory, but the MacBook Neo has a fixed 8GB, and some desktop configurations include only a 256GB SSD. Unified memory cannot be upgraded later. An external SSD can add storage, but it cannot compensate for insufficient RAM.
Once the processor meets your needs, additional memory may be more useful than a faster chip. Compare a discounted Air with the Neo, too: the M5 Air starts with twice the memory and storage of the entry-level Neo. Our Mac buying guide explains which specifications suit different workloads.
Check whether the configuration includes nano-texture glass. This optional finish reduces glare and reflections, which can help in bright rooms or near windows, but increases the price. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may offer better value.






Should you buy an older Mac or MacBook?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older Mac can be excellent value if its price reflects its age and configuration. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of the newer equivalent, rather than focusing on a large percentage saving from its original launch price.
Previous-generation Apple silicon models are the most promising starting point. A discounted M4 MacBook Air or standard M5 MacBook Pro may meet your needs comfortably. Older Pro and Max configurations can also be worth considering if they provide the memory, graphics performance, and connections your work requires for substantially less money.
Check what the saving buys—and what you give up. An older Mac with more memory or storage could be more useful than a newer entry-level configuration. Conversely, a cheaper older Air with 256GB storage isn’t directly comparable with an M5 Air that starts with 512GB. The non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros also remain current options, despite the arrival of the standard M6 and touchscreen models.
Be much more cautious with Intel Macs. Their software support is winding down, and a low purchase price may leave you with a machine that has a limited useful life for current apps and macOS features. Check compatibility with the software you need before buying any older model.
For used or refurbished Macs, check battery condition on laptops, warranty coverage, and the returns policy. Confirm that Activation Lock has been removed and that the Mac isn’t still enrolled in an organization’s management system.

Should I buy a Mac Studio?






Mac or MacBook deals to avoid
Treat large advertised discounts carefully. Following June’s price increases, “$400 off” may simply bring a Mac closer to what it cost before the increase. Compare previous selling prices for the same configuration, rather than judging the offer solely against today’s recommended price.
Check whether the price includes AppleCare+ or another protection plan. Some Amazon listings bundle coverage with the Mac. If you don’t want it, a listing without coverage could be cheaper; if you do, compare the bundle with buying the Mac and coverage separately.
Check for a bundled power adapter, too. Some Mac laptops are sold without one in the U.K. and EU. A charger bundle may be useful if you need an adapter, but could mean paying extra unnecessarily if you already own a suitable one.
Compare the complete setup cost. A Mac mini or Studio requires a display, keyboard, and mouse or trackpad, while adapters and docks can add to the cost of any Mac.
Finally, distinguish cash discounts from gift cards, trade-ins, financing, and membership-only offers. Read the conditions, check the seller, and confirm whether the Mac is new, refurbished, or used, along with its warranty and returns policy.






How we choose Mac and MacBook deals
Macworld has covered the Mac since its launch in 1984, and our recommendations draw on decades of experience and hands-on reviews. We consider performance, display quality, battery life, portability, connectivity, and everyday use alongside price to explain which Macs suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess which upgrades are worth paying for. We look at whether additional processing power benefits demanding workloads, when more memory is useful, and whether a premium display justifies the extra cost. A MacBook Air may offer better value for everyday work, while a Pro, Max, or Ultra configuration needs to earn its higher price through the work it enables.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than judging a deal solely against today’s recommended retail price. A large advertised discount doesn’t automatically make an offer exceptional.
We consider the complete purchase, too: the retailer, product condition, warranty, and any conditions attached to the price. For desktop Macs, we also account for the display and accessories you’ll need. Our Mac buying guide and MacBook comparison explain how to choose the right model and configuration.

title: iPhone Duo: 20 Tips to Get the Most Out of Apple's Foldable
content:
The iPhone Duo's folding design features two displays that introduce several new ways to use an iPhone. Over the past few weeks, we've covered the best of them, from Split View multitasking to hands-free group photos.


If you're lucky enough to be an iPhone Duo owner, we've collected the 20 top tips worth trying below. Full tutorials for each tip can be found in our how-to section.

Use Two Apps Side by Side


Unfold your iPhone Duo so that it's in landscape orientation, then swipe up from the bottom. Drag an app to the left or right edge, and then tap a second app to make it fill the other side. You can also touch and hold an app icon and tap Open in Split View. The split is fixed at 50/50, and only one app plays audio at a time.

Lock Two Apps as an App Pair


With two apps open in Split View, simply tap the divider between them to ensure they always launch together. If you change your mind, drag the divider fully to either edge of the screen to unpair them.

Reach for the Outer Display


This one requires iOS 27.3, which is currently in beta. With your Duo closed, swipe left on the left edge of the outer display to bring the right side of the screen within reach, and vice versa. Note that it's on by default after updating to the beta (control it via Settings ➝ Accessibility ➝ Touch ➝ Reachability) and it works on the outer display only.

Keep a Video Playing Above an App in Portrait


Rotating to portrait normally drops Split View to one app, but Apple has provided a workaround. Start a video in a Picture in Picture-supporting app like Apple TV or Podcasts, then tap the PiP icon, swipe up to the Home Screen, open the second app (it can't be another video app), and tap the newly visible stack icon in the PiP window to dock the video above it.

Silence Quickly with no Mute Switch


The iPhone Duo has no Ring/Silent switch and no Action button that you can assign to silence your iPhone. The quickest alternative is to invoke Control Center and tap the Silent Mode bell. If the control is missing, add it via the plus button ➝ Add a Control. You'll find it under the Sounds category. Note that alarms and media audio will still play in Silent mode.

Open Control Center With a Tap, Not a Swipe


Tap the circular status bar immediately below the clock – the combined Wi-Fi, cellular, and battery indicator – instead of stretching for the top corner to swipe down Control Center. It sits even lower when a Live Activity is running, so it's often easier to reach one-handed. It also makes silencing the phone with the mute control a two-tap job.

Split the Keyboard in Landscape


With your Duo unfolded in landscape orientation, tap the More (...) button at the top-left of the keyboard, then tap Split for a more comfortable typing experience. Don't like it? Simply choose More ➝ Full to rejoin the layout. Another tip to remember is that when your Duo is closed, you can long-press the globe or emoji key to shift the keyboard to one side for easier one-handed typing.

Use StandBy Without a Charger


In Settings ➝ StandBy, you can tick the folding positions that you want, and if you keep Only While Charging switched off, you can enjoy your StandBy modes without a charger having to be plugged in. When you lock the phone, half-fold it like a book or make it into a tent shape it on a flat surface, StandBy will start automatically.

Turn the Hinge into an App Launcher


automatically launch whenever you unfold the phone. For example, if you choose the Kindle app, unfolding the Duo feels like opening a book. You can also constrain it with conditions like time of day or Focus.

Unlock iPhone Duo With Your Face


This one requires the iOS 27.3 beta 2, but it's a good one. If you authenticate into Settings ➝ Touch ID & Passcode, and toggle on the new Face Unlock option, you can unlock the device with the front camera. It only works at the Lock Screen when the Duo is closed, so you can't use it for authenticating Apple Pay purchases or inserting logins and passwords from the Passwords app. You also need to use Touch ID or a passcode for unlocking the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when it's unfolded.

Skip the Swipe Up With Rest Finger to Open


The toggle in Settings ➝ Touch ID & Passcode (also in Settings ➝ Accessibility ➝ Side Button) lets you open the phone straight past the Lock Screen, simply by resting your finger on the side button while the screen is awake. No more needing to swipe up to access the Home Screen.

Take Selfies With the Rear Cameras


Unfold your iPhone Duo, open the Camera app, then turn the phone around and drag the Show Camera slider on the outer display. You'll get the 48-megapixel rear Fusion cameras with a live preview on the side facing you, plus you can shoot with the on-screen shutter button, a volume button, or Camera Control.

Let Someone Beside You Join FaceTime 


Next time you're on a group FaceTime call and someone in the room wants to join in, simply tap the screen, tap the More button, then tap Duo FaceTime. The makes the person next to you get their own view via the Center Stage front camera and the under-display camera, meaning nobody has to squeeze into the same frame.

Lock Rotation for Each Display Independently


Found in Control Center, Orientation Lock on the iPhone Duo applies only to the display you're using when you enable it, so the outer display can stay locked in portrait while the inner display rotates freely. Note that videos will still rotate automatically in tent mode, regardless of the lock.

Make Volume Buttons Follow Rotation


Go to Settings ➝ Sounds & Haptics, and turn off Fixed Position Volume Controls. The top or right button is then always volume up, whichever way you are holding the phone. Apple's documentation suggests this dynamic behavior is the default, but that hasn't been the case on the early units we've tested.

Shift Left Edge for Case Wearers


If you enable the toggle next to Settings ➝ Display & Brightness ➝ Shift Left Edge, it will inset the outer display so that your case doesn't cover on-screen content. Apple's official case prompts you to enable it, but you can also turn it on manually if you have a third-party case.

Unlock With Your Apple Watch


If you have an Apple Watch, this tip is an absolute game-changer. Go to Settings ➝ Touch ID & Passcode ➝ Unlock with Nearby Devices and toggle on your watch model. With the watch on your wrist (and unlocked), wake the Duo and swipe up, and the watch is your authentication – no Touch ID required.

Let Your Subject See the Shot With Duo Preview


When lining up a shot in the Camera app, tap the Outer Display Options button and choose Duo Preview, and your subject will see a mirrored live preview on the outer display while you frame it up. You can do it for both photos and video.

Get Hands-Free Group Photos


Prop your iPhone Duo somewhere steady, tap the Smart Take button in the Camera pp, and get in the frame. The device will capture automatically when you pose or hold still, and can take up to 20 photos. If you have it half-folded on its side, one half of the screen becomes the viewfinder and the other shows the shots that have already been taken.

Get the Attention of Kids and Pets in Photos

title: Best AirPods Black Friday deals 2026: Our picks for Pro, standard AirPods and Max
content:
Macworld






Best Black Friday AirPods deals so far: U.S.
AirPods Pro 3: $149 ($100 off at Walmart, MSRP $249)

AirPods 5 (wireless charging case): £129 (£10 off at Amazon, RRP £139).
PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 24 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
Black Friday is a great time to buy AirPods, with retailers competing to offer discounts across Apple’s earbuds and over-ear headphones. Previous sales have brought substantial savings on established models, clearance bargains on older generations, and even discounts on newly released AirPods. But the biggest percentage saving doesn’t necessarily mean the best buy: an older pair needs to be sufficiently cheaper than its replacement to justify missing out on newer features.
The best Black Friday AirPods deal we’ve seen so far is on the AirPods Pro 3. Amazon has listed them for $149 in the U.S. and £165 in the U.K., saving about $100 and £54, respectively. Amazon has now sold out in the U.S., but the $149 deal is available at Walmart. That’s a much bigger U.S. discount than the roughly $30 off we saw last Black Friday. If you prefer over-ear headphones, Amazon has also listed the AirPods Max 2 for $419 in the U.S., $130 off and just $20 above the lowest price we’ve tracked.
If you prefer an open-ear fit, AirPods 5 are the cheaper option: we’ve seen the standard model for £109 in the U.K., while it was still at its regular $129 U.S. price at our last check. Below, we explain which AirPods to choose and how the offers compare with previous discounts. For savings on Macs, iPads, Apple Watch and more, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Apple’s own Black Friday offer runs November 27–30, 2026. Buy eligible AirPods directly from Apple, and you’ll receive a gift card to use on a future purchase. More details here: Apple Black Friday 2026: Up to $300/£240 in gift cards – full list of eligible products.




Which AirPods should you buy this Black Friday?


AirPods Pro 3 – Our best overall choice

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods Pro 3 are especially worth considering if you want strong noise cancellation, a secure in-ear fit, or Apple’s hearing-health features. Their foam-infused ear tips help improve the fit, while an in-ear heart-rate sensor adds another reason to choose them over standard AirPods. Battery life is rated at up to eight hours with noise cancellation enabled.
For most buyers looking for noise-isolating earbuds, these would be our first choice. Older AirPods Pro 2 are worth considering only when the clearance savings are substantial.
U.S. Black Friday price:  Amazon has slashed $100 off the AirPods Pro 3, to just $149, the same price as the AirPods 5 with wireless charging case and below their previous all-time low of $169. Amazon has sold out, but Walmart still has them at that price. 
U.K. Black Friday price: Earlier in November, AirPods Pro 3 were £30 off in the U.K., before rising to £200, then dropping down to £174, only to return to £200, but now they are down to £165! This is one to watch because that price is going up and down like a Swanee whistle. 
Apple’s deal: You can get a $50/£40 gift card with your purchase. 






AirPods 5 – Best for buyers who prefer earbuds without silicone tips

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods 5 offer a lower-cost entry point and an open-ear design for people who don’t like silicone-tipped earbuds. They include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, alongside Transparency mode and Adaptive Audio.
Check which charging case you’re buying. The Wireless Charging Case package adds wireless charging, longer battery life, a Find My speaker, and volume adjustment by swiping the stems. It’s our preferred package when the price difference is small.
U.S. Black Friday price: We’ve not seen a discount yet on the AirPods 5.
U.K. Black Friday price:  You can get £10 off the AirPods 5 in the U.K., but earlier in November there was £20 off. Apple’s gift card ‘saving’ is better if you are likely to spend the voucher with Apple.
Apple’s deal: Get $25/£20 gift card with the purchase of AirPods 5. 






AirPods Max 2 – Best for over-ear listening

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods Max 2 are the option to consider if you specifically want over-ear headphones. The March 2026 update introduced Apple’s H2 chip and improved noise cancellation, while retaining the premium design and a choice of colors.
We find them difficult to recommend at full price, so the size of the discount matters. Compare any offer with previous sale prices rather than judging it solely against Apple’s asking price.

Apple’s deal: Get a $75/£60 gift card with the purchase of AirPods Max 2.






Other headphones – Worthy AirPods alternatives

				
					

				
			
Beats




If AirPods aren’t in your budget, Apple also sells a line of Beats headphones and earbuds that offer many of the same features for a lower price, including the popular on-ear Solo 4 and Powerbeats Pro 2. We’ll also track headphone deals in our roundup of the best earbuds for iPhone and best over-ear headphones if you’d like to see deals on other brands.

Should you buy AirPods now or wait for a better deal?

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need AirPods immediately. But the sales now stretch across much of November, so you don’t necessarily need to wait for Black Friday itself. If an early offer is close to a model’s previous low, it can be worth taking: last year’s best deals frequently sold out, and popular offers could go quickly again.
Previous sale prices provide useful benchmarks. We’ve seen AirPods Pro 3 reach $169, while AirPods Max 2 fell to $399 during June Prime Day. An offer above those prices may still be worth considering, but a reduction from Apple’s regular price doesn’t automatically make it an exceptional deal.
For AirPods 5, waiting for a discount makes sense if you aren’t in a hurry: they didn’t receive a significant reduction during October Prime Day. With AirPods Max 2, we’d hold out for a substantial saving rather than pay full price.
Compare retailers, too. Amazon isn’t always cheapest: Walmart and Best Buy also compete on AirPods pricing, while Argos offered competitive U.K. deals last year. Our guide to the best time to buy AirPods has more advice on purchase timing.






Should you buy an old pair of AirPods? 
Older-generation AirPods can be a good buy at the right clearance price. Compare their actual selling price with the discounted price of their replacement, rather than focusing on the percentage saving from an old launch price. A substantial discount can make an older pair worthwhile; a small difference may leave you sacrificing useful features for little saving.
AirPods 4 are harder to recommend now that AirPods 5 include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, starting at the same $129 price previously charged for AirPods 4 without ANC. Check which AirPods 4 version you’re buying—there were models with and without noise cancellation—and look for a substantial saving over AirPods 5.
AirPods Pro 2 remain worth considering if they’re significantly cheaper than Pro 3. However, the newer model improves fit, noise cancellation, and battery life, while adding heart-rate sensing. Compare their sale prices carefully: a strong Pro 3 discount could make the older pair’s clearance offer less attractive.
The original AirPods Max also need a substantial discount to justify choosing them over Max 2. The newer headphones add the H2 chip, improved noise cancellation, and features including Adaptive Audio and Conversation Awareness. Check the generation rather than relying on the charging port alone: the original AirPods Max were also sold in a USB-C version.
Buying older stock new is different from buying used or refurbished AirPods. For those pairs, check the stated condition, charging case, warranty, and returns policy, and buy from a reputable seller. Be cautious about battery condition and unusually low marketplace prices, since convincing counterfeits can resemble genuine AirPods. Our guide explains how to spot fake AirPods.
For more advice, see our AirPods buying guide and guide to the best time to buy AirPods.






AirPods deals to avoid

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Check exactly what an offer includes before comparing prices. Different charging-case packages can affect features and value, so make sure you’re comparing equivalent versions. Also check any spending requirements, contracts, or rebates attached to offers advertising “free” AirPods.
Judge the price against previous selling prices as well as the advertised discount. A large saving from the recommended retail price doesn’t necessarily mean a particularly good deal if retailers regularly charge less.
Check whether the listing is for a new, refurbished, or used pair. For used or refurbished AirPods, look for clear information about condition, warranty, and returns coverage. Battery condition deserves particular caution: a low purchase price may be less attractive if listening time has deteriorated.
Finally, check who is selling and dispatching your order, particularly when shopping through a marketplace. Unusually low prices from unfamiliar sellers warrant caution, since counterfeit AirPods can look convincing. Our guide explains how to tell if AirPods are fake.






How we choose AirPods deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on AirPods reviews. We consider sound quality, noise cancellation, comfort, battery life, and everyday use – not just the specifications or advertised saving.
Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our AirPods Pro 3 review assessed how securely the redesigned ear tips stayed in place during exercise, checked battery life against Apple’s claims, and evaluated the heart-rate sensor. Our AirPods Max 2 review weighed their excellent sound and noise cancellation against drawbacks including weight and the Smart Case.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. Our Best AirPods guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the best choice for everyone: fit, listening habits, and the features you need all matter.
For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our roundups of the best Mac deals, iPad deals, and Apple Watch deals.

title: Next Apple event: Expected dates and what Apple could launch next
content:
Macworld





Apple hasn’t announced a date for its next event. Its usual timetable puts WWDC in June and the flagship iPhone event in September, but spring is less predictable. Some years Apple holds a keynote or invites the media to try new products; in others, it announces them through press releases. The first announcements of 2027 could come as early as February or March.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is targeting that window for the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and a new entry-level iPad. An M6 MacBook Air and a second-generation MacBook Neo are also expected early in the year, while the next iPhone Air, an OLED iPad Air, and an updated iPad Pro could follow later in the first half of 2027. 
October 2026 showed how that can work. Apple announced the iPad mini with A20 Pro on October 26, followed by the 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro and M6 iMac the next day. It then introduced its first touchscreen MacBook Pro at its “Pro and Tell” media experience in Los Angeles on October 28.
In this guide, we use Apple’s past event dates and the latest reporting to assess when the company might next make an announcement, which new Apple products could arrive first, and what may have to wait until later in the year. We’ll also explain when you can expect a livestream and update the calendar as Apple confirms dates.


When is Apple’s next event?
Apple’s next product announcements could come as early as February 2027, although the company has not confirmed a date.
Over the past decade, Apple has held spring events and media experiences on several dates:
March 4, 2026
May 7, 2024
March 8, 2022
April 20, 2021
March 25, 2019
March 27, 2018
Apple can also announce products without holding an event. In 2025, it introduced the iPhone 16e in February, followed in March by the seventh-generation iPad Air, 11th-generation iPad, MacBook Air and Mac Studio.
That makes spring 2027 a plausible window for further launches, whether Apple holds an event, invites the media to a hands-on experience or announces products through press releases.






What could Apple announce at its next event?
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple could announce the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, and a new entry-level iPad in February or March 2027. A second-generation iPhone Air is also in the works, but it may arrive later.
Gurman also expects an M6 MacBook Air and a second-generation MacBook Neo early in 2027.





Apple event calendar 2027: What will Apple launch?


TimescaleEvent themeDatesProducts

Early 2027 Possible product announcementsFebruary or March (reported)iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, entry-level iPad
JuneWWDC7 June (predicted)Expected: To reveal plans for: iOS, macOS and other software
SeptemberiPhone eventTBCExpected: New iPhones, new Apple Watch

 



				
					

				
			
Calendars at the ready.

Foundry





 FAQ 


1.
How far in advance does Apple announce an event?
Apple usually announces its events around one to two weeks before they take place, although the timing varies. The October 13, 2026 Experience was announced just five days in advance. Apple also sometimes chooses to announce products via press release without holding an event. 





2.
How long do Apple Events usually last?
Apple keynotes usually last between one and two hours and feature the CEO alongside various other Apple executives.
WWDC and the September event tend to be longer keynotes; the spring and late-fall events can be slightly shorter. 
For example, the September 2024 keynote event was 1 hour 38 minutes.





3.
What time do Apple events normally start in U.S., U.K. and other global time zones?
Apple’s keynote events tend to start at 10 am PT or 1 pm ET. That translates to the following times in the countries where most of our readers live:
U.S.: 10 am PDT, 11 am MDT, 12 pm CDT, 1 pm EDT
Canada: as above, plus 2 pm ADT
U.K.: 6 pm
Europe: 7 pm CEST, 8 pm EEST
India: 10:30 pm IST
Australia: next day — 1 am AWST, 2:30 am ACST, 3 am AEST
New Zealand: next day — 5 am NZST
The timings are generally the same for all Apple Keynotes, but can be slightly different if Apple holds the event during the period of a couple of weeks when the clocks have changed in the U.S. but not elsewhere.
Sometimes Apple holds events at different times, for example, in October 2023 the event was held in late afternoon in San Francisco, which meant it was midnight in the U.K. The event on October 13, 2026 started at 9 am in New York, 2 pm in the U.K.
If Apple doesn’t hold an event and instead just issues a press release, that usually happens around 8 am PT, 11 am ET and 4 pm U.K. time.





4.
How often does Apple hold events?
There can be as many as four Apple events in a year:  
Spring Event
WWDC in June
iPhone Event in September
Late Fall Event in October
This event calendar is by no means set in stone, though, with the spring and October events being less regular. Some years, Apple doesn’t hold a spring event at all. In 2025 Apple only held two events, preferring instead to announce new products via press release.





5.
Will there be a live stream at the next Apple Event?
Apple doesn’t livestream its media experiences, but for events like WWDC and the iPhone launch in September, it livestreams a keynote presentation. 





6.
Does Apple ever announce products without an event? 
Apple frequently announces products without a keynote event, often opting for press releases or multi-day announcement windows. In recent years, the company has increasingly reserved its large-scale media events for major flagship launches, such as the primary iPhone lineup in September, while using press releases for iterative updates or “chip bumps” that may not warrant a full hour-long presentation.





7.
How to watch an Apple event
Apple events are typically broadcast across several digital platforms, allowing viewers to tune in from almost any device. While the company previously restricted access to its own hardware or the Safari browser, these barriers have been removed in recent years.
You can access live Apple presentations through the following official channels:
YouTube: This is often considered the easiest way to watch. Apple streams its keynotes live on its official YouTube channel, which can be accessed via any web browser or the YouTube app on smartphones, tablets, and smart TVs.
Apple.com: The company hosts a dedicated “Events” page on its official website. 
Apple TV App: The stream is available within the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV hardware. Keynotes are usually listed in the app’s lineup a day or two before the event begins.
Apple Podcasts: Apple also showcases its events through the Podcasts app on Apple devices, where you can watch the video presentation.
We usually run a Live Blog which will provide minute-by-minute text updates and analysis as products are announced.
Following the end of the event, detailed breakdowns will also be available on the Macworld Podcast, which can be found on Spotify, Soundcloud, and Apple Podcasts. 








Will Apple hold a spring event in 2027? 

				
					

				
			John Ternus: Apple’s new CEO.
Michael Simon / Foundry




Apple’s spring events have become increasingly unpredictable. The company has not held a traditional spring event since May 2024, although it did invite members of the media, including Macworld, to a “Special Apple Experience” in 2026. 
Rather than a keynote presentation, the March 4, 2026 gathering was a hands-on showcase that followed three days of product announcements, including the MacBook Neo, iPhone 17e, and M5 MacBook Air.
Apple hasn’t announced a spring 2027 event, but Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is looking to spread its launches across more of the year, so the early 2027 products could be announced in stages through press releases and smaller hands-on events.
The iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and entry-level iPad could arrive in February or March. An M6 MacBook Air and a second-generation MacBook Neo are also expected early in the year. The next iPhone Air, an OLED iPad Air, and an updated iPad Pro could follow later in the first half of 2027.






When is WWDC 2027?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




When is the WWDC keynote?
In 2026 the WWDC keynote was on Monday June 8. In 2025 it started on Monday June 9. We expect WWDC will start on Monday 7 June in 2027. 
WWDC generally runs from the Monday to Friday in the second week of June. 
What Apple could launch at WWDC
WWDC is Apple’s big developer event at which it reveals plans for the operating systems that run on Apple hardware.
In June 2027 we expect Apple to unveil details of iOS 28, iPadOS 28, macOS 28, updates to watchOS, tvOS, HomePod software, and an update to Apple’s visionOS.
Apple sometimes announces new hardware at WWDC, usually the high-end models targeted at power users, so we could see new Macs.
Following the keynote on Monday, developer events and sessions will run throughout the week. You can read more about WWDC date, times and everything you need to know in a separate article.





Apple event calendar 2026: What did Apple launch in 2026?

title: Meta's Muse Personal AI Agent Launches in the UK
content:
Meta has rolled out its Muse personal AI agent to users in the United Kingdom. Launched in the U.S. in September, Muse can complete tasks for users on their behalf, like sending an email or booking travel. 


The yeti-like character Meta designed to represent Muse appears in its standalone app, and users can also interact with the agent via WhatsApp.  

Meta says Muse is a tool users can trust to lend a "helping hand" with anything, from chasing a refund to doing the Christmas shopping. Muse can also use payment credentials at checkout with Link, a secure wallet for agents built by Stripe.

press release:
With Muse, you're in control. You choose what it can access, approve important actions before Muse carries them out , and can ask it to remember and or forget something. We built Muse to be private, safe, and secure by design. Every Muse gets its own virtual computer in the cloud, like a laptop that's just for you. Your information and logins are kept there, not in Meta's other services, and no one else's Muse can access them.
Meta says Muse is launching in the U.K. with popular global Connectors, and it also partners with British brands and retailers, including Marks & Spencer, Debenhams Group, ASOS, Currys, easyJet and Jet2. Muse can only be used by people aged 18 and over.

Reuters reported last week that Meta staffers had raised concerns internally about "undesired actions" carried out by the agent since it went live, from accessing encrypted messages to supplying bogus information about purchases. Meta has called these "isolated incidents."

Dots," but it has yet to roll out to the UK market.

title: New Apple products coming in 2027: What’s next?
content:
Macworld





What new products will Apple launch in 2027? Rumors point to a redesigned iPhone to mark its 20th anniversary, an OLED iPad Air, and potentially Apple’s first smart glasses. Updated Macs, more affordable iPhones and new AI-focused accessories could also be on the way.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is targeting February or March 2027 for the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, a new entry-level iPad, and updates to the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air. A second-generation iPhone Air, an OLED iPad Air, and an updated iPad Pro could follow later in the first half of the year.
Later in the year, attention will turn to the iPhone’s anniversary redesign, while camera-equipped AirPods and further smart-home developments could expand Apple’s lineup. 
Below, we round up the latest Apple product rumors for 2027 and beyond, including expected release dates, possible features and whether an upcoming update makes it worth waiting before you buy. Read on to find out what new products to expect at Apple’s next event and in 2027 and beyond.
Apple’s roadmap: At a glance


ProductExpected timingKey rumors

iPhone 18February or March 2027, reportedA20 chip and more RAM
iPhone 18eFebruary or March 2027, reportedA20 chip and possible Dynamic Island
iPad (12th generation) February or March 2027, reportedApple Intelligence support
MacBook Neo 2February or March 2027, reportedA19 Pro and more memory
MacBook Air M6February or March 2027, reportedM6 chip
iPad AirFirst half of 2027, possibly after the entry-level iPadOLED display
iPad ProFirst half of 2027, possibly after the entry-level iPadFaster performance; vapor-chamber cooling
iPhone Air 2First half of 2027 rumored, possibly after the 18 and 18e, according to Mark GurmaniPhone 18 and 18eSecond rear camera
Apple Smart GlassesWWDC introduction rumoredCameras, audio, Siri/Visual Intelligence
20th-anniversary iPhoneFall 2027 rumoredMajor redesign; possible iPhone 20 branding
Camera-equipped AirPods2027 rumoredCameras for AI features rather than conventional photography
Apple Watch 13, SE 4, Ultra 4Fall 2027 rumoredMajor redesign for Apple Watch Series 13 rumored
Larger iMac/iMac ProUnknownOlder reports suggest a 32-inch display and pro-level processors
Higher-end HomeViewLate 2027 at the earliest; potentially 20289-inch display, motorized arm and autonomous AI features; estimated $1,000 price

 






Every New Apple Product Launching in 2027 and beyond
In the sections below we’ve split the upcoming new products into categories including Mac, iPad, iPhone, Apple Watch, Home, AirPods, and some new product categories.








What new iPhones are coming in 2027?
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is targeting February or March 2027 for the standard iPhone 18 and the lower-cost iPhone 18e. A second-generation iPhone Air could follow later in the first half of the year. In the fall, Apple is rumored to be planning a major redesign to mark the iPhone’s 20th anniversary, with iPhone 20 among the names being floated.

				
					

				
			There are new iPhones coming.
Foundry




iPhone 18 & iPhone 18e
February or March 2027 
The iPhone 18 and 18e are rumored to arrive together in the spring of 2027. Both could gain A20 chips and more RAM. The iPhone 18 is expected to retain dual rear cameras and gain a 24MP selfie camera; the 18e may keep one rear camera and a 60Hz display. Read about the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e rumors. 
iPhone Air 2
First half of 2027 rumored, could be after the iPhone 18 and 18e
The iPhone Air could also be getting an update. Purported accessory-maker dummy images posted by Sonny Dickson show a separate Air-style handset with two rear-camera openings.
There were previously rumors that the iPhone Air 2 will actually merge with the iPhone 18. See our iPhone Air 2 rumors.
iPhone 19 or 20 – 20th anniversary iPhone 
September, as per tradition
Apple’s 20th-anniversary iPhone could feature curved glass, ultra-thin bezels and two larger display sizes. Under-display Face ID could reduce the camera cutout. See our iPhone 19 or 20 rumors – because one thing nobody is sure about is whether Apple will skip 19 like it skipped 9 with the arrival of the iPhone X. 
iPhone Duo 2
September, possible
Apple’s second-generation iPhone Duo could arrive in fall 2027, with Face ID and an Action button among the reported priorities.
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has a prototype with Face ID hardware. More substantial changes, including a telephoto camera and a thinner, lighter design, reportedly remain longer-term goals and not arrive until 2028 or later. 
Should you buy an iPhone now or wait? 
If you need an iPhone now, compare current models with discounted older stock and refurbished alternatives. If your existing phone still meets your needs and you’re considering a standard or lower-cost model, waiting for the rumored spring 2027 launches may give you more choice. See our guide to When is the best time to buy an iPhone.






Which new iPads are coming in 2027?
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman expects Apple to announce the next entry-level iPad in February or March 2027. The OLED iPad Air and updated iPad Pro could follow later in the first half of the year. 

				
					

				
			
Screenshot

Foundry




iPad (12th generation)
February or March 2027
When Apple updated the standard iPad in March 2025, the biggest disappointment was its A16 chip, which doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. The next model is expected to address that with an A18 or A19 chip, bringing Apple’s AI features to its entry-level tablet.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman previously predicted a 2026 launch but now expects the new iPad in the first quarter of 2027 at the earliest. Read more in our new iPad rumor roundup.
iPad Air
First half of 2027 rumored, may be later than iPad 
The next iPad Air could gain an OLED display, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. That would make screen quality a potentially significant part of this update, alongside any processor improvements.
iPad Pro
First half of 2027 rumored, may be later than iPad 
Gurman also expects a faster iPad Pro with vapor-chamber cooling. The cooling system could help manage heat during gaming and demanding AI tasks. 
Apple Pencil USB-C and Pro
Apple is reportedly preparing updated versions of both the Apple Pencil USB-C and Apple Pencil Pro for early 2027, potentially alongside new iPads. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has suggested that changes could include batteries that are easier to replace.
Should you buy now or wait? 
If you’re after the cheapest iPad and can wait, hold off until early 2027 when a new model is expected, unless you find a good deal. The M4 iPad Air and M5 iPad Pro are both due an update in the first half of 2026, but we still consider them worth buying at a good price if you need one now. We also recommend buying from Apple’s Refurbished Store if you want a bargain. Read: Should I buy an iPad now or wait?






Which new Macs are coming in 2027?
Apple’s two most affordable laptops could be first in line for a Mac update in 2027. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is targeting February or March for an M6 MacBook Air and a second-generation MacBook Neo. 
MacBook Air with M6 
February or March 2027
Now that the MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac mini have the M6 chip, it’s only a matter of time before the MacBook Air gets its processor upgrade. 
MacBook Neo 2
February or March 2027
Currently, the MacBook Neo is powered by the A18 Pro chip. We expect it will get an upgrade to the A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip.
A larger iMac

				
					

				
			The iMac Pro with its large display and powerful processor is missed. 
Apple




Apple has launched the M6 iMac, but could there be something bigger coming? Reports suggest Apple has explored a new iMac Pro with a 32-inch mini-LED display. Pro-level performance is rumored, with more powerful chips and greater memory capacity than the standard model.
Read about the larger iMac rumors.
Should you buy now or wait? 
With the prices of Macs increasing in June due to the global RAM shortages you may want to hold off buying one now. If you are going to pay more at least get the most up-to-date model, or buy from Apple’s Refurbished Store to get a bargain. Read the following for more guidance:
Should you buy the MacBook Pro now or wait? 
Should you buy the MacBook Air now or wait?
Should you buy a Mac mini now or wait?
Should you buy a Mac Studio now or wait?






New Apple Watches coming in 2027
So far we only have a limited picture of Apple Watch plans for 2027: no specific 2027 models or confirmed features are identified. 

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




Apple Watch Series 13
Fall 2027
The Apple Watch Series 13 could get a redesign in what is rumored to be one of the biggest Apple Watch upgrades in years. As well as a new design, a new way to attach bands, and a better display, we could see improved health sensors. 
Apple Watch SE 4
Fall 2027
With no new Apple Watch in 2026, an update in 2027 seems likely based on Apple’s historical two-to-three-year upgrade cycle. 






New AirPods coming in 2027

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods with a camera?
According to a brief update in Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter for Bloomberg in August, Apple is aiming to launch camera-equipped AirPods.
The new earbuds are expected to resemble the AirPods Pro 3, although it’s not yet clear whether they will also include a heart rate sensor.
The cameras are said to include both visible-light and infrared sensors, but they reportedly won’t be designed for taking photos or recording video, as their placement and image quality would make them unsuitable for those tasks. Instead, the cameras are expected to enable AI-powered features, such as hand gesture recognition, adapting audio based on the surrounding environment, and detecting whether someone is speaking directly to you or simply talking nearby.
Wondering whether to buy AirPods? Read Should I buy AirPods now and our AirPods buying guide. 






Software updates
Apple released iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 and its other major updates in September 2026, introducing Siri AI, expanded Apple Intelligence features, new parental controls and app improvements. Further point updates will bring additional features, refinements and bug fixes.
For current features, availability and forthcoming additions, see our macOS 27 and iOS 27 guides. Our separate  latest iOS beta and latest macOS beta guides track testing of future updates.
Siri and Apple Intelligence
Siri AI brings more natural conversations, personal-context and onscreen awareness, and more actions across apps. Not every promised Siri AI feature was available at launch. 
October’s 27.2 updates added French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish alongside English. Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese are due by year-end. In the EU, Siri AI is available on macOS but remains unavailable on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS.
Availability depends on device, language and region, and some users may need to join a waiting list.
iOS 28, iPadOS 28, macOS 28
Apple is expected to preview its next major operating systems at WWDC in June 2027, followed by summer beta testing and public releases in the fall.






Apple smart-home products coming in 2027 and beyond
In October 2026 Apple announced a major expansion of its smart-home lineup with the launch of the HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K and the Apple Home Collection at its “Welcome Home” experience. We are still waiting for the update to the larger HomePod, with hope that could arrive in 2027.

				
					

				
			
Screenshot

Foundry




HomePod 3
Expected: 2027 
The HomePod mini was updated in 2026, but not the larger HomePod. The reason for the delay may be that a more advanced HomePod speaker featuring a built-in display is coming. 
HomeView Ultra
Possible release: Late 2027 at the earliest, potentially 2028, according to The Information.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is developing a higher-end HomeView, codenamed J595, with a 9-inch display mounted on a motorized arm. The screen could rotate through 360 degrees and automatically turn toward whoever is speaking.
A November 2 report from The Information suggests the device could cost around $1,000 and arrive in late 2027 at the earliest, although its launch could slip into 2028. Development of its autonomous AI features reportedly remains a constraint, with Apple still deciding which capabilities to include in the first-generation model. Cameras and sensors could allow it to respond to its surroundings – for example, turning on lights when someone enters a room.
This would be a separate, more advanced model than the 7-inch HomeView announced in October 2026. Apple has not announced the device, and “HomeView Max” and “HomeView Ultra” remain speculative names. Read more about the HomeView Ultra here: ‘HomeView Ultra’ with robot arm may be coming next year






Upcoming Vision devices, AR and spatial computing
Apple Smart Glasses 
Possible June 2027 launch, shipping by end of 2027
Apple could unveil its first smart glasses at WWDC in June 2027, with shipments following before the end of the year, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. However, software development is reportedly running behind, so delays remain possible.
The first-generation glasses are expected to combine cameras, speakers and Siri-powered features, including Visual Intelligence and voice-controlled actions in apps. They reportedly won’t have a display for overlaying digital information on the wearer’s surroundings. Multiple frame styles and colors are also being developed.
Vision Pro
Possible 2028 update
Prior to 2026, Apple’s spatial computing strategy has focused on the high-end market, but reports indicate a more affordable version of the headset is in development. Apple has reportedly paused work on a successor to the high-end Vision Pro and could instead release a cheaper Vision Pro.






Apple products announced in 2026
Here is what Apple has announced in 2026:

And… RIP Mac Pro: Apple has confirmed that it is discontinuing its tower workstation.

title: Not even AI can make this stuff up
content:
Macworld





Hey, let’s take a break from AI. I know that will disappoint you, but surely there’s something else we can talk about.
Anything.
How about upcoming products? That sounds fun.
“Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as C.E.O.”
…



Nnn-nnn. Nope. No.
How about that upcoming anniversary iPhone?! What is the deal with that?!
A prominent leaker by the name of Ice Universe on Weibo says Apple is testing two designs, with two sizes for each.
Just remember, Apple recommends that you buy eight of them. Four to use and four to keep mint in the box.
As for the source of that rumor…Ice Universe? That’s not a rumor source. That’s an alternate reality from “Dark Matter”.
One wonders what the 20th anniversary iPhone will look-
“Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as C.E.O.”
Stop that!

				
					

				
			
If you’d like to receive regular news and updates to your inbox, sign up for our newsletters, including The Macalope and Apple Breakfast, David Price’s weekly, bite-sized roundup of all the latest Apple news and rumors.

Foundry




ONEWONDERSWHATITWILLLOOKLIKE.
One design has a flat back, the other has a curved-glass back. 
The last design is described as “breaktastic”.
 Apple has been refining the curve of that model over time, but it’s not clear which one will go into production.
Unlike, say, Megan Thee Stallion, who could no sooner ramp back ambitions with the curvature than she could stop breathing.
Since Apple has moved the release of the base iPhones to spring, the first six months of the calendar year are now the months for “the rest of us”.
“MacBook Neo 2 likely to launch around March, could feature new colors: report”
New colors?! That’s excit-
“Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as C.E.O.”
Grrrrrrr…
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple’s “budget” products–the base model iPhone 18s, the iPhone 18e, and the MacBook Neo–will launch around the February to March timeframe. The Neo’s colors are expected to be refreshed “frequently,” but it’s unknown if that means in the upcoming second iteration or just in the years following when you, personally, bought one in an older, boring color.
“Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as C.E.O.”
Nnnnnnnnnnnnnn…
Hey, you know what one of the biggest questions is in technology today: what the heck is “Infinity Vision” anyway? Let’s take a look-
“Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as C.E.O.”
OK, FINE, WE’LL TALK ABOUT AI, OMG.
Ugh. So angry.
“Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as C.E.O.”
Boy, it seems like it was just two weeks ago that the Macalope was saying accountability was for the little people. Oh, it was just two weeks ago! While you may hate lack of accountability, you have to admire its speed.
Someone who apparently agrees with the view that rich people should be untouchable is serial smarmist and president of The Club for Men Who Look Like a Possessed Ventriloquist’s Dummy, Jason Calacanis. Calacanis claimed Huang couldn’t be guilty of these charges because “there is no way one of the richest people on the planet … would ever commit treason.”
EVER. CASE CLOSED.
MS NOW host Stephanie Ruhle had the perfect retort.
“One of the reasons he may be one of the richest people on the planet is because he was committing treason,”…
Zing. Calacanis, however, was undeterred. See, he is also rich, so he can’t be wrong about something! Psh. Ha-ha. Don’t be silly.
“I think he is obviously not guilty on any of these charges…”
You sure about that, techbro?
“U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair”
The CEO of a firm at the heart of the AI industry being involved with a suspected agent of a foreign power forbidden by U.S. export law to receive its technology is very disturbing. Surely this is a matter of the gravest concern to those at the highest levels of our govern-
“Trump Is Said to Have Directed Effort to Reinstate Nvidia Chief”
OK. OK. Of course. That… just… Yep.
Well, he just likes the guy, right? There’s not other reas-
“Trump bought Nvidia, Palantir, SpaceX in September as federal deals, White House ties grew”
…



Say, are there any jobs for a sarcastic human/Mac/antelope hybrid outside of the tech field? Or just off-planet entirely? How does one set up an Indeed search for openings in the off-world colonies?
See, the thing is, it increasingly feels like everything going on in tech makes it clear that tech itself is no longer for us. It’s for them. Products like AI are picked because they leverage existing relationships; they’re designed solely to further enrich the same cadre of already extremely wealthy people and are shoved into every conceivable use case, whether warranted or not, simply to generate volume and unearned legitimacy.
Please, Apple, the Macalope feels like a broken record, but he is begging you: Do not become an AI firm.

If you’re looking for a mouse for a Mac or MacBook, you’ve got plenty of options beyond Apple’s Magic Mouse.
These days most mice will work on either Mac or PC, so you’ve got access to just about the entire PC mouse market, from wired to wireless, trackpads to trackballs, and even over-the-top dedicated gaming mice. The more sophisticated mice require software, so ensure that the settings app works on a Mac. All the mice tested here that have Settings apps are Mac-compatible.
A lot of people prefer using a mouse to their laptop’s trackpad. A mouse makes things much easier and just feels more comfortable and familiar. But for some people mice can be an ergonomic nightmare, so luckily there are alternatives.
Beware of the cheapest wireless mice out there. Many require a nano receiver to plug into an old-school USB-A port on the computer, and newer MacBooks have just one or two USB-C/Thunderbolt ports instead. Ideally, you’ll want a Bluetooth-compatible mouse to connect wirelessly to a MacBook or Mac.
If you’re trying to get the hang of your Apple-friendly mouse, you may want to know how to right-click on a Mac. We also have a round up of the Best Keyboards for Mac.
Best Mice to use with MacBook or Mac 
We’ve rounded up our favorite Mac mice below, starting with Apple and moving to ultra-productive mice with multiple buttons and scroll wheels, gaming mice and trackpads, and ultra-ergonomic solutions. Whether you want a basic spare or travel mouse, we’ve tested the best Mac mice we can find. 
While we love Apple’s Magic Mice there are some better options that will probably better meet your needs – we discuss how to pick the best mouse for your Mac at the bottom of this article. For example, the Logitech MX Master 4, features a comfortable ergonomic design, two scroll wheels, multiple programmable buttons, and haptic feedback technology. 
If you prioritize wrist comfort, the Logitech Lift is designed with a 57-degree vertical angle to place your hand in a natural handshake position, which helps reduce strain. 
Known for its gaming gear, Razer also offers a compelling productivity mouse called the Pro Click 2. It features a comfortable design and programmable buttons. 
And for those who are always on the move with their MacBook, the ESR MagMouse offers a unique solution. It’s a lightweight, capable wireless mouse that can magnetically attach to an adhesive base stuck to your laptop, making it harder to lose or drop. Read on for our Mac mice reviews and buying guide. 
Below this chart of the best Mac mice, we look in more details about how to pick the right mouse for your Mac.

Like it or not, the Apple Magic Mouse is the mouse that all others have to square up to in the battle to find the best mouse for Mac users. Unchanged since 2015 (aside from an update to USB-C from Lightning in 2024) and in reality little changed since 2009, the Magic Mouse is what Apple ships with every iMac (in seven accented colors) and Mac Pro (black) and one of only two mice you can buy as a separate on the Apple Store (in black or white).
The Magic Mouse is sleek and elegant, the way an Apple product should be. There are no old-fashioned buttons or scroll-wheels to spoil the mouse’s streamlined design, as the entire top multi-touch surface panel acts like a small, touch-sensitive trackpad. It works really well and cleverly combines the fluidity of a trackpad with the physicality of a mouse.
Some mice have scroll wheels that can be noisy, but the Apple Magic Mouse’s trackpad top is silent in that regard.
The low-profile design won’t suit people with larger hands, but the touch controls do work very well, allowing you to scroll both horizontally and vertically simply by flicking your finger in the required direction.
You can set up a secondary button, rather than settle for the all-over click, on either side within the Mouse tab in your Mac’s System Settings.
Where the Magic Mouse stands out of the nest of Mac mice, is gestures. You can control gestures, such as zooming and switching between applications and pages, by using the Mouse Preferences panel on the Mac. Double-tap with two fingers to launch the Mac’s Mission Control. In Settings you can also turn on Pointer Acceleration for faster or more precise mouse movements.
The button-free design also means that the Magic Mouse is suitable for both left- and right-handed users—unlike the Logitech MX Master 3S mouse reviewed below.
The rechargeable battery lasts for only about a month at a time—which would be fine if it weren’t for one thing… Apple did finally get around to switching the Lightning connector to a USB-C connector for charging the internal battery, but it is still on the base of the mouse, which means that you can’t use the mouse while it’s charging, as you have to flip it over on to its side in order to insert the cable.
Apple also sells a black version of the Magic Mouse for an extra $20/£20, which is a bit cheeky as no other mouse manufacturer charges more for color choices.

Apple’s Magic Mouse is what iMac users get in the box with their new computer. It’s a fine mouse but is rather limited with just two buttons. Logitech’s MX Master 4 mouse has eight buttons. The latest 2025 version updates 2022’s MX Master 3S in subtle ways, with new haptic feedback technology (just for Adobe users right now), an Action Ring, and longer battery life.
Note that there is the “Logitech MX Master 4” and a version called the “MX Master 4 For Mac”. Either works just fine with the Mac. The Mac version is priced the same but doesn’t come with the USB-C Bolt receiver that is bundled with the plain version. Some prefer using the longer-range and more secure USB receiver—which is aimed at busy office environments where there may be lots of Bluetooth devices in use all together—so buy the standard rather than “For Mac” version if this fits your situation. The USB dongle is now thankfully USB-C rather than legacy USB-A but it will take up a Thunderbolt port on your Mac or docking station.
Its smoothly curved surface fits the palm of the (right) hand very well, along with a thumb-rest for extra comfort. It has the usual left/right buttons and a scroll wheel at the top. The scroll-wheel works in two different modes, with a feature called SmartShift that automatically switches the scroll wheel from line-by-line scrolling to super-fast scrolling when it senses you want to scroll much faster.
There’s also a second scroll wheel on the side, which allows you to scroll horizontally—which is great for photo-editing and graphics work plus very long spreadsheets—and three more buttons that can be programmed using the excellent Options+ app.
The MX Master 4 has the same 8,000dpi sensor and high-speed scrolling wheel as its predecessor, but includes a new processor and an antenna inside the mouse that provide a more reliable wireless connection. The outer casing of the mouse uses a more robust, stain-resistant coating, and the thumb rest is larger to accommodate the new haptic feedback features.
The “For Mac” version comes two differently named although startlingly similar colors—Space Black and White Silver—to the plain MX Master 4’s Graphite and Pale Gray.

Its trackpad-like features—via the dedicated INFTYLAB Glide software—rely on configurable scrolling and button shortcuts rather than full Multi-Touch gestures, so don’t expect the same experience as using a MacBook trackpad but it’s an interesting approach that’s combined with a compact ergonomic design.
You can customize scroll modes and map shortcut buttons; for example, making the scroll direction match your Mac trackpad. Choose “Natural” in the Glide desktop app for traditional mouse scrolling, where moving the mouse’s top scroll wheel down pulls the page content down with your fingers—mimicking the direct, touch-like feel of a MacBook trackpad. The Logitech Mobi Fold is a lightweight, foldable mouse built for travellers, offering excellent portability and month-long battery life. Its main compromise is comfort, as the slim design feels less substantial than a full-sized productivity mouse.
Microsoft is probably giving the side-eye to Logitech’s new Mobi Fold right now, as it looks very similar to Microsoft’s Arc mouse, with a slimline, lightweight design that is very much intended for portable use when travelling with a laptop. But, of course, most mice share the same basic design, so that’s hardly a major criticism.
Rather than the bulkier design of a conventional mouse, that allows you to grip the entire body of the mouse in the palm of your hand, the Mobi Fold—like the Arc—consists of a thin slab of plastic that curves upward to fit your palm. The body of the Mobi Fold measures just 11mm thick although, as mentioned, it curves upwards so that it stands 33mm high, 57mm wide and 122mm long when in use. However, you can also fold it in half and quickly slip it into a jacket pocket or bag when you’re travelling (and that is different to the Arc, which simply lies flat when it’s not in use).
As you’d expect, the Mobi Fold has Left and Right buttons on its top panel, but instead of a scrolling wheel—which wouldn’t work with the Mobi’s folding design—there’s a small trackpad sitting between these buttons that allows you to scroll through documents by sliding your finger instead. The mouse Settings panel in macOS does allow you to switch the Left and Right buttons, which means that—unlike the MX Master—the Mobi Fold is suitable for left-handed MacBook users as well.
Battery life is good too, with the Mobi’s rechargeable battery lasting for a full month when fully charged, while a quick one-minute charge gives you around 22 hours of use. The USB-C charging port is on the rear edge of the mouse, though, which means that your charging cable will sit under your wrist when it’s charging—which is almost as bad as having the charging port underneath, as is the case with Apple’s Magic Mouse. There’s no cable included either, so you’ll need to provide your own USB-C cable for charging.
I do prefer the larger, more solid feel of Logitech’s MX Master mouse when I’m working in the office with my desktop Mac, but if you want a compact, lightweight mouse that you can carry around with your MacBook then the Mobi Fold could be just what you’re looking for.

The Razer Viper V4 Pro is a premium, ultra-light, wireless gaming mouse designed for serious gamers who prioritise speed, precision, and customisation. While it is expensive at $159.99/£159.99, it delivers high-end performance that makes it one of the strongest gaming mouse options currently available for Mac users.
At its core, the Viper V4 Pro is built for competitive gaming. It features an ultra-lightweight design of just 49–50g, a highly accurate 50,000 DPI optical sensor, an 8,000Hz polling rate, and an extremely low latency of 0.204ms. These specifications translate into fast, responsive performance and excellent accuracy, making it ideal for fast-paced games where every movement matters. Despite its lightweight construction, the mouse feels durable, with switches rated for up to 100 million clicks and an optical scroll wheel designed to be more reliable than traditional mechanical alternatives.
The mouse is aimed primarily at dedicated gamers, but it may also appeal to power users and creative professionals thanks to its programmable buttons and extensive customisation options through Razer’s Synapse software. The Mac version of Synapse remains in beta and is more complicated than rival software such as Logitech Options+, but it allows users to create shortcuts and custom commands for productivity applications as well as games.
However, there are several compromises. The most significant is the high price, which places it well above mainstream alternatives from Logitech and Apple. Connectivity is also more restrictive than many rivals, as there is no Bluetooth support. Instead, users must rely on Razer’s proprietary HyperSpeed wireless dongle or a wired USB connection. The included cable uses USB-A, which may require an adaptor for many modern Macs. In addition, the design is right-handed only.  
Portability is excellent thanks to the mouse’s extremely low weight, although users will need to carry the wireless dongle when travelling. Battery life is impressive, lasting around 45 hours at maximum performance settings and up to 180 hours with lower sensitivity and polling-rate settings.
Overall, the Viper V4 Pro is an outstanding gaming mouse for serious gamers, but its price, lack of Bluetooth, and right-handed-only design make it difficult to justify for casual users.

The myAir.0 OriMouse is one of the most innovative computer mice available today, combining a full-size working mouse with an ultra-portable foldable design. At just 5mm thick when folded and weighing less than 40g, it is arguably the most travel-friendly mouse on the market. Using an origami-inspired structure and magnetic closure, it folds completely flat for storage in a jacket pocket, laptop sleeve, or alongside a tablet, then quickly snaps into shape when needed.
The OriMouse is designed primarily for frequent travellers, remote workers, and anyone who values portability above all else. Its unique appearance is also likely to appeal to users who enjoy distinctive, conversation-starting tech accessories. However, it may not suit power users, gamers, or productivity-focused professionals who rely on advanced features such as horizontal scrolling, ultra-high precision sensors, or traditional scroll wheels.
In use, the mouse feels surprisingly comfortable despite its lightweight construction. It features standard left and right-click buttons, while scrolling is handled by a touch-sensitive pad rather than a physical wheel. This is the biggest adjustment users will need to make, as the scrolling experience requires a gentler, trackpad-like motion that may feel unfamiliar at first. While some users may eventually prefer it, others will miss the precision and familiarity of a conventional scroll wheel.
Performance is solid when used on a mouse pad, thanks to its 4000dpi infrared sensor, although it is less impressive on reflective desk surfaces. The unusual design also offers good durability, with the lightweight construction making it less vulnerable to damage if dropped.
Battery life is another strength. The rechargeable battery is claimed to last up to three months between charges via USB-C, outperforming competitors such as Apple’s Magic Mouse and Logitech’s MX Master series. It can also be used while charging.
Overall, the OriMouse is a highly original product that prioritises portability above all else. The key compromise is adapting to its touch-sensitive scrolling and accepting fewer productivity-focused features. As well as being Mac-compatible, the HP 715 Multi-Device Mouse is well designed, versatile and provides good value for money.
The HP 715 mouse is quite compact, so you can easily carry it around with a laptop. I found it a little small compared to the chunky Logitech mouse that I normally use, but that’s a matter of personal taste. And, despite the compact design, the HP 715 manages to find room for lots of useful features, including left/right mouse buttons, and two thumb buttons on the left-hand side of the mouse (which seem mostly suitable for right-handed people).
We reviewed this mouse alongside the HP 975 Keyboard here: HP 975 Keyboard and 715 Mouse review, both of which work with the HPAC app (HP Accessory Centre). It’s good to see HP extending its support for the Mac, including full Mac-compatibility for its HPAC app.
Like the HP 975 keyboard, the mouse can be paired with two devices using Bluetooth, and a third device using the USB-A dongle included with the mouse (you may need an adaptor). 
There’s a clickable scroll wheel that can scroll both horizontally and vertically. You can use the HPAC app to reprogram the buttons and scrolling wheel functions – although you’ll need to do a bit of experimenting to make the most of the mouse’s many features.
The mouse should last for around three months when fully charged, and HP says that a quick one-minute charge will give you up to three hours of battery life.
How to pick the right mouse for your Mac 
When choosing a mouse for your Mac, you have a wide array of options that extend far beyond Apple’s own offerings. Most mice on the market today are compatible with both Mac and PC, but there are several key factors to consider to ensure you find the perfect fit for your needs. 
Connectivity: Most modern mice connect wirelessly, but it’s important to check how. Many cheaper wireless mice use a small USB-A receiver, which can be an issue for newer MacBooks that only have USB-C ports. For the most seamless experience with a MacBook, a mouse with Bluetooth compatibility is ideal. Some high-end mice offer both Bluetooth and a dedicated USB receiver, which can provide a more stable connection in crowded wireless environments. 
Software and Customization: More advanced mice often come with software to customize buttons and settings. It’s crucial to confirm that this software is compatible with macOS, especially with recent versions and Apple Silicon chips. Companies like Logitech and Razer have made efforts to provide Mac-compatible apps, allowing users to reprogram buttons, create app-specific profiles, and adjust sensitivity. For mice without official Mac software, third-party apps like Mac Mouse Fix can sometimes restore functionality for extra buttons.
Sensitivity: Changing your mouse’s sensitivity can be a beneficial function. Dots per inch (dpi) dictates cursor speed. A less sensitive mouse (400-1000dpi) helps with tasks that require precise cursor movements, such as photo/video editing. A more sensitive mouse (1200dpi and higher) can reduce the effort needed to move a cursor across several screens, useful for high-resolution monitors.
Ergonomics & Comfort: Comfort is a major reason to switch from a trackpad or even Apple’s Magic Mouse, which some users find uncomfortable due to its low profile. Ergonomic mice are designed to fit more naturally in your hand, reducing strain. Some models, like the Logitech Lift, feature a “handshake” position to improve wrist posture. However, be aware that many ergonomic designs are for right-handed users only.
Features and Productivity: A third-party mouse can significantly boost your productivity with features that Apple’s mouse lacks. Look for models with multiple programmable buttons, which can be set up for tasks like navigating web pages (Forward/Back) or launching Mission Control. Some mice, like the Logitech MX Master series, include a second scroll wheel for horizontal scrolling, which is invaluable for working with spreadsheets or wide documents.
Ultimately, the best mouse is a personal choice that depends on your workflow, comfort, and budget. By considering connectivity, software support, and the specific features you need, you can find a mouse that will make your Mac experience more efficient and enjoyable.

Apple’s MacBooks are great, but—as with all laptops—using one isn’t that great for your back or neck. Continual bowing of the head to see a screen can lead to a stiff neck and what doctors scarily call spinal stenosis, which can compress blood vessels and displace nerves—cutting off blood supply to the brain. That’s not a good thing.
Your screen should be at a comfortable height that doesn’t make you bend your neck down to see it. Try to make sure your eyes are in line with the screen while sitting with a straight back. This also helps when making video calls, so the other people aren’t staring up your nostrils. 
Using a laptop stand also makes using a separate keyboard and mouse much easier. See our roundups of the best Mac keyboards and best Mac mouse. And, after use, you can hide away your keyboard under the raised stand on certain models.
Some stands raise the laptop to eye level, and others—known as “vertical” or “closed” stands—just keep the MacBook closed for minimal desk disruption if you have connected external displays to increase your screen size—learn how to set up a second screen for a Mac.
The eye-level, open laptop stands are more ergonomic, raising the MacBook screen so that you are not straining your neck muscles, shoulders and back. It should also reduce screen glare, which means less eye strain and fewer headaches. On such a stand, the MacBook’s webcam will also be at a more natural level with your head, meaning less video calls with people looking up your nose or down on your head.
Buy a vertical/closed laptop stand to keep your desk tidy and free up space for other stuff—be that a charger for your iPhone, backup hard disk, or a cup of coffee.
Both types of stand should also raise the laptop, raising it off the desk and keeping it cooler. If a laptop gets too hot, its performance is likely to suffer.
A laptop stand also works nicely with a MacBook docking station, which can multiply the number of ports and slots available to you and allow for multiple larger displays. Some stands even have their own integrated USB-C hub, which is a very clever addition.

title: OpenAI Brings GPT-6.2 Sol to ChatGPT's Chat Tab
content:

Compared with GPT–6, GPT–6.2 Sol does a better job detecting fine details in photos, like symbols on a sign or text on a label. It has improved at choosing options online based on the user's priorities, and it is smarter about when to offer a follow-up after a conversation, such as an alert about a price drop.

The model meets OpenAI's safety policies in challenging conversations 91 to 94 percent of the time, up from 77 to 80 percent for GPT–6.

title: Google Search Gets Wallet Access, With Drive Coming Soon
content:
Google today said it is making Search "more tailored" with support for connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode.


According to Google, AI Mode will be able to map financial milestones, find ways to trim spending, and get the most from credit card benefits. The feature can read information from accounts included in Google Wallet, but it can't move, manage, or invest money.

In the coming weeks, Google plans to add connections for Google Drive and Gemini to Google Search. Google Drive will give Search access to docs, sheets, PDFs, and more, with search responses that take into account personal information.

Gemini integration will let both the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search share context and content. Google says if you ask the Gemini app something, AI Mode will "have that foundation to build on." With today's announcement, Google says you'll start seeing more personally relevant responses based on recent search context in both AI Mode and AI Overviews. Responses that use your personal data will soon have a "Personalization" icon below them to let you see what data was used.
