1.
What’s best, MacBook Air or MacBook Pro?
We explore this question in detail in our MacBook Air vs MacBook Pro comparison. The MacBook Air is the best choice for most people, offering enough performance for everyday work, studying and many creative tasks. The MacBook Pro is worth considering if you need sustained performance for demanding workloads, more ports or a more advanced display.
The entry-level MacBook Air costs $1,299/£1,299, although you can often spend less by shopping around – we regularly round up the best MacBook Air deals. If you want more screen space without paying for professional-level performance, the 15-inch MacBook Air is considerably cheaper than a 14-inch MacBook Pro.
Within the MacBook Pro range, the standard 14-inch M6 model provides a middle ground between the Air and the more expensive M5 Pro and M5 Max configurations. Its fan helps maintain performance during longer processing tasks, while its Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI port and SDXC card slot add flexibility.
The M5 Pro and M5 Max models suit more demanding professional workloads, offering more CPU and GPU cores, higher memory capacities and Thunderbolt 5. M5 Pro is a strong option for software development, photography and video editing. Consider M5 Max if your work benefits from its additional graphics power, media engines or higher memory ceiling; spending more won’t necessarily make everyday tasks noticeably faster.
You can also choose a MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR touchscreen. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, these models add an OLED display, touch controls alongside the keyboard and trackpad, Dynamic Island, and a thinner, lighter design. Starting at $2,899/£2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399/£3,399 for the 16-inch, they cost $400/£400 more than equivalent non-touch M5 Pro models. They use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chip families, so the main reasons to pay extra are the display, portability and touch input.
Choosing between a 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro comes down to workspace, portability, battery life and price. The larger model gives you more room for editing timelines, coding and multitasking, while the 14-inch is easier to carry. Both sizes offer powerful Pro and Max configurations. For external monitors, current M5 Pro models support up to three displays and M5 Max models support up to four, depending on resolution and refresh rate.
For a tighter budget, the MacBook Neo lowers the starting price of a Mac laptop to $699/£699. It’s worth comparing its compromises with a discounted previous-generation MacBook Air before deciding.





2.
Should I upgrade from my Intel Mac?
Yes. It’s time! We are now more than six years into Apple’s transition from Intel processors to its own silicon that includes CPU, GPU, and unified memory. The transition began with the introduction of the M1 in November 2020. Since June 2023 every Mac Apple sells uses Apple’s own chips rather than Intel processors.
If you’ve yet to upgrade your Intel Mac to one powered by Apple’s silicon what are you waiting for? If you are concerned that a must-have app doesn’t run on an M-series Mac, consider finding a new app because the performance gains are tremendous.
Another good reason to replace an Intel Mac is that Apple’s support for these models is winding down. macOS Golden Gate, released in September 2026, is the first major version of macOS to support no Intel Macs. Intel Macs compatible with older versions of macOS may continue receiving security updates for a limited period, but they are now outside Apple’s current feature-release cycle. Apple does not guarantee how long those updates will continue, and machines limited to macOS Sequoia are likely to lose support sooner than those capable of running macOS Tahoe. Read: How long does Apple support Macs.





3.
Where can I get the best price for a new Mac?
Apple rarely offers direct price cuts on new hardware, but resellers frequently do. Getting the best price on a new Mac requires knowing where to look and when to buy: 
Top U.S. Retailers:
Amazon: Often has the lowest prices, especially during events like Prime Day. For example, during the July 2026 Prime Day event, a 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro was available for $1,749, a $450 discount. Even outside of events, Amazon frequently undercuts Apple’s MSRP.
Best Buy: A reliable source for discounts and trade-in offers. In late 2025, Best Buy offered a massive $1,150 off an M2 Ultra Mac Studio.
B&H Photo: A well-regarded authorized reseller that often has competitive pricing on Macs.
Walmart: Known for exclusive deals on older models, like the M1 MacBook Air, which has been sold brand-new for just $599.
Top U.K. Retailers:
Amazon UK: Similar to the U.S., Amazon UK is a primary source for discounts.
KRCS: An Apple Premium Reseller that frequently offers good deals.
John Lewis & Currys: Reliable high-street retailers that often have competitive prices and good customer service.
If you’re looking for a great offer, visit our Best Apple Deals page which is regularly updated.





4.
What specs do I really need for my Mac?
Chip: The specs you need depend on what you plan to do with your Mac. For web browsing, email, office apps and light photo editing, a standard M-series chip is more than sufficient. The M6 is available in the Mac mini, iMac and standard 14-inch MacBook Pro, while the MacBook Air uses M5. The budget MacBook Neo uses an A18 Pro chip. A newer generation number doesn’t automatically make a chip better for every workload: compare its CPU, GPU, memory and capabilities with what your apps actually need. 
If you regularly work with complex spreadsheets, large Photoshop files, audio projects, video editing or more demanding games, look at a Pro chip. The M5 Pro Mac mini, for example, offers up to an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU and up to 64GB unified memory.
A Max chip is worth considering for demanding graphics, complex 3D work, high-resolution video production or projects that need more memory than a Pro configuration supports. Many developers, photographers and video editors will be well served by a Pro chip. The M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU, up to a 40-core GPU and up to 128GB unified memory, depending on configuration. 
The M5 Ultra, with up to a 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU and 512GB unified memory, is aimed at the most extreme workloads, including VFX, scientific computing and running very large AI models locally.
GPU: One of the biggest differences between Apple’s chips is GPU performance. Standard M-series chips are easily sufficient for everyday graphics, casual gaming and light creative work. Pro chips add considerably more GPU power for video editing, graphics work, 3D applications and gaming. Max chips are designed for professional graphics, high-resolution video and demanding 3D workflows, while Ultra provides Apple’s highest GPU performance. The M5 Max offers up to 40 GPU cores, while the M5 Ultra doubles that to 80 GPU cores. Both also have Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core to speed up AI workloads.
RAM: Apple calls RAM Unified Memory. The MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB, which is probably the biggest drawback of that machine. Most Macs start with at least 16GB, which is plenty for everyday use, although we recommend choosing more if your budget allows because the memory cannot be upgraded later. 24GB or 32GB is a good choice for heavier multitasking, photo editing, podcasting, moderate video production and gaming. Developers and professional creative users may benefit from 48GB, 64GB or more. The new M5 Pro Mac mini can be configured with up to 64GB, M5 Max Mac Studio with up to 128GB, and M5 Ultra Mac Studio with an enormous 512GB.
Storage: Even with iCloud and external drives available, it can seem like you can never have enough storage inside your Mac. 256GB may be sufficient for basic web and office use, but it can fill up quickly. We recommend 512GB for most people who want to keep a Mac for several years, particularly if you store photos, games or media locally. For regular video or audio production, 1TB or more is preferable. Professional users may need several terabytes. The M5 Pro Mac mini offers up to 8TB, while the M5 Ultra Mac Studio and touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro offer up to 16TB. Maximum capacity varies by model and chip, so check the configuration you’re considering. Choose enough internal storage when ordering rather than relying on a later internal upgrade. An external SSD can add capacity for media libraries, project files and archives, often at a lower cost than Apple’s internal storage upgrades.
Display: Consider screen quality and workspace alongside processing power. The MacBook Air’s display is suitable for everyday work and many creative tasks, while MacBook Pro models add XDR brightness and ProMotion refresh rates. The PROLED XDR models also offer OLED, Adobe RGB support and touchscreen input in a lighter design. Choose them if those features will benefit how you work; they use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chip families as the non-touch versions.
For more information to help you decide which Mac to buy see our Mac processor comparison where we compare Apple silicon and Intel. We also offer advice about how much storage, RAM, and cores in How much MacBook RAM, SSD, GPU, and CPU do you really need.





5.
When were the Macs last updated?
In March 2026, Apple introduced the M5 MacBook Air, the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and M5 Max, and the new MacBook Neo. All went on sale on March 11.
On August 25, 2026, Apple announced the Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro, and the Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra. Both ranges went on sale on September 22.
On October 27, 2026, Apple announced the M6 iMac and standard 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro. The following day, it introduced the 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR displays and M5 Pro or M5 Max chips. In-store availability for these October models begins November 6.
Apple discontinued the Mac Pro in March 2026. The Mac Studio is now its highest-end desktop Mac.





Why you can trust Macworld’s advice
Macworld has been covering everything Apple related since our first issue which arrived alongside the original Mac in 1984. Nobody knows Apple better, except probably Apple, but the difference is that we are completely impartial. We are made up of a team of experts with decades of experiences with Macs and other Apple products, and between us we have reviewed every Apple product meaning we are uniquely positioned to provide buying advice.
Price increases June 2026
In June 2026, Apple increased prices significantly across several product lines including Macs, iPads, the Apple TV 4K, and HomePod models, citing an unprecedented rise in component costs. 
The company stated it had “never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly” and that it had shielded customers from these increases for as long as possible before finally raising prices. 
For Macs, prices increased from $100/£100 to $500/£500 depending on the model.
MacBook Neo is $100 more
MacBook Air is $200 more 
MacBook Pro is $300 to $500 more 
Mac mini was $200 more, but is now $300 more following the August update
Mac Studio is $500 more
Prices have been updated throughout this article.

If you need another reason to buy an Apple Watch now, the Black Friday Sales are underway with some fantastic savings on the new and old models. If the exact size and configuration you want is near its lowest recorded price, there’s no need to wait until Black Friday itself. If the model you want is still near full price, it’s worth checking again over Black Friday weekend and on Cyber Monday. If you miss those offers and aren’t in a hurry, Amazon Prime Day and other major retailer sales are usually good times to look again.
Below, we explain which Apple Watch models are worth buying now, when to wait for a better price, and how to avoid paying full price just before a new model arrives. For a closer look at the differences between models, see our Best Apple Watch guide.

Buy an Apple Watch now if…

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now on sale alongside the SE 3 and there are no new models expected. Buy now if you need a watch soon or the model you want meets your needs at a price you’re happy to pay. The Series 12 is the best everyday choice, the SE 3 is the best value, and the Ultra 4 makes sense if you need its longer battery life or outdoor features. A discounted Series 11 or Ultra 3 could also be worth buying if you don’t need the latest additions.
You should consider buying now if:
Your current Apple Watch cannot run watchOS 27, or its battery no longer lasts long enough for your needs.
You’re buying your first Apple Watch or upgrading from a much older model. The current watches offer substantial improvements in displays, performance, health tracking and battery life.
You want the Series 12 or Ultra 4’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings, and Readiness score. Live Rewind and Siri Recap are coming in iOS 27.3.
You would benefit from the Ultra 4’s up to 50-hour battery life, satellite communication or specialist outdoor features.
You need a watch before a trip or event, or you find a worthwhile discount on a model that suits you.


						

							


Don’t buy an Apple Watch now if…
Black Friday deals are already underway, so there’s no need to wait for Friday itself if the exact model you want is near its lowest recorded price. Check our best Apple Watch Black Friday deals before paying full price.
You may want to wait, keep your current watch, or choose a different model if:
Your preferred size or configuration is still near full price. Check again over Black Friday weekend and on Cyber Monday. If you’re flexible, compare the sale prices of the Series 12 and Ultra 4 with remaining Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock.
You already own a Series 10 or 11 and don’t need the new health sensors. If your current watch still meets your needs, there’s little reason to upgrade. The Series 12 has the same 24-hour battery rating as the Series 11.
You own an Ultra 3 and its battery life meets your needs. The Ultra 4’s clearest upgrade is its rated battery life of up to 50 hours, compared with 42 hours for the Ultra 3.
You’re considering an older model and want the latest watchOS features. The Series 8, SE 2, and original Ultra can’t run watchOS 27. Check compatibility before buying clearance, used, or refurbished stock.
You use an Android phone. Apple Watch requires an iPhone for setup and doesn’t pair with Android.
You’re considering the SE 3 but want advanced health features. Choose the Series 12 if you want ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring where available, or the newer Health Sensing System.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is the best choice for most people. Starting at $399/£369 – the same starting price as the Series 11 – it combines Apple’s advanced health features with a smaller, lighter design than the Ultra 4. Its new Health Sensing System measures heart rate every five seconds and heart-rate variability more frequently, providing data for a new Readiness score. The S11 chip also supports Audio Intelligence features, although Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due to arrive iOS 27.3 later in 2026. 
Apple still rates everyday battery life at up to 24 hours, the same as Series 11. The company says outdoor workout tracking lasts longer, however, and a 15-minute charge now provides up to 12 hours of use, compared with around eight hours for Series 11. 
In our review of the Apple Watch Series 12, we recorded 51 and 40 hours of battery life across two runs – an average of 45.5 hours, compared with 47.5 hours for Series 11. Charging also varied: our Series 12 watch reached 58% and 72% after 30 minutes in separate tests, falling short of Apple’s claimed 80%. While these results show that endurance can comfortably exceed Apple’s 24-hour rating, they don’t demonstrate a consistent improvement over Series 11. 
Aluminum models gain a tougher Ceramic Shield 2 display. 
Buy the Apple Watch Series 12 if:
You’re buying your first Apple Watch or upgrading from a much older model and want the best everyday option.
You want the new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements, and Readiness score.
You want advanced features missing from the SE 3, including ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring and hypertension notifications.
You prefer a lighter watch with two size choices over the larger Ultra 4.
Don’t buy the Apple Watch Series 12 if:
You own a Series 10 or 11 that still meets your needs. The new health features may not justify the cost of upgrading, and Apple’s 24-hour everyday battery rating has not changed.
You can get a Series 11 at a meaningful discount and don’t need the new health sensing or upcoming Audio Intelligence features.
You mainly want fitness tracking, notifications and basic safety features. The SE 3 costs $150/£150 less.
You prioritize longer battery life between charges, satellite communication or specialist outdoor features. Consider the Ultra 4.
Our verdict: The Series 12 is worth buying if you want Apple’s latest health sensing features in a smaller, less expensive watch than the Ultra 4. However, our review found inconsistent battery life and charging speeds, plus occasional sluggishness during testing. Owners of a Series 10 or 11 should weigh the new health features against the cost of upgrading: keeping their current watch, or buying a substantially discounted Series 11, may offer better value.

Announced in September 2025, it brought many features that were previously reserved for Apple’s premium watches, including an always-on display, temperature sensing, fast charging and the S10 chip used in the Series 11 and Ultra 3.
If you don’t need Apple’s most advanced health sensors, the SE 3 delivers almost everything that makes the Apple Watch great at a much lower price. It starts at $249 / £219, although we’ve already seen it discounted to $199 during major sales.
The SE 3 also supports Siri AI in watchOS 27 when paired with a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone. Siri AI is currently in beta and rolling out in English. Buy the Apple Watch SE 3 if:

You want the brightest display and most premium design—the SE 3 still has thicker bezels than the flagship models.
You need longer battery life. The SE 3 is rated for 18 hours, compared with 24 hours for the Series 12.
You’re happy to spend more for Apple’s most advanced health and fitness features.
Our verdict: The Apple Watch SE 3 is an outstanding budget smartwatch. Its always-on display, S10 processor, fast charging and improved health features make it a huge step up from the SE 2. Unless you specifically need ECG, blood oxygen monitoring or the longer battery life of the Series 11, the SE 3 is the Apple Watch we’d recommend to most buyers.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is Apple’s most capable watch, aimed at endurance athletes, hikers, divers and anyone who regularly spends more than a day away from a charger. It starts at $799/£749, the same starting price as the Ultra 3, and retains the 49mm titanium case, bright display, dual-frequency GPS, satellite communication and diving support. 
Battery life is the strongest reason to choose the new model. Apple rates the Ultra 4 for up to 50 hours of normal use, up from 42 hours on Ultra 3, or 84 hours in Low Power Mode, up from 72. Its new Extended Workout modes can track outdoor activity for up to 25 hours with full GPS and heart-rate readings, or up to 45 hours in Max Extended Workout mode. Like the Series 12, it gains the new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings, and a Readiness score. Its S11 chip supports Audio Intelligence, although Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due in beta later in 2026. 
Buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4 if:
You want the longest battery life available on an Apple Watch, particularly for travel, long shifts or time away from a charger.
You need extended outdoor workout tracking, precision dual-frequency GPS or satellite communication.
You hike, dive or take part in endurance sports and will use its rugged case, Action button and specialist features.
You want the new Health Sensing System in an Ultra watch and are upgrading from a substantially older model.
Don’t buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4 if:
You already own an Ultra 3 and its 42-hour battery life meets your needs. It retains many of the same outdoor features, including satellite communication and dual-frequency GPS.
You find an Ultra 3 at a substantial discount and do not need the Ultra 4’s longer battery life, new health sensing or extended workout modes.
You mainly want advanced health features in an everyday watch. The smaller Series 12 has the same new Health Sensing System and S11 chip for half the starting price.
You prefer a smaller or lighter watch. The Ultra 4’s 49mm case can feel bulky, especially for sleep tracking.
Our verdict: The Ultra 4 is worth buying if you will benefit from its 50-hour battery life, extended workout tracking or outdoor safety features. It also offers the Series 12’s new health sensing in a more rugged watch. For everyday use, the Series 12 offers better value; if you already own an Ultra 3, compare the cost of upgrading with how much its extra eight hours of rated battery life and new health features matter to you. 

							
		


Should I buy an older Apple Watch?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are now the previous-generation models and may be good buys if retailers discount them enough. Before choosing any older Apple Watch, check both its price against the current model and whether it can run watchOS 27. The Series 9 and Ultra 2 are the oldest supported Apple Watch models models in their respective ranges; the SE 3 is the only supported SE.
The following models cannot install watchOS 27, so we would generally avoid buying them unless the price is exceptionally low and you are comfortable using older software:
Apple Watch Series 6 (2020)
Apple Watch Series 7 (2021)
Apple Watch Series 8 (2022)
Apple Watch SE (2nd generation, 2022)
Apple Watch Ultra (1st generation, 2022)
Start by comparing a discounted Series 11 with the Series 12, or an Ultra 3 with the Ultra 4. The Series 11 retains the Series 12’s 24-hour everyday battery rating but lacks its new Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features. The Ultra 3 retains satellite communication and dual-frequency GPS, but its rated battery life is 42 hours rather than the Ultra 4’s 50 hours. Series 10 and Ultra 2 can offer further savings if their price and battery condition make sense; Series 9 is the oldest standard model that runs watchOS 27.
What to look for when buying an older Apple Watch
Choose an S9 chip or newer for the longest software support.
Buy refurbished if possible. Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store includes a one-year warranty, while reputable third-party refurbishers can also offer good value.
Shop during major sales. Previous-generation Apple Watches often receive their biggest discounts during Prime Day and Black Friday.
Check the battery and Activation Lock. If you’re buying used, confirm the battery is in good condition, inspect the watch for damage, and make sure Activation Lock has been removed before you buy.

When is the best time to buy an Apple Watch?
The best time to buy an Apple Watch depends on whether you want the newest model or the lowest price.
The Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now on sale, alongside the SE 3. If you want the latest model and are happy with its price, you can buy now without an imminent replacement to worry about. If getting a discount matters more, compare retailers during the expected October sales and Black Friday in November.
The September launch also makes the Series 11 and Ultra 3 worth checking. Retailers may reduce remaining stock, but compare the actual saving with the features you would give up: the Series 12 and Ultra 4 add new health sensing, while the Ultra 4 also increases rated battery life from 42 to 50 hours.
Apple kept the new models’ starting prices at $399/£369 for Series 12 and $799/£749 for Ultra 4. Individual configurations and retailer prices vary.


						

							


When shouldn’t you buy an Apple Watch?
Avoid buying an Apple Watch:
Just before Apple’s annual September event, unless you need one immediately.
At full price when a major sale is only days away, such as Prime Day or Black Friday.
Without comparing prices. Check multiple retailers and use price-tracking tools such as CamelCamelCamel to avoid inflated “sale” prices.
If you’re paying extra for cellular but don’t need it. Cellular Apple Watch typically cost around $100 more and require a monthly data plan, while the GPS model offers better value for most people.
If battery life is your top priority. Apple Watch battery life still trails some competing smartwatches, so you may prefer an alternative platform if multi-day battery life is essential.


						

							






Best time to buyWhy

Prime Day (July/October)Best deals on current-generation models.

After the September launchPrevious-generation models receive substantial discounts.
Worst time: August to early SeptemberNew Apple Watches are expected within weeks.

 






Where to find the best Apple Watch deals

				
					

				
			
IDG




Apple rarely discounts the Apple Watch itself, so the best deals are usually found at third-party retailers – we check these every month and record the best deals here: Top Apple Watch discounts & deals – Big savings on all models.
Best places to buy: Amazon is consistently one of the best places to find Apple Watch discounts, particularly during major sales. Other good options in the U.S. include Best Buy, Walmart, Target and Costco. In the U.K., check Amazon, Currys, Argos, John Lewis and KRCS.
Shop during major sales: The biggest discounts typically arrive during Amazon Prime Day (July and October) and Black Friday/Cyber Monday (November). Savings of $100–$150 on current-generation models are common. During Prime Day 2026, for example, the Apple Watch Series 11 fell to $279 ($120 off) and the Ultra 3 dropped to $649 ($150 off).
Check for education discounts: Students, teachers and education staff may qualify for discounted Apple Watch pricing through Apple’s Education Store U.S. (and Education Store U.K.). For more information read our guide to how to get a student discount at the Apple Education Store.
Tip: Before buying, compare prices across several retailers and check the recent price history with a tool such as CamelCamelCamel to make sure you’re getting a genuine deal rather than a temporary “discount” from an inflated price.


						

							


Is it worth buying a refurbished Apple Watch?
Buying a refurbished Apple Watch is another great way to save money, provided you buy from a reputable seller and choose a model that will continue to receive software updates.
Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store is the safest option. Every watch undergoes rigorous testing, cleaning and inspection, comes with a one-year warranty, includes new accessories, and is eligible for AppleCare. Apart from the plain white box, it’s difficult to tell the difference between a refurbished Apple Watch and a brand-new one. You can typically save around 15% on recent models, with even bigger discounts on older generations.
Check Apple’s U.S. Refurbished Store or U.K. Refurbished Store for current models, configurations and prices. Stock changes regularly; compare any refurbished Series 11 or Ultra 3 with the price of a new Series 12 or Ultra 4 before buying.
The best Apple Watch refurbished deals: 
Apple’s U.S. Refurbished Store often has Apple Watch Series 11, 10 and 9, SE 3, SE 2, Ultra 2 and Ultra 3.
Get a refurbished Apple Watch Series 11 for $339, $60 off
You may also find the Apple Watch Series 11, 10 and 9, SE 2, SE 3 and Ultra 3 at Apple’s U.K. Refurbished Store. 
Get a refurbished Apple Watch Series 11 for £309, £60 off
Third-party refurbishers can also offer excellent value, but quality varies. Terms such as “Excellent” or “Grade A”aren’t standardised, so always check the seller’s warranty, return policy and battery condition before buying. Be aware that Amazon Renewed devices, for example, aren’t refurbished to Apple’s standards and may not include a new battery or replacement parts.
The other key consideration is software support. Older Apple Watches eventually stop receiving new versions of watchOS, so avoid buying a model that’s nearing the end of its supported life. For the best balance of price and features, compare refurbished Series 11 and Ultra 3 models with the new generation first. Series 9, Series 10 and Ultra 2 can cost less and still run watchOS 27, but check their condition and savings carefully.
A refurbished Apple Watch can be one of the best values in Apple’s lineup – as long as you buy from a trusted seller and don’t choose a model that’s too old.
Read: Should I buy a refurbished Apple Watch? for more information.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
Should I wait for the next Apple Watch?
You do not need to wait for 2026’s launch: the Series 12 and Ultra 4 went on sale in September 2026, and the SE 3 remains in Apple’s lineup. If you need a watch now, choose the model that fits your needs and budget. If you are mainly looking for a lower price, consider waiting for a sale or comparing discounted Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock. 
Apple has not announced when the next Apple Watch models will arrive, but we expect that the next update will happen in September 2027.





2.
How long does Apple support an Apple Watch?
Apple has traditionally supported Apple Watches with major watchOS updates for around five to six years, but that changed with watchOS 27, announced at WWDC 2026.
Apple dropped support for five older models in a single release:
Apple Watch Series 6 (2020)
Apple Watch Series 7 (2021)
Apple Watch Series 8 (2022)
Apple Watch SE (2nd generation, 2022)
Apple Watch Ultra (1st generation, 2022)
As a result, watchOS 27 only supports Apple Watches with an S9 chip or later, starting with the Apple Watch Series 9. While Apple may continue to provide security updates for older models for a limited time, they no longer receive new watchOS features.
The change makes software support a much more important consideration when buying an older or refurbished Apple Watch. If you want the longest possible lifespan, choose a model with an S9 chip or newer.





3.
Is the Apple Watch Series 11 still worth buying?
If it is substantially cheaper than the Series 12. Both have up to 24 hours of rated everyday battery life, but the Series 12 adds more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements, a Readiness score and support for upcoming Audio Intelligence features, so be sure that you are willing to give those features up for the saving.

title: Jensen Huang Reinstated as Nvidia CEO
content:
Nvidia today announced that its board of directors has voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as President and CEO of the company effective immediately.


Huang had resigned on November 12, after it was reported that he had extramarital affairs.

Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him, after which the board was satisfied with respect to his "candor and ability to lead" the company. The board received input from "senior levels of the U.S. government" and is confident that Huang "poses no national security risk."

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," said Nvidia's chairman Harvey C. Jones. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company."

Speaking on a November 17 earnings call, Jones said Nvidia's board did not intend to reinstate Huang, so the company has reversed course.
